Furthermore, we regard prediction as an image-inpainting problem that recovers missing pixels from known pixel values, and we propose applying the U-Net to solve this problem. Numerical experiments show that the proposed method outperforms conventional methods in prediction accuracy and spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Identifying Nephrotoxicity of Small Molecules Using Machine Learning
abstract: Nephrotoxicity is a severe condition characterized by kidney damage resulting from exposure to harmful substances such as drugs, diagnostic agents, chemicals, or environmental toxins. The potential for nephrotoxicity in drug molecules remains significant, often leading to severe consequences for patients. Despite existing computational methods for identifying nephrotoxic molecules, these approaches fail to provide stable and reliable performance due to biased modeling (e.g., small sample sizes, imbalanced classes, and data leakage). In this study, we offer a refined dataset for nephrotoxicity prediction tasks. Our dataset was collected from existing studies, rebalanced, and carefully curated to improve the quality of data for Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship modeling. Additionally, we implemented a series of 32 prediction models using eight machine learning algorithms in combination with three types of molecular representations. The implementation of these machine learning models serves as a preliminary survey of how conventional methods perform on the refined dataset. Our findings indicated that all implemented models achieved satisfactory performance. Our dataset could serve as a valuable resource for developing more advanced prediction methods in the future.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Performance and Reliability of IoT Systems Using Predictive Route Recovery Mechanism
abstract: The rapid proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has brought numerous challenges related to the performance and reliability of these systems. Frequent link failures due to the dynamic nature of IoT environments, including device mobility and varying signal strengths, often disrupt communication. This paper presents a novel overhearing-based route recovery mechanism designed to predict potential link failures and maintain active routes by leveraging the overhearing capabilities of neighboring nodes. This proactive approach significantly reduces packet loss, enhances data transmission efficiency, and ensures robust network connectivity, thereby improving the overall performance and reliability of IoT systems. The proposed mechanism's efficacy is demonstrated through extensive simulations using the ns-3 network simulator.

articleTitle: Adaptive Step Length Estimation and GNSS Integration to Improve PDR Accuracy
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method to improve the accuracy of Pedestrian Dead Reckoning (PDR) by refining step length estimation and integrating GNSS data using Kalman filters. We developed an adaptive step length estimation model that dynamically adjusts based on real-time gait state detection. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances PDR accuracy across various gait patterns and environments, providing a more robust and reliable positioning solution for smartphone users.

articleTitle: Image Comparative Index (ICI): A Pixel-Wise Image Similarity Metric for Computational Super-Resolution (SR) Microscopy
abstract: We compare the outputs of several widely-utilized image quality metrics (such as the PSNR, SSIM, MS-SSIM, FSIMc & IMMSE) in the context of AI-mediated image super-resolution (SR) microscopy derived from a GAN. Although these metrics are often employed in the image analytics space for assaying image quality, the findings of our study indicate that such metrics may not be quite suitable for determining the quality of a GAN-generated image in the context of image SR microscopy, namely in the preservation of fine details and structures which are crucial aspects of high-resolution images (as determined visually). For instance, in some of the assayed images, we observed that these metrics returned a relatively favorable score, while on closer visual inspection, the generated image was observed to be prone to reconstruction artifacts, bearing little similarity to the Expected (ground truth) image. In this respect, we have sought to develop a custom image quality metric capable of assessing image similarity on a pixel-wise scale irrespective of the bit-depth of the image. Our proposed metric [termed the image comparative index (ICI)] has proven to be a viable determinant of similarity between 2 images, closely corroborating with a pixel-wise map of the differences between the assayed images, thereby allowing for more detailed analysis and identification of specific areas of improvement. We postulate that these results represent an important consideration for researchers seeking to utilize deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) for image SR (particularly when assessing the similarity between a DCNN-generated and the ground truth images during model training) with potential extrapolations of the proposed ICI metric in image classification & object detection use-cases as well.

articleTitle: Advantages and Challenges of FMCW Radar Imaging with Shifting Sub-Bands
abstract: High-resolution imaging is an ever-popular research topic in the radar community. However, achieving higher resolution generally necessitates larger bandwidths, posing significant engineering challenges. To overcome these challenges, synthesizing a large bandwidth using shifting sub-bands across different center frequencies has emerged as a promising technique. This study explores the advantages and challenges of frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar imaging with shifting sub-bands. Methods to compensate for phase errors have been investigated to synthesize baseband signal. The imaging performance has been evaluated through both simulations and outdoor experiments using universal software radio peripheral (USRP) X410.

articleTitle: V-Band Power Amplifier MMIC Cell Implemented in GaAs
abstract: A versatile compact power-amplifier cell for rapid development of V-band GaAs MMICs is reported. It was designed using a single-finger, non-linear model with an EM simulation of the interconnect. In a small active area of 1.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the cell offers 30.1 dB power gain over the 58–66 GHz band. The versatility for rapid development is demonstrated by assembling various amplifiers: two cells in parallel, a full-balanced amplifier with four cells, and a transceiver MMIC using a single-cell as the transmitter and a half-cell as the receiver. For these variants output power is 27.3, 29.3, 19.6 dBm at 1-dB gain compression, and 29.8, 29.9, 27.3 dBm in saturation respectively.

articleTitle: 2D Ultrasound to 3D CT Image Registration for Liver Ablation Surgery
abstract: Minimally invasive liver cancer treatments are increasingly favoured for their reduced risks and improved patient outcomes. However, real-time guidance during liver ablation remains challenging due to limited resources and the reliance on ultrasound (US) imaging. This project introduces a deep learning-based approach for 2D US to 3D Computed Tomography (CT) image registration, eliminating the need for 3D tracking systems. By integrating self-supervised feature embeddings and matching point estimation methods, our approach enhances real-time visualization of the liver, improving surgical precision and cost-effectiveness. With around 0.99 Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC) value and 25.48-pixel distance in US and CT image registration, this research promises significant advancements in liver tumor ablation procedures and holds potential for broader applications in other ablation therapies.

articleTitle: The Development of a Lithium-Ion Battery Analyzer for Data-Driven Analysis of Battery Performance
abstract: As demand for higher energy density, faster charging, and longer lifespan increases, so too does the need for sophisticated analysis of battery performance. This study focuses on the development of a lithium-ion battery analyzer for data-driven battery performance analysis. The system comprises a hardware platform and a cloud-connected software infrastructure. The hardware utilizes an STM32 microcontroller integrated with an LTC6803 for precise battery parameter measurements, including voltage, current, and temperature. The charging circuit is an LTC-4162, allowing for controlled charging profiles. A Raspberry Pi, running Raspbian OS, acts as the central processing unit, collecting data from the microcontroller and displaying it on a user-friendly human machine interface developed using Node-RED. Crucially, the system leverages cloud connectivity for data storage, analysis, and remote monitoring. The system transmits measured data to a cloud platform, which offers scalable storage and facilitates the development of sophisticated data analysis algorithms. This cloud integration allows for real-time battery performance monitoring and visualization through a dedicated application. Additionally, the system incorporates a local data backup mechanism, ensuring data accessibility even during internet disruptions. The developed system provides a comprehensive platform for data-driven insights into battery health, enabling informed decisions regarding battery operation and maintenance.

articleTitle: A Source-Drain Engineering Di-Electrically Modulated Double Gate TFET Based Label-Free Biosensor
abstract: The effect of drain doping and source material engineering of a dielectrically modulated double gate TFET (DMDGTFET) based label free biosensor has been analyzed in this article. The analysis of the biosensor has been done by introducing dielectric modulation in the cavity at the source side to sense the biomolecules. The trapped immobile biomolecules induce the drain current, hence the sensing of the biomolecules is based on the drain current of the device with respect to the different biomolecules. The drain current is higher for higher dielectric constant. Due to splitting of the drain region in three regions, one lower doping region sandwiched between two higher doping regions, it increases the tunnelling width and hence improves the ambipolar current. SILVACO ATLAS has been used for simulation purpose. Also, the proposed biosensor provides better performance without deteriorating the on current. The maximum sensitivity achieved is about 4.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> for k=10.

articleTitle: ECoSense: IoT-Driven Power Monitoring and Centralized Control System for Energy Conservation
abstract: The research study addresses the prevalent issue of high energy consumption at FAITH Colleges due to non-adherence to responsible practices, such as neglecting to turn off air conditioning units after use and unauthorized use of vacant rooms for leisure activities, resulting in significant energy wastage. To tackle this challenge, the study proposes the implementation of the ECoSense system, an Internet of Things (IoT)-driven power monitoring and centralized control system. The system utilizes a wireless sensor network to monitor energy consumption, which also includes real-time data collection, data analysis, data processing, automated control operation, database management, and data power visualization. Project implementation involved key components such as the PZEM -004T sensor, ESP8266, mini circuit breaker, MG996r Servo Motor, and Google Drive applications. Notably, ECoSense provides users with real-time data insights and automates air conditioning units' operational status based on user-defined schedules, significantly contributing to energy conservation efforts. The results demonstrate successful ECoSense implementation, highlighting its effectiveness in reducing energy consumption and cutting electricity costs.

Author Keywords: IoT-power monitoring and centralized control system

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Antenna Using Automated, Multi-Size Pixelated Design
abstract: This paper presents an in-house developed tool to optimize antenna designs with limited human involvement. While most work focused on the flexibility to interface with different optimization methods, this work enhances modelling experience, it provides complete modelling packages from separate shapes to combined shapes such as probe feeds with different pads and layers. Together with the flexible optimization flow and data collection function, the final goal to achieve automated antenna design becomes more feasible. The tool has been used to extend the bandwidth of a well-known UWB antenna. The measurement shows an increment of more than 10% has been successfully achieved with the same material and PCB size.

articleTitle: Gender Difference in Hearing Health in the United States: A Spatiotemporal Analysis
abstract: Hearing loss is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide, affecting people's quality of life adversely and causing substantial economic costs in the United States. Existing studies pointed out that men are more prone to hearing loss than women. To explore the gender difference in hearing health and the mechanism behind it, this study performs a spatiotemporal analysis of hearing health at the county level in the United States. The results show that 132 of 3,103 counties with effective data have a higher female hearing loss rate than males, with more than 60% of them in rural areas. We also find that counties with similar levels of hearing loss rate have a tendency to cluster spatially. In addition, the correlation analysis shows that counties with higher hearing loss rates have lower infrastructure density. This study is the first to analyze the infrastructure-related hearing health imbalance between sexes, with a particular focus on female hearing health issues. We believe that this pioneering study will help bridge the healthcare gap by addressing hearing health disparities. Targeted public health interventions and infrastructure development, especially in rural areas, are essential to mitigate the adverse effects of hearing loss and improve overall health equity. Future research should focus on identifying specific infrastructure elements that contribute to hearing health disparities and develop gender-specific strategies to mitigate hearing loss.

articleTitle: Effect of Gap Variation on DC Series Arcing Characteristics in PV Farms Using Fast Fourier Transform Method
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) systems constitute a crucial aspect of renewable energy generation, yet they can pose safety hazards due to current disturbances in the DC series system, particularly electric arc faults. These arc faults typically occur as a result of system irregularities such as loose connections or damaged cables. Arc faults are characterized by electrical discharges originating from potential differences between two conductors or electrodes. In this study, electric arc faults in the electrode gap were examined at three different distances: 0.05 mm, 0.1 mm, and 0.15 mm. The current and voltage signals from the electrical arc were acquired, and subsequently, the current signal was processed and analyzed for its characteristics using the Fast Fourier Transform method in MATLAB. The test results indicate that current spikes during arcing consistently occurred at higher levels than under normal conditions in the frequency domain. Within the frequency range of 0 Hz to 500 Hz, the characteristic frequencies of the series arcing were determined to be 100 Hz, 150 Hz, and 200 Hz.

articleTitle: Optimizing Deep Learning on Sustainable Embedded Systems: A Study of Handwritten Digit Recognition with CNN and OpenCV
abstract: This senior thesis develops a real-time handwritten digit identification system using a Raspberry Pi 3B+ with a camera module, leveraging a lightweight CNN optimized with MNIST. The project highlights the effective implementation of deep learning on edge computing devices through seamless integration of CNN, TensorFlow Lite, and OpenCV's real-time image processing. The system is both cost-effective and precise, enabling real-time digit recognition tasks. This proposed work illustrates the potential of AI applications in education, industry, and commerce, setting the stage for future advancements in embedded AI systems.

articleTitle: Pain Screening in Orthopedics Using Machine Learning
abstract: In this study, we focus on a diagnostic system for the field of orthopedic surgery that classifies patients' pain with high accuracy. The proposed system uses machine learning on questionnaire response data to determine pain and incorporates questionnaire items in addition to the traditional ones. Traditionally, the screening of neuropathic pain using existing methods has yielded diagnostic accuracy rates of 10 - 20%. However, our proposed approach achieves an 80% accuracy rate based on empirical data.

articleTitle: Forest Canopy Cover Mapping in High-Resolution Multisource Satellite Imagery Using Attention Recurrent Residual U-Net
abstract: This study presents a novel deep learning (DL) model for tropical forest canopy mapping using high-resolution multisource remote sensing (RS) data. The model integrates soft attention mechanisms and recurrent residual (R2) networks with a U-Net backbone to enhance feature focus and capture contextual information. Evaluated using the mean intersection over union (MIo U) metric, the proposed model achieved 0.9521 accuracy, surpassing the traditional U-Net (0.9266), U-Net with attention (0.9383), and Deeplabv3+ (0.9419) models. It also generated superior forest canopy change maps. These improvements enable better monitoring of tropical forests, which face increasing anthropogenic threats from deforestation, urban sprawl, agriculture, and climate change.

articleTitle: Lot Quality Prediction in Semiconductor Manufacturing Final Test Using Multilayer Perceptron
abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing relies on final test (FT) to ensure the quality of integrated circuits before shipment. To optimize manufacturing and reduce costs, this study develops an AI model that can shorten the FT cycle time. Benefits include early detection of problematic lots, more accurate forecasting, and more thorough root cause analysis. Using a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) to predict lot quality, all programming, training, and evaluation were coded using Python through Jupyter Notebook. Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's tests showed that increasing hidden layers from two to five did not significantly improve accuracy. Afterward, hyperparameter tuning identified the best model configuration, resulting in to-fold cross-validation with an average classification accuracy of 88.4622%, an F1-score of 88.4309%, and an ROC-AUC of 96.2478%.

articleTitle: Wi-Con: Wi-Fi Channel State Information for Sensing in Confined Environments
abstract: Wi-Fi has become a cost-effective sensing mechanism due to its widespread availability. Channel State Information (CSI) from the OFDM-based physical layer of Wi-Fi contains rich information for sensing static and dynamic channel conditions, and hence for sensing activities within the channel. Numerous applications which combine CSI-based sensing with machine learning (ML) available for both indoor and outdoor environments. We extend the use of CSI- based Wi-Fi sensing to a unique setting: a confined environment. An industrial beverage cooler is specifically considered. We address the challenges of sensing device placement in such confined environments, where line-of-sight obstruction and near-field effects play a key role in CSI stability. We compensate for these effects by introducing novel combinations of data preprocessing techniques and input feature definitions. We demonstrate an accuracy of 89% for dynamic conditions such as door movement and item removal in our experiments,

articleTitle: High Speed Low Power Dynamic CMOS Comparator for SAR ADCs
abstract: This work presents the design of a dynamic CMOS comparator for SAR ADCs. The proposed comparator implements three improvements, namely: (1) it introduced a shared charge technique on the output terminals to reduce the delay; (2) it employed control and switch transistors on the pre-amplifier stage to reduce power consumption and (3) it replaced the PMOS tail current with NMOS to eliminate the need of an inverted clock to reduce noise. A conventional double-tail dynamic comparator is simulated alongside the proposed comparator to assess the performance of the novelty of the proposed comparator. The use of the same aspect ratio and common test bench assured the unbiased results. Results show that with 1.2GHz clock frequency and 1.2V supply voltage, the proposed comparator consumed a total average power of 886.4uW with a delay of 18.3ps, a total noise output of 0.7mVrms and an input referred noise of 7.027uVrms. While that of the conventional comparator consumed a total average power of 997.1uW with a delay of 51.93ps, a total noise output of 27.8mVrms and an input referred noise of 278uVrms.

Author Keywords: total noise output and input referred noise

articleTitle: Highresolution Net for Estimation of Fetal Growth Parameters from First Trimester Ultrasound Images
abstract: Crown-rump length (CRL) from ultrasound is the the standards for estimating gestational age in the first trimester, however it must be measured manually. This work introduce Highresolution Net (HRNet), a deep learning model for fully automated fetus contour recognition and CRL measuring using ultrasound. The architecture integrates multi-scale contextual information as well as fine detail to ensure exact localization. Highresolution Net detects the fetus shape with 0.926 Dice similarity across 3205 images. The CRL measuring error is 0.67mm compared to experts. Derived gestational ages allow for delivery date prediction within 7 days in 96% of cases. Automated CRL quantification and pregnancy date in the first trimester may reduce interobserver variability and enhance workflow. A reliable measurement of early fetal growth will improve surveillance and anomaly prediction.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Wide Angle Beam Scanning Composite Right/Left-Handed Leaky- Wave Antenna
abstract: Although leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) have excel-lent radiation properties, many suffer radiation in the broadside direction. This limitation restricts the beam scanning of LWAs, particularly uniform LWAs, in the forward direction only. A composite right/left-handed (CRLH) LWA for millimeter wave application is discussed in this paper. The unit cell of the antenna consists of two patches with a gap between them, one with a slot in the middle and another shorted to the ground using four vias. The simulation results confirm that the radiating beam of the antenna scans continuously from -63° to +70° as frequency sweeps from 31.5 to 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Enhanced Battery Degradation-Aware Scheduling for Distribution Network with Electric Vehicle Load
abstract: Batteries play a key role in today's power grid. In this paper, we investigate the impact of battery degradation on the distribution network. We formulate a multi-objective framework for optimizing battery scheduling with the goals of minimizing monetary costs and improving network performance. Our frame-work incorporates energy purchase and battery degradation into the costs and measures the network performance through energy losses and voltage deviation. We propose Bach for battery degradation-aware scheduling based on s-constraint and fuzzy logic methods. Bach is implemented for the IEEE 33-bus network for an experimental study. The results show the effectiveness of Bach in optimizing costs and performance simultaneously with battery degradation awareness and demonstrate the flexibility of further customization.

articleTitle: Deadtime Compensation-Based Approximate Decoupling Control Approach for Multivariable Processes
abstract: The interaction effects among individual loops and multiple time delays are the prime reasons for degrading the closed-loop performance of multivariable systems. For highly interacting systems, decouplers are used to counteract interaction effects. However, decouplers may not be realizable and even if they are realizable, for high dimensional systems, decoupler elements may be complex. To improve the decoupler realizability, a dead-time compensation (DTC) approach is proposed in this work. The DTC framework can minimise the impact of dead-time on system dynamics. The proposed decoupler is designed based on the dynamic relative gain array (DRGA) to compensate for interaction effects. The DRGA reveals more insights about the coupling effect between a pair of input-output loops. The DRGA elements are used as decoupler elements for the multivariable process. The minimization of both interaction effects and dead-time dynamics can be achieved with the proposed DTC-based decoupling control approach. The simple IM C PI tuning rules are utilized to implement controllers for each loop. The simulation study affirming the proposed method provides better desired closed-loop performance, error indices for nominal and plant model mismatches, and robust stability against plant uncertainty over the popular existing decoupler based approaches.

articleTitle: Smart Solar Forecasting: Machine Learning Approaches for Predicting Solar Power
abstract: Solar energy is one of the most popular renewable energy sources in recent years. These solar systems not only reduce the need for electricity but also greatly improve the environment. Due to our excessive dependence on fossil fuels and their limited sources and the pollution caused by them, most people are turning to solar energy to power their homes and industries. It's critical to understand the location of the solar panel and the local weather since solar power efficiency is highly dependent on environmental factors. With the inherent unpredictability of photovoltaic power output, machine learning is a useful tool for predicting how weather conditions affect solar power plants, and there are various other viable prediction methods available. This research evaluates several meteorological characteristics for PV forecasting using numerous machine learning algorithms. Using the collected historical data set, a machine learning model is created. Necessary preprocessing techniques such as univariate and bivariate analysis are used. Machine learning algorithms benefit from data visualization as it makes it easier to understand features and create a robust classification model. Accuracy-related performance metrics such as MAE, MSE, and RMSE are used to compare the methods. We evaluate and contrast the various models' performances. This evaluation approach helps to choose the algorithm that best suits the task at hand.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Windshield Wiper Control Compensating Chatter Oscillation Characteristic Based on the Phase Difference Between Left and Right Arms
abstract: This paper proposes a windshield wiper control and its design method to reduce chatter oscillation of wiper arms. First, a windshield wiper model including the chatter oscillation characteristics is expressed. The model is described as a three-inertia resonance system. The parameters of the model are identified to realize the dynamics observed with the wiper test rig. A controller to compensate the chatter oscillation characteristic is designed based on H-infinity control theory. This control is implemented on the wiper test rig. Its performance is evaluated in comparison with the conventional control designed by an optimal regulator. The effectiveness of the control is demonstrated by the experimental results in the two kinds of conditions that chatter oscillation is likely and unlikely to occur.

articleTitle: Understanding the Effects of Naturalistic Music Listening in Brain Circuit Dynamics using Neural Manifold Learning in Patients with Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) causes severe memory and cognitive impairment, representing the most common and costly form of dementia without a cure. While current pharmacological treatments offer some symptom relief, they often fall short of desired clinical efficacy and may pose risks like radiation exposure and adverse side effects. Thus, non-pharmacological approaches like music therapy (MT) are gaining attention for their cost-effectiveness and accessibility, particularly in treating elderly patients. While numerous studies support MT's effectiveness in reducing AD symptoms, most focus on qualitative behavioral outcomes, highlighting the need for quantitative neurological measures. Electroencephalography (EEG) emerges as a valuable tool to track neural activity before, during, and after MT sessions, enabling the extraction of neurophysiological biomarkers. This study employs EEG datasets, one assessing the effects of different music genres on AD patients and another comparing healthy individuals with AD patients. Utilizing Neural Manifold Learning (NML) and Recurrence Quantification Analysis (RQA), the study explores changes in EEG data over time. Results reveal no significant difference in recurrence rates among music genres (p = 0.4164) but significant variation among AD severity classes (p = 0.00797). These findings underscore EEG's potential for quantifying MT's neurological impact in AD treatment.

articleTitle: Towards Achieving Singapore's Carbon Emission Reduction Goals by Means of Electricity Imports
abstract: This study presents a comparison of pathways to emission reduction in Singapore including its neighbouring countries. Given Singapore's limited renewable resources, electricity imports are one possible pathway to reduce the country's carbon footprint. This study quantitatively shows that restricting greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in Singapore alone leads to a higher dependence on electricity imports as compared to setting a GHG emission reduction goal for the whole Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) which allows for more local power generation from fossil fuels in Singapore. Our findings show that with regional collaboration and infrastructure investment for grid expansion, Singapore can leverage ASEAN's renewable energy resources to meet its targets, enhancing both regional energy security and economic integration. This study aims to provide strategic insights for policymakers on achieving a low-carbon future through regional energy cooperation.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Forecasting Performance with the Hybrid Machine Learning Techniques for Online Shopping Channels: A Case Study of Electronic Products in Thailand
abstract: This study proposes novel hybrid forecasting models, which are the combination between Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network and traditional models. The objective is to investigate the trend of customer behavior on electronic products and reduce the demand variation that will be impact the total cost in the supply chain. In order to prove the performance of our proposed hybrid models, a Thai company case study is tested with four online shopping electronic products. Accuracy and demand variation are used to compare the effectiveness of our hybrid forecasting model. For the accuracy, some performance indicator tools, such as MAE, RMSE, and MASE, show that the hybrid models provide the lowest error among these indicators with three products, while the single LSTM provide the lowest error with only one product. For the demand variation, all forecasted demand provide the coefficient variation (CV) score less than 0.25, which mean that all products are less variation, and can be used to calculate the forecast stock levels in the company.

articleTitle: Speaker Recognition Using Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: Accurately classifying age and gender using sound is beneficial for speaker and speech recognition as well as speech emotion classification. This is because separate acoustic models for men and women have been shown to perform better. Gender-based labelling is widely used in image-related applications such as video summary and robot-human interaction. Even still, gender classification is still in its infancy in voice processing and advanced in image processing. Accurate age classification helps determine how best to respond to a given user who fits into a certain group. This can assist customer service organizations and emergency hotlines in tailoring their answer to the individual requiring their help. After meticulous manual selection and using established methods, characteristics retrieved for classification are chosen using machine learning models. To categorize data into the appropriate age and gender classes, we have employed a variety of straightforward classifiers. Additionally, we used various convolutional neural networks with the power spectrum characteristics of the acquired voice samples.

articleTitle: Maximizing Output Power of a PV Array Under Non-uniform Solar Irradiation Conditions
abstract: Modules of PV array receive different level of solar irradiance under partial shading conditions causing lower power generation resulting in poor efficiency. An effective approach to improve this efficiency is to rearrange the physical location of the module in a manner so that uniform shading on all modules can be achieved. In this paper, a generalized physical relocation of modules with a fixed electrical connection in a TCT configuration is presented which is valid for square as well as rectangular PV array. The proposed configuration disperse the shadow effectively over the entire array. The performance of the proposed configuration in term of power generation and mismatch loss is compared with the other configurations under different shading patterns. From the simulation results, it is found that the power generated by the proposed configuration is higher and mismatch loss is less as compared to other configurations. Hence, the proposed configuration is more effective under any kind of shading conditions.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a 3D Printed Rainwater Energy Harvester for Household Application
abstract: The quest for alternative sustainable energy sources has led to innovative solutions, such as harnessing energy from rainwater. This study aims to evaluate the performance of a 3D printed pelton wheel turbine for a household rain gutter application with a height of 3m and 5m. The design and simulation were done via SolidWorks with varying number of buckets: 15, 18, and 20, evaluating the shaft power and rpm. Initial design parameters were calculated and simulated. The actual prototype and test were done. The results show an overall turbine efficiency of 71 percent and was able to produce an 8W power output. In this research, a 3D printed pelton turbine for a household application during rainy season was designed, simulated, fabricated, tested, and analyzed.

articleTitle: Implementing Agrivoltaics in Suburban Small Farms: A Solar Tree Prototype
abstract: This paper presents a solar tree prototype for implementing agrivoltaics in small suburban farms. Agrivoltaics integrates photovoltaic power generation and agricultural activities, minimizing competition between energy and food production. While technical aspects of agrivoltaics are well-studied, its implementation remains challenging, especially for small farms. The prototype uses IoT, 3D printing, and commercial components. Design principles, structure, solar-to-electricity conversion, and solar tracking mechanisms are discussed. Experiments had been conducted to enhance light-dependent resistor (LDR) accuracy for tracking, exploring shielding and tradeoffs.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Control of Integrated Drive and Chagre Mode Bi-Modular Power Converter for PV Assisted Light Electric Vehicle
abstract: This paper presents the topology and machine learning based power control of unified bi-modular inverter for drive and charge operations of PV assisted battery electric vehicle. A multilevel bi-modular inverter is considered for integrated simultaneous PV and battery power conversion which also configured for charging of battery from PV source with locked rotor acting as interfacing inductor. The proposed pattern recognition type ANN based machine learning control serves for power conversion control for multi-mode operation with maximum power point operation. The proposed system is implemented using MATLAB/SIMULINK. The performance of the proposed system is verified through simulation results for effectiveness of machine learning, accuracy of closed loop power conversion. A comparison on sizing of power converter is presented to verify the structural advantages of the proposed system.

articleTitle: A Study on Configuration Strategy of Inverter-Based Power System
abstract: Inverter-based resources (IBRs) are connected to the grid at an unprecedented rate owing to the transition towards renewable generations. However, conventional inverters, operating under grid-following (GFL) mode, do not provide grid regulatory services. To overcome this, some inverters are requested to operate in grid-forming (GFM) mode in replacement of synchronous generators (SGs). This paper aims to investigates the stability issues and placement strategy of inverter in such power systems. We first built a simulation model of a power system comprising two types of inverter control modes. Subsequently, the small-signal model of GFL inverters is derived. Utilizing the Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC) method, we evaluated the stability performance of different placement topologies and studied the placement strategy. Our findings indicate that an optimal ratio of 1:1 for GFM/GFL inverters and a specific placement strategy enhance system stability and response to disturbances. The study concludes with a guideline for the future design of inverter-based power systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Readout Speed of NP-H-CAM Using Clocked CMOS Inverters
abstract: An H-CAM (Content Addressable Memory with Hamming distance search function) is a specialized similarity search hardware. Previous papers proposed and studies NP-H-CAM (Non-Precharge-H-CAM) to reduce the power consumption. The power consumption issue of the NP-H-CAM was improved by adding a clocked CMOS inverters to each memory cell. But the NP-H-CAM using clocked CMOS inverters has an issue with the long readout time. In this paper, we insert our newly proposed the “SIS (CMOS Switch-Inverter-Switch) type” clocked CMOS inverters into the memory cells of the NP- H -CAM to enhance the readout speed by about 30% with increasing the power consumption by about 3%. We compare the readout speed of the proposed and conventional circuits using HSPICE simulation and show the advantages of the proposed NP-H-CAM in terms of the readout speed.

articleTitle: Enhancing Train Transportation in Sri Lanka: A Smart IOT Based Multi-Subsystem Approach Using MQTT
abstract: This research proposes a system as a solution for the challenges faced by Sri Lanka's historic railway system, such as scheduling delays, overcrowding, manual ticketing, and management inefficiencies. It proposes a multi-subsystem approach, incorporating GPS tracking, RFID-based e-ticketing, seat reservation, and vision-based people counting. The GPS-based real-time train tracking system performs accurately within 24 meters, with the MQTT protocol showing twice the speed of the HTTP-based system. All subsystems use the MQTT protocol to enhance efficiency, reliability, and passenger experience. The study's data and methodology demonstrate the effectiveness of these innovations in improving scheduling, passenger flow, and overall system performance, offering promising solutions for modernizing Sri Lanka's railway infrastructure.

articleTitle: A Scalable Decentralized Reinforcement Learning Framework for UAV Target Localization Using Recurrent PPO
abstract: The rapid advancements in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have unlocked numerous applications, including environmental monitoring, disaster response, and agricultural surveying. Enhancing the collective behavior of multiple decentralized UAVs can significantly improve these applications through more efficient and coordinated operations. In this study, we explore a Recurrent PPO model for target localization in perceptually degraded environments like places without GNSS/GPS signals. We first developed a single-drone approach for target identification, followed by a decentralized two-drone model. Our approach can utilize two types of sensors on the UAVs, a detection sensor and a target signal sensor. The single-drone model achieved an accuracy of 93%, while the two-drone model achieved an accuracy of 86%, with the latter requiring fewer average steps to locate the target. This demonstrates the potential of our method in UAV swarms, offering efficient and effective localization of radiant targets in complex environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Development of a 3kWh Battery-Supercapacitor Hybrid Energy Storage System
abstract: As the concern of climate change and environmental issues escalates, the demand for renewable and sustainable energy increases. The energy generation through wind turbines, Solar panel, and other methods of energy generation requires a reliable energy storage system to efficiently store the surplus energy for usage where energy generation would otherwise be unavailable. This paper introduces the development of a 3kWh Battery-super-capacitor Hybrid Energy Storage system, the outcome, and potential improvements for future development. It is built using lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) batteries with prismatic lithium-ion capacitors (LIC). Additionally, the built-in battery management system (BMS) allows data visualization and provides the necessary protection for the system.

articleTitle: Custom ANN: An Approach for Efficient Modulation Classification
abstract: Modulation is a fundamental technique for transmitting signals between a transmitter and receiver in wired and wireless scenarios. In a non-cooperative communication scenario, the receiver should be capable of classifying the modulation type efficiently. Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) is designed to monitor the radio-frequency spectrum and for making effective transmission decisions. Earlier AMC methods relied on feature extraction and likelihood-based approaches. However, with the rise of Deep Learning (DL), AMC has gained momentum due to its superior predictive capabilities. In this work, we propose a custom artificial neural network (ANN) for modulation classification. We analyze the impact of a deep learning model on AMC and how different modulation techniques influence its accuracy.

articleTitle: Image Question-Distractors Generation as a Conversational Model
abstract: This paper introduces an approach leveraging Visual Language Models (VLM) to automate the generation of educational assessment content for primary school students in Singapore. By integrating Image Captioning and Text Generation tasks, the proposed model generates multiple choice questions (MCQs) from cartoon images aimed at enhancing literacy and comprehension skills. Leveraging advancements in AI, particularly generative AI, the model reduces the workload of educators by automating question-answer generation, thus allowing more efficient use of classroom time. This approach not only improves interactive learning but also addresses the scalability of personalised education through technology. Initial results indicate that the model performs well in generating relevant and contextually appropriate questions. While the model performance is not as good as GPT-40, it can perform inference with significantly fewer resources and limited training examples. This indicates potential performance improvement when more training examples are used.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Framework for Monitoring Student Outcomes with Individualized Dashboard in Outcome-Based Education
abstract: Outcome-Based Education (OBE) emphasizes the importance of defining and assessing specific learning outcomes. Effective monitoring of these outcomes is crucial for ensuring student success and program effectiveness. Previous research has explored various approaches to enhance program outcome monitoring, however, have not fully addressed the need for individualized and comprehensive progress tracking that goes beyond binary pass or fail measurements. This paper presents a novel approach to enhance program outcome monitoring through the development of individualized dashboards and the application of an adaptive neuro-fuzzy logic (ANFIS) framework. Data were derived from CSV reports of students in a learning management system and Canvas New Analytics from a sample class in the pilot study. The ANFIS framework is based on formative and summative assessments, total and maximum page views and participation, and average weekly page views and participation. The ANFIS model and dashboard results demonstrate its effectiveness in providing students and educators with a deeper understanding of student progress in terms of program outcomes, enabling targeted interventions and personalized learning experiences. This comprehensive approach empowers educators with the tools and insights needed to optimize educational practices and ensure that all students achieve the desired learning outcomes.

articleTitle: N2N2N: A Clean Data Independent Speech Enhancement Approach with Modified cGAN
abstract: This work presents a novel approach for speech enhancement in scenarios where clean data is unavailable but noise type is known, using a modified Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) with a Residual Attention UNet (RAUNet) as the generator. The proposed Noise-to-Noisy-to-Noise (N2N2N) algorithm works on known noise types to iteratively refine speech signals, achieving high performance even in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions such as -15 dB. We demonstrate that our method surpasses existing solutions in terms of robustness, phase preservation, and computational efficiency. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of our approach, showcasing significant improvements in PESQ, STOI, CBAK, COVL and SSNR metrics across various noise environments.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Based Model Predictive Current Control for Improved Power Quality in Microgrid Clusters
abstract: Forming microgrid (MG) clusters in an enclosed area is an emerging solution to enrich the benefits of MGs. However, the integration of power electronic devices, renewable energy sources, and nonlinear electronic loads creates power quality issues in them. So, proper control of power converters became an important challenge in MGs. With this motivation, this paper proposes a new inverter control method named “fuzzy logic-based model predictive current control (FL-MPCC)”. This proposed method consists of two parts viz., (i) fuzzy logic-based synchronous reference frame theory (SRFT) for producing the reference currents and (ii) model predictive current control (MPCC) for producing the inverter switching pulses by using the reference currents produced by SRFT. The feedback mechanism employed in this proposed control method enables the MG to effectively handle disruptions and uncertainties. The test system for simulation studies is realized in MATLAB/Simulink 2022a software. The fruitfulness of the suggested method is analyzed over different power quality indices for example sag/swell, frequency response, and total harmonic distortion. From these comparative results, it is observed that the proposed FL-MPCC shows superior performance than the conventional MPCCs.

articleTitle: Assessment Mapping Strategies for Competency-Based Computing Education
abstract: There is an increasing trend in higher education on the emphasis on competency-based education (CBE). It is recognized that CBE can be highly effective in training industry-ready graduates. An important component of devel-oping CBE courses is the design and planning of appropriate competency-based assessments. While assessment methods have been well-studied in general, the practical aspects of planning how assessments map to competencies in a course and how to feasibly implement an assessment plan in real-time has been less studied. In this paper, we look at practical strategies to map and implement competency-based assessments in computing education by presenting examples applied to courses with topical or topic-agnostic competencies.

articleTitle: Systems Thinking in the Writing of Logbooks
abstract: Systems thinking helps students see the interrelationship between elements in a system. This study presents how systems thinking was introduced to undergraduate students in a logbook writing workshop over 3 lessons taught via zoom. The findings show that the students' logbook entries showed improvement in terms of mean scores, specifically in terms of content relevance and depth, critical analysis and integrating supporting ideas. Furthermore, the most frequently mentioned systems thinking habits were seeking to understand the bigger picture; considering short, long-term and unintended consequences of actions; and considering how mental models affect current reality and the future. It is noted that out of the 14 habits, 10 were mentioned. This might suggest that the systems thinking habits were helpful in adding value and meaning to the practice of logbook writing.

articleTitle: Image Encryption and Decryption Based on Reformed System Transformation
abstract: A recent study proposed an alternate approach of simultaneous input and state estimation (ASISE) for linear time-invariant continuous-time stochastic systems. This method utilizes a reformed system transformation technique to convert the original system into one that can reflect all online estimable unknown inputs in the measurement equation. This approach may reduce the computational complexity of the estimation pro-cess. This study further explores the extension of the ASISE for discrete-time stochastic systems and its application in designing an image encryption and decryption system.

articleTitle: Preparing Future Engineers: Strategies for Integrating AI Platforms in Higher Education
abstract: This paper investigates how AI-driven tools and platforms are integrated into engineering curricula to ready future engineers for the digital age. It emphasizes the advantages of improved learning experiences and tailored education, stressing the significance of updating curriculum content and training faculty. It also addresses challenges such as ethical concerns and integration complexities, highlighting the necessity for strategic planning to optimize AI's role in encouraging innovation and preparing students for careers in technology.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Automatic Classification of Carotenoid Associated Color Pigmentation
abstract: This study explores the application of deep learning models, specifically ResNet-34, ResN et-50, and EfficientNet-B0, for the automatic classification of carotenoid-associated color pigmentation in tomatoes. The dataset comprises 250 images categorized into five pigmentation levels, reflecting the varying carotenoid content. Carotenoids, such as lycopene and beta-carotene, are key pigments influencing the color of tomatoes, with deeper reds and oranges indicating higher concentrations. The models were evaluated for direct classification and regression followed by classification. Results show that EfficientNet-B0 achieved the highest accuracy in direct classification (94.00%), while ResNet-34 excelled in regression tasks (91.33%). Future research will continue exploring regression tasks to predict actual carotenoid content in tomatoes, enhancing prediction accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Optimum Design of Conformal Bandpass Frequency Selective Surface for X-Band RADAR Communications
abstract: This paper presents a novel X-band Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) employing an octagonal loop, rhombus and square loop resonator. The proposed dual-sided FSS serves as a spatial bandpass filter in the X-band spectrum (8 GHz – 12 GHz). The FSS reported in this paper is constructed on a conformal polyimide substrate and hence it offers flexibility in conforming to irregular surfaces while maintaining optimal performance. The design optimization is achieved through the innovative application of the Firefly algorithm, ensuring superior efficiency and selectivity within the desired frequency range. The utilization of octagonal loop and rhombus resonators contributes to the compactness (5.75×5.75 mm) and transmission efficiency (above 70%) of the FSS design, allowing robust functionality in diverse applications such as RADAR systems, communication devices, and sensing technologies. The bandwidth of operation of the FSS is controlled using the square loop resonator printed on the opposite side of the FSS. This abstract encapsulates the key features and potential applications of the proposed X-band FSS, presenting it as a promising solution for enhancing signal filtering and manipulation in X-band frequency ranges.

articleTitle: NOMA Pilot Based Channel Estimation for 6G CF–mMIMO Communication System
abstract: This paper delves into the intricacies of channel estimation within cell-free massive multiple input multiple output (CF-mMIMO) systems integrated with pilot signals of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), promising enhanced spectral efficiency and scalability to meet increasing user demands in the 6G cellular wireless communication system. In this work, maximum likelihood (ML) and linear minimum mean squared error (LMMSE) based channel estimation is adopted for proposed NOMA pilot based CF-mMIMO systems. Next, a closed-form expression for channel estimation mean square error (MSE) for both ML and LMMSE techniques for NOMA pilot based CF-mMIMO system is derived, which include power allocation techniques for pilot symbols. Next, a MATLAB-based thorough simulation analysis is performed and a MSE vs. signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) curve is obtained for both ML and LMMSE techniques. Finally, the result obtained is compared with the conventional orthogonal pilot symbol-based channel estimation for the CF-mMIMO system. The result comparison concludes that the NOMA pilot based channel estimation outperforms the conventional technique with little high computational complexity, however it further reduces the pilot contamination problem.

articleTitle: Person Re-identification System by Selecting Appropriate Trained Model
abstract: Person Re-identification (ReID) involves verifying whether an individual captured across multiple cameras is the same person. While numerous studies focus on ReID, many assume environments with overlapping fields of view or uniform lighting conditions. However, security cameras in public facilities are often sparse in number and scattered due to cost and privacy considerations. This sparse arrangement results in varying angles of view and environmental contexts for each camera, posing challenges for re-identifying individuals using specific features. Consequently, ReID using specific features becomes difficult in such scenarios. To address this, our study proposes a system that performs feature extraction and ReID by dynamically selecting the optimal model for human images captured by multiple sparsely distributed cameras. By selecting a model suited to the shooting environment, we aim to improve ReID accuracy compared to using a single feature, thus enhancing the reliability of person identification across diverse camera setups.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Variable Airgap Permanent Magnet Motor for Electric Drivetrain
abstract: This paper presents performance analysis of a variable flux permanent magnet motor. The proposed machine can flexibly control the air-gap flux by adjusting the separation distance between the rotor and stator, allowing for variation in electromagnetic coupling based on operating conditions. Simulation results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the self-adjusted variable air gap motor, which maximizes power transfer by controlling the electromagnetic coupling.

Author Keywords: variable air gap permanent magnet motor

articleTitle: A Novel Non-Invasive Cuff-Less Method for Continuous Blood Pressure Estimation Using Machine Learning and Photoplethysmography
abstract: Hypertension requires timely monitoring to prevent complications like strokes and heart failure. This study introduces a non-invasive, cuff-less method for continuous blood pressure (BP) estimation using machine learning (ML) and photoplethysmography (PPG) signals. Our approach reveals BP fluctuations by examining the correlation between arterial BP (ABP) and PPG signals. Validation with standard metrics shows that a 16-second segmentation technique and Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm achieve mean absolute errors (MAE) of 10.54 for systolic BP (SBP) and 5.28 for diastolic BP (DBP), with R-squared values of 0.59 and 0.34, respectively. This method offers a practical and superior alternative for BP monitoring in healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Optimal Dispatch for Large-Scale Renewable Energy Bases Without Conventional Power Support
abstract: In large-scale renewable energy base and HVDC systems, the absence of conventional power support makes commutation failures a significant threat to system security and stability. An optimal dispatch method based on Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) is proposed, which considers voltage and frequency dynamic security constraints. First, a time-domain simulation model of the system is developed to generate training data for KAN. The KAN is then designed to estimate the transient overvoltage at the point of common coupling in the renewable energy base after the occurrence of commutation failure. Frequency fluctuation is calculated by frequency nadir prediction model. Thirdly, an optimal dispatch model is formulated to maximize the delivered power of HVDC, which considers both operational and dynamic security constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed optimal dispatch model enhances system security with an acceptable reduction in delivered power.

articleTitle: Adaptive Traffic Signal Cycle Control for Green City Traffic Management
abstract: Traffic congestion at road intersections is one of the critical challenges for vehicular traffic systems. In the urban environment, this traffic congestion results in an increase in the travel time, more driver fatigue, higher pollution, etc. Consequently, traffic congestion not only exacerbates travel delays but also impacts the environment and human health. As a consequence, the implementation of adaptive traffic signal cycle control to alleviate traffic congestion is of paramount importance. In this work, we use Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) based traffic simulation to control traffic signal cycle for smart cities. We propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based adaptive traffic signal cycle control that aims to minimize carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) emissions while simultaneously decreasing the waiting time of the drivers. The results showcase that with the use of a DRL-based adaptive traffic signal control cycle, specifically, the average waiting time of the vehicles increases by 15.58% as the number of vehicles increases from 1750 to 2000. Furthermore, the average CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions of the vehicles increase by 25% as the number of vehicles increases from 1750 to 2000.

articleTitle: Automation System of Organic Hydroponics with Vermicompost as Nutrients Source Using Forward Chaining Method
abstract: This paper deals with the automated organic hydroponic system which uses vermicompost tea (VCT) as its main nutritional source and compares its performance with the traditional soil and conventional hydroponic methods to grow the lettuce variety of Lactuca sativa ‘Estrosa’. The system comprises pH, EC, temperature, humidity, and light intensity which are critical parameters for plant growth, using LED grow lights to optimize them. The result presents that the traditional farming method using soil yielded an average of 15. 78 leaves per plant, while the organic hydroponic system obtained 14 leaves, and the conventional hydroponic production was 13.89 leaves. The organic system, supported using LED lights, was only about 5% away from the traditional method's leaf area and 2% away from its leaf number. This signifies a successful attempt at achieving the desired growth. On the other hand, biomass production in the organic method was lower by 10% compared to the conventional system evidenced by the fresh and dry weight of 90% for the former. The shoot height in the organic system was 92% of that in soil-based traditional growing, showing both the effectiveness and the scope for improvement in the controlled conditions. Note that the VCT (vermicompost tea) concentration used in the organic hydroponic system was low compared to what is usually used in conventional hydroponics. Such lower concentrations could be responsible for the inhibition of growth or observational indicators like fresh weight and dry weight, thus, indicating an area for future experimentations.

Author Keywords: Vermitea or Vermicompost tea as Liquid Fertilizer

articleTitle: SENYAS: A Filipino Sign Language Recognition System Using MediaPipe and CNN-LSTM
abstract: Filipino Sign Language (FSL) is an important mode of communication for the deaf community in the Philippines yet the shortage of qualified interpreters creates barriers to effective communication. Thus, in this work, we developed a web application using computer vision and deep learning to recognize Filipino Sign Language (FSL) in real-time. The application extracts key features from hand gestures using Mediapipe and utilizes a CNN-LSTM model, combining strengths of convolutional neural networks and long short-term memory networks, to achieve high accuracy in recognizing both static and dynamic FSL signs. We performed a comparative analysis between five distinct CNN-LSTM models, evaluating them based on their performance on prediction speed, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The best performing model was CNN-MP-LSTM which achieved 98% accuracy during training, and 86% accuracy in real-world testing. Ultimately, this application has the potential to significantly improve communication accessibility for the deaf community in the Philippines.

articleTitle: State Estimation of Jagged-Shape Chaotic Oscillator Using Noisy Sensor Measurements
abstract: This ongoing work introduces a novel chaotic oscillator, termed the Jagged-shape oscillator, into the filtering domain. We have formulated the dynamics of the Jagged-shape oscillator and integrated it with a noisy measurement model, capturing the complex behavior of various real-time systems. To estimate the unmeasured internal states of this chaotic system, we employ the third-degree spherical-cubature rule-based Kalman filter (CKF). The CKF has demonstrated efficiency in tracking the states of the chaotic oscillatory system. The accuracy of the state estimation is validated through different scenarios that consider low to increased noise levels.

articleTitle: High PSR Low Power Negative-R-Assisted LDO
abstract: A Low-Dropout Regulator with adaptive low power mode and negative-R assisted technique is proposed in this paper. Two designs namely, adaptive low power mode to dynamically adjust power consumption under different load conditions and, negative-R assisted technique to improve the stability and transient response, have been simulated on Cadence virtuoso using 45nm technology. For both designs, an output voltage of 1V has been achieved for an input voltage of 1.2V. Furthermore, study has been done on both the LDOs transient response for varying loads. Also line regulation, load regulation, PSR and stability analysis have been carried out for both the designs. The PSR is found to be 50% better than the existing work and both the circuits are found to have good load and line regulation.

articleTitle: Translation of Air-Written Baybayin Using Optical Flow in Complex Background
abstract: Motion tracking plays a vital role in computer vision, yet its use in real-time script translation, particularly in complex environments, remains underexplored. This study compares the effectiveness of two optical flow methods—Lucas-Kanade and Farneback—for real-time translation of air-written Baybayin characters in challenging backgrounds. The system utilizes Color Thresholding for background subtraction, optical flow for motion tracking, and a combination of Tesseract OCR with a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model for character translation. Results show that the Lucas-Kanade method achieved a significantly higher accuracy of 82%, outperforming Farneback's 44%, which struggled with delayed tracking and incomplete character formation due to its higher computational demands. Lucas-Kanade's smoother and more reliable motion tracking allowed for more accurate character recognition, even in environments with complex backgrounds and variable lighting conditions. These findings demonstrate that Lucas-Kanade is the more effective optical flow method for real-time Baybayin translation, making it a promising approach for future applications in script recognition and translation tasks in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Classical to Quantum Neural Network Transfer Learning Approach for Speech Emotion Recognition
abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) has gained utmost attention among researchers for its vital role in Human-Computer Interaction, enabling systems to understand and respond to the emotional states of the users. In this work, the concept of transfer learning has been extended to the novel domain of hybrid classical-quantum neural networks for enhancing SER performance. The classical part involves preprocessing raw speech signals to generate three-channel log mel-spectrograms and the pretrained VGG 19 network for extracting useful emotional features. The quantum part is built upon a dressed quantum neural network (QNN), comprising multiple parallel QNN blocks, for accurate emotion classification. Extensive experiments on the publicly accessible TESS dataset reveal that the proposed hybrid transfer learning approach achieves state of the art accuracy of 98.93 %. An ablation study demonstrates the significant performance improvement attributed to the incorporation of QNN blocks. The integration of classical and quantum neural networks provides a robust and efficient solution, leveraging the strengths of both computational paradigms to enhance SER based applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Accuracy and Stability in Standing Wave Acoustic Levitation Systems
abstract: Acoustic levitation, an emerging technology that employs sound waves to suspend solid particles and liquid droplets in mid-air, holds immense promise. Its potential applications span diverse fields, including environmental science, mechanical engineering, biochemistry, food science, and cancer therapy. The method involves manipulating matter using sound waves to create novel forms of energy and material. However, standing wave acoustic levitation faces challenges, particularly unstable soundwaves that hinder stationary levitation. This study delves into the intricacies of the standing wave acoustic levitation system. Additionally, it compares this method with near-field and parametric array levitation techniques. Each approach utilizes sound waves to create “invisible fingers” that hold objects, but they have distinct advantages and limitations. To address instability, two standing wave acoustic levitation systems are constructed and tested: a simpler version and an expert-level setup. The goal is to enhance accuracy and stability. Ultimately, this research aims to unlock the full potential of acoustic levitation.

articleTitle: Effect of Check Meter Quantity on Theft Detection in Distribution Networks with Rooftop PV and Net Metering
abstract: The increasing demand for renewable energy has led to the rise of rooftop photovoltaics (PV) and net metering (NM). However, these complicate energy theft detection, necessitating a more complex approach. This paper explored the effect of varying the number of check meters (CM) in distribution networks with rooftop PV and NM on theft detection algorithms, specifically for detecting meter tampering in households. Using the Ausgrid Dataset and IEEE European Low Voltage Test Feeder in OpenDSS and Python, power flow simulations were conducted with varying levels of PV and NM penetration, and the number of houses connected per CM. Features extracted from the simulated data include Gamma Deviance (GD), Log Cosh Loss (LCL), Percent Loss Error (PLE), and Poisson Deviance (PD). These were used as input to three machine learning algorithms: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), and Decision Tree (DT); their test accuracies were used to asses their performances. Kendall's Tau correlation test assessed the correlation between the theft detection accuracy and CM quantity. LCL and PD exhibited a moderate to high correlation between theft detection accuracy and CM quantity at a 99% confidence level, and are more robust to varying levels of PV and NM penetration for all algorithms. This provides insights into the development and implementation of theft detection systems, reducing electricity theft risk and promoting sustainable energy transition.

articleTitle: Symbiotic Insights Prediction on a Multi-Cooperative Modular Mobile Robot using Machine Learning
abstract: This paper presents the use of machine learning in predicting the symbiotic insights such as coefficient and carrying capacity of a given modular mobile robot configuration doing a cooperative load pushing task. The independent parameters were load and the number of modules. The actual experiment results from a DFRobot Maqueen mobile robot pushing a range of loads were used as dataset in the study. Various regression models were run as an ML algorithm to assess symbiotic relationship of a given configuration whether harmful, beneficial or has no effect and to yield the total distance that can be traversed given a set of input parameters. The researchers used python in running the ML model on Google Colab Notebook. Results show that Gradient Boosting performed best in the prediction of distance carrying capacity with 95.87% and Extra Trees for symbiotic coefficient with 93.75% accuracy which took about only 5 seconds training time on a T4 GPU device. The researchers were able to develop a custom trained ML regressor model that can immediately return a symbiotic insight on a cooperative pushing modular mobile robots.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithm for Handwritten Numerical Character Identification Using FPGA Based Custom IP Core
abstract: Many recent advances in computer vision are based on the fundamentals of image classification techniques. These schemes have already been proved advantageous to the commer-cial, industrial, healthcare, and defense industries. Every pixel in image undergoes numerous mathematical operations during the classification processes. Sequential execution of these operations leads to a slower throughput. Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) have been used to develop hardware accelerators for parallel image processing that shorten pixel processing time. The classification of handwritten letters is an important step in optical character recognition (OCR). The open source Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology's (MNIST) handwritten numerical digits dataset is frequently used to train handwritten character classification models. The goal of this work is to create a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) based custom intellectual property (IP) core on the PYNQ-Z2 platform that can classify handwritten numerical characters with 97.48 % blind test accuracy.

articleTitle: A Shared Aperture Hybrid DR Antenna for Dual-Band mmWave 5G Applications
abstract: A novel hybrid dielectric resonator antenna (DR) antenna design is proposed for dual-band 5th generation (5G) millimeter-wave (mmWave) applications. This antenna integrates strip, slot, and innovative dielectric resonators to operate effectively across two distinct frequency bands. The lower band (LB), spanning 27.2 GHz to 32.2 GHz, leverages strip and slot resonances, while the upper band (UB) from 36.7GHz to 40.0 GHz is achieved through a uniquely shaped DRA with a stub. This innovative hybrid DRA shows significant potential for enhancing mmWave wireless communications, supporting frequencies at both 28 GHz and 38 GHz bands.

articleTitle: A Study of Generating Exhaustive Cycles in Wireless Mesh Networks for Disaster Notification
abstract: Japan is prone to earthquakes, causing disasters like a fire and collapse of buildings. Existing disaster notification systems depend on wired communication networks, which have risks of damage and disconnection of cables. Hence, we consider a wireless mesh network inside a building connecting a control room and disaster prevention equipment, such as smoke detec-tors. Notification from a device to the control room should be fault-tolerant and have low latency. To obtain paths satisfying such requirements, we propose a method to detect cycles on the wireless mesh network exhaustively. A small cycle through the source and destination of notification consists of two non-overlapped short paths, so notification with redundancy and low latency is available. Through simulation experiments, we clarify the overhead of detecting cycles according to the network scale and topology.

articleTitle: Sliding Window Gradient Sign Attack
abstract: An adversarial attack is an intentional attempt to fool or affect a machine learning model by giving deliberately generated input data, often known as adversarial examples. An adversarial attack exploits flaws in the model's decision-making process, resulting in inaccurate or unexpected results. Attacks on deep learning models, especially in computer vision, threaten their reliability. This work introduces a novel adversarial attack technique. This attack effectively targets vulnerable areas by producing imperceptible perturbations localised to particular sections of an input image by utilising the gradient sign idea. The approach drastically lowers the accuracy of deep learning algorithms by applying gradient-based perturbations throughout the image using the sliding window technique. Extensive experiments on state-of-the-art deep learning architecture were conducted to assess the feasibility of the suggested attack. We identified the specific weak points in the input photos by varying several parameters to control the degree of disturbances. The findings indicate that the nose and eyes are among those parts of the face most susceptible to hostile attacks.

articleTitle: ProfileOTMM: Automated Glycan Motif Analysis Through Pattern Recognition of Tree Structures
abstract: In recent times, tree-structured data has been rapidly spreading with the advent of the World Wide Web and Bioinformatics. It is employed as a common format for the storage and depiction of data. Glycans, essential substances in all organisms, are biomolecules that play diverse functional roles in the body. They are commonly modeled as tree-structured data and analyzed using machine learning techniques. Nevertheless, more detailed information is imperative to comprehensively understand the biological attributes and functionalities of gly-cans. In this research, we aim to propose a new model called profileOTMM (profile Ordered Tree Markov Model) for the complete automation of glycan analysis. As an initial step, feature engineering was conducted using the OTMM model, which serves as the foundational model for profileOTMM. By improving the accuracy of glycan data input through OTMM, we integrated monosaccharides, the elemental constituents of glycans, along with their linkage types into tree-structured glycan data. This enhanced approach enabled the extraction of biologically meaningful structures with a high degree of precision and accuracy, surpassing the results of previous research efforts. This research will encourage the understanding of glycan structures and their functions.

articleTitle: Innovative Sustainable Solutions for Continuous Power Supply in Wearable Technology Through Energy Harvesting
abstract: Wearable devices can enhance quality of life by allowing patients to live independently while monitoring vital signs remotely. The reliance on batteries, however, is a limitation, as devices stop working once the battery is depleted. Energy harvesting from human and environmental sources presents a solution, providing continuous power for wearables and portable devices. This project focuses on low-voltage energy harvesting methods like photovoltaic cells, thermoelectric generators, piezoelectric materials, and magnetic induction to power IoT systems, with stored energy in batteries.

articleTitle: Investigation of Bending Performance of Flexible Optoelectronic Synapse Based on ZnO
abstract: We report an optoelectronic artificial synapse based on ZnO fabricated on a flexible substrate. The essential synaptic properties including excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC), duration-time-dependent plasticity (DTDP), short-term memory (STM), long-term memory (LTM) and paired pulse facilitation (PPF) behaviours were simulated in flat state as well as in bent state. The device offers a PPF index of around 140% in both cases. This work highlights the impact of bending on the synaptic properties. Experimental results prove that the device is robust to bending giving comparable performance. This makes the device suitable for applications like wearable electronic devices, prosthetic devices and medical devices, etc.

articleTitle: Mental Health Evaluation Through Text Analysis
abstract: Assessment of a person's mental health is a complex phenomenon that affects many people around the world. This study aims to develop an accurate and efficient method to identify possible mental health concerns through text analysis, such as written messages and social media posts. This paper uses the capabilities of Amazon SageMaker Autopilot and KNIME to deliver improved model performance. This approach yields an improvement in accuracy compared to baseline models, demonstrating the potential to take advantage of cloud-based machine learning platforms and data science tools to streamline workflows. The results of the experiment demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Specifically, XGBoost achieved the highest accuracy of 93.6%, outperforminag Linear Learner and Multilayer Perceptron.

articleTitle: Prototype Development of a Multilevel Solar Dryer for Agriculture
abstract: Basic food processing in the Philippine agricultural sector relies on drying, which makes food products less perishable. A common practice is traditional sun-drying, which is simple, but exposes the produce to contaminants.
