Results indicate that the wrist is the optimal measurement site for various physiological parameters. Post-processing techniques were deliberately chosen to enhance the system's overall performance. The focus on HR necessitated evaluating two algorithms, given its critical importance. For SpO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and RR, single algorithms were selected to streamline processing while ensuring reliable measurements. The developed system exhibits acceptable power consumption of 51.98 m W and achieves an average coverage of 80% in controlled tests, indicating a significant portion of monitoring time provides accurate physiological data. This study emphasizes the deliberate selection of algorithms and measurement sites, demonstrating the superiority of the Z-Score algorithm and the practicality of integrating HR, SpO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, RR, and PPG monitoring in a single system.

articleTitle: Three-Terminal GaN-Based p-n Diode: From Device to Integrated Photonic Applications
abstract: We present a three-terminal gallium nitride (GaN)-based p-n diode capable of functioning as both a light emitter and detector. The device integrates a traditional p-n diode with a third terminal (Tt) composed of metal/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> layers on the p-GaN layer. In emitter mode, the applied bias on the Tt modulates the energy band of the p-GaN layer, increasing bandwidth from 160 MHz to 263 MHz. As a detector, the TTD enables the configuration of optoelectronic logic gates (OELGs) such as NAND and NOR by adjusting the bias voltage at the p- and n-electrodes. This multifunctional design enhances performance and flexibility in optoelectronic applications.

articleTitle: Continual Learning Enabled Smart Industrial Edge Computing Platforms
abstract: Industries increasingly depend on deep learning-based predictive quality systems to anticipate product quality using process data. However, the dynamic nature of production processes poses a significant challenge. These changes can render previously trained models ineffective, and thus, Memory Aware Synapses (MAS)-based continual learning approach for edge-enabled industries is adopted. This work extends MAS with knowledge transfer and a time-efficient MAS hyperparameter selection mechanism using a hybrid grid search and Particle Swarm Optimization mechanism. The experimental analysis demonstrates that the proposed mechanism reduces the overall model loss by 39.03% and 27.18% compared to MAS mechanisms, respectively, for two real-world use cases. An Android-based mobile application is designed as a ready-to-use solution for the mobile edge device.

articleTitle: An Electronic Agricultural Soil Quality Assessment Device
abstract: Agriculture in the Philippines is one big sector that plays an important role in the Philippine economy. The growth of the economy in the agricultural sector partly depends on crops yield. To have a good crops yield, soil quality will have to be good enough to nourish the crops for good harvest yield. Laboratory method of soil quality analysis methods can take weeks to months to produce the nutrient content of the soil. In this paper, the proponents propose the use of a hybrid electronic nose and sensors to identify the ammonia, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, pH and moisture content that affect the quality of soil for planting the best produce, in a shorter amount of time. The prototype will consist of a micro controller that will interface a MQ137 sensor that will detect without delay, the volatile organic compound (VOC's) present in the soil, along with a soil moisture sensor probe and Nitrogen, Phosphorous and Potassium (NPK) sensor that will determine the moisture, NPK and pH content of the soil. The sensed parameters are to then be displayed in a human machine interface (HMI) with a graphical user interface (GUI) firmware interfaced with the micro controller. This will allow farmers and agricultural technicians to determine the needed fertilizer mix for agricultural-grade soil, consequently, can lead to more produce. The prototype was compared to a chemical method of soil testing i.e. Rapid Soil Test Kit of the Department of Agriculture's Bureau of Soils and Water Management. The prototype was concluded to be a viable replacement for chemical soil quality tests.

articleTitle: EchoEyes: Shopping Items Identification Assistant for People with Vision Impairment
abstract: Vision impairment is a global issue and a daily struggle for those affected. Activities requiring access to information, particularly shopping, are a major hindrance for people with vision impairment. This study aimed to bridge the accessibility gap for people with vision impairment or PVI by developing assistive technology to aid them in shopping. The developed device used the Raspberry Pi with the YOLOv8 object detection model in eyeglasses form factor to detect shopping items using a custom dataset with Philippine shopping items and output the detected item description as audio feedback.

articleTitle: A Hue Preserving Image Enhancement Based on Multiple Parametric Sigmoid Functions in Each RGB Component
abstract: In this study, a new image enhancement method for digital color images is proposed. The proposed method realizes the lightness contrast enhancement and the image sharpening simultaneously and effectively while preserving hue of an input image. In the proposed method, concretely, the method based on the multiple parametric sigmoid functions is applied to each of R, G, and B components of the input image, and its outputs are fused by the geometrical processing so that the hue of the resultant image is the same as that of the input image. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the experiments using various digital color images.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Security of Encrypted Communication Systems Through Redundancy Design
abstract: The vulnerability of cryptographic keys to exposure represents a critical risk to modern cryptographic techniques. In this paper, we present an approach to enhancing the security of encrypted communication systems through the strategic incorporation of redundancy design. As hardware costs continue to decline, deploying such redundancy becomes increasingly feasible. This approach allows for the protection of individual keys through the amalgamation of multiple redundant keys, significantly lowering the probability of security breaches. The study's findings demonstrate that the proposed scheme not only enhances the resilience of encrypted communication systems against potential eavesdropping and key exposure but also provides a scalable solution for improving overall cryptographic security.

articleTitle: Speech Signal Analysis Using Fractal Geometry for Phoneme Boundary Detection
abstract: Phoneme segmentation deals with identifying the boundary points between two different phonetic units. It plays a vital role in automatic phoneme segmentation and annotating speech data. Deep learning methods require a huge amount of data for training which is not a favourable situation for low-resource languages and low-cost devices. Therefore, algorithms that require less data are desirable in both situations. In this paper, we propose a fractal-based method for phoneme segmentation that works by understanding the structural properties of a speech signal.

articleTitle: Scalable RFID-Based Automated Attendance Recording and Reporting System
abstract: Manual attendance tracking in schools is inefficient and error-prone. This project developed an RFID-based attendance system to address these issues. The system uses a WiFi-enabled microcontroller, RFID scanner, MySQL database, and Python scripts to automatically record and manage attendance data. A pilot implementation across six classes demonstrated the system's superiority over manual methods in terms of speed, efficiency, and reliability, with both students and lecturers expressing strong preference for the RFID system. The system presents potential for wider adoption in educational institutions.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Fault Detection Scheme for AC Microgrid: Based on Multilayer Perceptron
abstract: In the evolving landscape of renewable energy systems, ensuring the reliability and efficiency of AC microgrids is paramount. This paper presents an intelligent fault detection scheme for AC microgrids, leveraging Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) for signal decomposition and feature extraction, coupled with a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) for fault detection and classification. EMD effectively decomposes complex electrical signals into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), facilitating the extraction of significant fault-related features. These features are then fed into an MLP, a type of artificial neural network, which is trained to detect and classify faults with high accuracy. The proposed scheme demonstrates superior performance in identifying various fault types, ensuring robust protection and operational stability for AC microgrids.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning-Based State of Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Battery at Varying Temperatures
abstract: Accurate estimation of the Lithium-ion batteries (LiBs) state of health (SOH) is essential to ensure the safe and reliable operation of battery-powered devices. Most of the current data-driven SOH estimation models are designed under fixed ambient temperatures, overlooking the high sensitivity of LiBs to changing ambient temperatures. To bridge this gap, a novel method is proposed with transfer learning (TL) to model and estimate the SOH at varying ambient temperatures. First, canonical variate analysis is employed to capture the temporal dynamics in the time-series data of LiBs and extract temporal features. Second, at the reference temperature, an interpretable SOH estimation model with a long short-term memory network is utilized to learn the regression relationship between the temporal features and the labeled capacities. Third, at the new temperature, a small amount of data is projected into the key feature domain at the reference temperature to obtain the common temporal features. Afterward, TL is employed to take advantage of the existing process knowledge through keeping all functional layers of the previous well-trained SOH estimation model. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed method is verified on the NASA dataset with two discrete temperatures, 24°C and 44°C. Evaluated by the index of root mean squared error, the proposed method is capable of improving prediction accuracy by 94.18% when the model is transferred from 44°C to 24°C.

articleTitle: Wi-Fi Based Human Activity Recognition Using BiLSTM with Kernel Ridge Regression
abstract: In this paper, we propose a fusion network for human activity recognition based on the Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) signals. The system employs a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) layer to extract action features from CSI data blocks and then trains them using the Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR). The trained block responses are subsequently fused based on the sum-rule to form the final decision. In contrast to deep learning, this process is computationally efficient because there is no need to train the BiLSTM. The proposed method has been tested on two publicly available databases to validate the accuracy performance.

articleTitle: A Cebuano Parts-of-Speech(POS) Tagger Using Hidden Markov Model(HMM) Applied to News Text Genre
abstract: Part of speech tagging (POS) is crucial in natural language processing, identifying the grammatical categories of words in sentences. This research highlights the lack of focus on POS tagging for Asian languages, particularly Cebuano. Limited research on Cebuano has hindered linguistic documentation and understanding of its grammar and vocabulary. This study introduces a Cebuano POS tagger using the Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to improve Cebuano text processing. The researchers also propose a method for handling unfamiliar words. Results show the algorithm performs well on a news text corpus of 25,000 datasets, with an accuracy of 84 %, precision of 80%, recall of 81.52%, and F1-score of 82%. These outcomes demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness in addressing language challenges in specific genres. Additionally, the research contributes to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by promoting linguistic diversity and fostering inclusive language technologies. The study provides insights into Cebuano's linguistic traits and grammatical structures, offering a foundation for further research in natural language processing.

articleTitle: Refined Trademark Sticker Detection Method Using Minimum Pooling Features *
abstract: Trademark sticker detection stands as a crucial visual task within industrial quality inspection scenarios, de-manding precise determination of the accurate positioning of adhered trademarks on products. Despite the remarkable suc-cess achieved by current deep learning networks, their training requirements often involve extensive datasets, posing significant challenges for direct application in trademark sticker detection systems. A major obstacle lies in the vast variety of trademarks encountered in real-world industrial settings, coupled with the rapid speed of trademark updates and iterations. This renders it impractical to gather samples of every trademark type for training purposes. Furthermore, the process of collecting and annotating industrial data samples can be both time-consuming and costly. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces a novel approach that utilizes image subtraction to analyze the differences between the image with adhered trademarks and the image without adhered trademarks. This approach circumvents the need for vast sample sizes and extensive data annotations. By integrating minimum pooling techniques into the analysis of these difference images, this paper introduces an efficient approach that effectively filters out noise and alleviates the generalization challenges arising from frequent trademark replacements. Experimental findings underscore the robust flexibility of our method in precisely and adaptively detecting and recognizing packaging box labels. Consequently, this approach significantly enhances the quality of product packaging and trademark sticker detection, offering a viable solution for addressing the challenges posed by the diverse and rapidly evolving nature of industrial trademarks.

articleTitle: PUP UniChain: A Blockchain-Based University Events Access Management System for Polytechnic University of the Philippines
abstract: University events are essential avenues for faculties and students to promote community building and engagement, social interactions, skills development and the overall enhancement of learning for the welfare of the whole university. However, the majority of the universities do not implement a secure yet transparent and organized access system for such activities, leading to denied access for the learners, undesirable user experiences, and the general mismanagement of events. With this, the proponents' aim is to develop a blockchain-powered ticketing and access system to facilitate university events for PUP. A smart contract implementing ERC-721 was developed to mint Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) to reserve slots/seats for certain events, while a user interface was built to select the listed events on a website. The researchers made various tests for smart contracts and mock transactions to evaluate the functionality of the proposed system. In conclusion, PUP UniChain offers potential solutions to handle event access and management for PUP.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Oversampling Techniques and Deep Learning for Imbalanced Tabular Data
abstract: Imbalanced datasets pose a significant challenge in machine learning, where some classes are heavily underrepresented, affecting model performance and robustness. This paper offers a comprehensive comparative study of traditional data balancing techniques and explores the potential of deep learning-based tabular data synthesis algorithms. Focusing on Generative Adversarial Networks, Variational Autoencoders, Transformer-based models, and Diffusion models, we evaluated the practical applicability of these methods to the generation of high-quality synthetic data and the improvement of model performance on imbalanced datasets. This study highlights both the potential and limitations of deep generative models, suggesting the need for further research into integrating deep learning with traditional balancing methods.

articleTitle: Novel Estimation Problems in Non-Gaussian Noise Models: Maximum Likelihood Approach
abstract: Scalar estimation in the presence of noise is a basic problem in the estimation theory, an important branch of statistical signal processing. Estimation in Gaussian noise is well-studied and important in communication theory. However, one can find gaps in maximum likelihood (ML) estimation problems in non-Gaussian noise (NGN). NGN, such as exponential noise and Gamma noise, exist in laser imaging systems. In this short work, I consider novel ML estimation problems in exponential noise and Gamma noise, which are non-trivial and interesting. I present an analysis of the ML estimates and obtain interesting insights. It includes analytical expressions for insightful lower bounds on the variance of the estimated parameter for both the noise models. For a finite number of observations, I present numerical examples and determine the estimated value of the scalar. The problems and analysis I present are useful in applications such as optical imaging, where NGN is present.

articleTitle: Knowledge-Based Extraction for Inverse Design of Optical Thin-Films
abstract: In this paper, we've developed an inverse design framework for optical thin-films assisted by Generative Pre-trained Transformers (GPT). As a Large Language Models (LLMs)-powered tool, this creates an integrated platform for users to perform various functions related to inverse design on thin-films using an accessible and unique natural language interface via the assistant tool. With the consultant tool, users can query important design information and receive relevant answers to enhance the design knowledge of optical thin-films. This platform proves capable of speeding up design of thin-film structures compared to traditional ways and can also save many hours for repeated knowledge querying. The developed platform significantly reduces the resources and time (~3 x) for designers in developing optical thin-films to reach an optimal design. This will allow the thin-films' applications to be brought to the market faster and with increased efficiency.

articleTitle: Biomechanical Analysis of Foot Landing: A Machine Learning Approach Using Wearable Sensor System
abstract: Foot landing is crucial in daily activities and sports, providing balance, stability, and energy efficiency while reducing injury risk. Proper landing distributes impact forces evenly, preventing overuse injuries. In racquet-based sports like badminton, proper foot landing and racquet handling are believed to be key factors that affect players' performance. During athletic activities or training, players can make mistakes or movements that are potentially harmful if not addressed. Therefore, performance analysis is crucial in these situations. While numerous studies have examined the biomechanical characteristics of the upper limb, including various stroke and posture analyses at different levels of gameplay, research on the lower limb has been relatively scarce in racquet-based sports. The main objective of this study was to develop a wearable motion sensor system to correctly classify foot landing, specifically distinguishing between heel and toe landing during a game of badminton, to discern the high impact on the lower limb, which is susceptible to injury. For the classification of foot landing, we developed a machine-learning algorithm to evaluate its performance. Eight healthy participants (age: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{21.4}\pm \mathbf{1.5}$</tex> years) were analyzed. Experimental results indicate that our trained algorithm achieves an accuracy of 97.53% for foot landing classification.

articleTitle: Kalasag: Development of Smartfoam for an Arnis Electronic Scoring System
abstract: Electronic scoring systems in combat sports aim to ensure fair and objective scoring by using wearable electronics to detect impacts on valid body parts, reducing human error. This technology has been successfully integrated into protective gear in sports like Olympic Fencing and Taekwondo. This study focuses on developing a low-cost electronic scoring system for Arnis, the national sport of the Philippines. The proposed system uses a Smartfoam architecture with an RFID-based proximity sensor and a Velostat-based thin film impact sensor. To evaluate the system, a stationary test bed simulated a sparring match between two Arnis athletes. The test, repeated three times, measured the accuracy of hit validation by comparing detected hits to actual valid hits. The system achieved a high accuracy rate of 99%. The few missed hits were attributed to issues with the RFID reader and tags in the Smartfoam and Arnis stick. Thus, the study recommends further experiments to optimize the RFID components for better performance.

articleTitle: Using Local Phase Quantization to Identify Fake Faces in Online Social Networks
abstract: The rapid advancement of Generative AI, especially Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), has increased the issue of fake news on Online Social Networks (OSNs) by generating deceptive face images for social media profiles. Although existing detection methods are accurate, their effectiveness decreases when images are post-processed, which is common on OSNs. In this paper, we present LPQ-Net, a model combining Local Phase Quantization (LPQ) for feature extraction with a CNN-based classifier. We explore two variants: one sets a new benchmark in detecting StyleGAN2-generated images, and the other excels in identifying images shared on Facebook, WhatsApp, and Instagram. LPQ-Net also operates with minimal parameters, outperforming state-of-the-art methods and making it ideal for resource-constraint applications. Furthermore, our solution demonstrates its effectiveness by performing exceptionally well in detecting images generated by various Diffusion models. We further show that incorporating LPQ features into fine-tuned classifiers like ResNet50, ResNet101, InceptionV3, and DenseNet121 significantly improves performance.

articleTitle: Q-Learning and Double Q-Learning with Sliding Mode Control to stabilize a Ball-and-Beam System
abstract: In this paper, Q-learning and Double Q-learning reinforcement learning algorithms were used to fine-tune sliding mode controller parameters to balance the Ball-and-Beam system. Each algorithm was experimented with a 5-action action set and a 12-action action set, and the results were compared. The result is evaluated based on the system response after a disturbed reset. The experiment result shows that Double Q-learning performs better with larger action sets, putting the ball at the center of the beam only after 1.8 seconds. However, Q-learning performs better with smaller action sets, taking up to 2.3 seconds. Double Q-learning generally performed better than Q-learning, taking approximately 0.3 seconds less overall.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependence of Photogenerated Carriers in GaN Layer of AlGaN/GaN HEMT
abstract: In this study, we irradiated light with energy greater than the bandgap of GaN from the top of the GaN-HEMT to generate photogenerated carriers in the GaN layer. By investigating the behavior of photogenerated carriers, we elucidated the carrier behavior in the GaN layer. Photogenerated carriers were generated under different temperatures. The temperature dependence of the high frequency characteristics of photogenerated carriers was also investigated. According to the results, the attenuation of high-frequency gain due to high temperature was canceled out by photogenerated carriers. Furthermore, analysis of the parasitic capacitance between the gate and source electrodes confirmed that the parasitic capacitance tended to increase as the drain voltage increased. The hole accumulation effect caused by photogenerated-carrier holes of near the source electrode was experimentally found to inhibit current gain amplification.

articleTitle: Characterizing the Effects of Different Music Genres in Brain Circuit Dynamics of Patients with Depression using Neural Manifold Learning
abstract: Mental health disorders, or neuropsychiatric disorders, encompass disturbances in cognition, emotion, behavior, and physical well-being, with depression being one of the most prevalent. The subcortical limbic brain regions, particularly the amygdala, hippocampus, and dorsomedial thalamus, are profoundly impacted in depressed individuals. Music therapy has emerged as a promising intervention for various health issues, including depression, demonstrating substantial improvements in mental health, emotional well-being, and overall quality of life. Despite its global recognition, music therapy remains underutilized in the Philippines. This study aims to quantitatively assess the neu-rophysiological effects of music on patients diagnosed with depression using EEG-based neural manifold learning. This paper implements neural manifold learning and analysis on two datasets to quantitatively assess the effects of music on brain states and to characterize the effects of depression on neural manifolds. Our analysis revealed that distinct features of music provide a compelling effect on the neural manifold structures, suggesting a relationship between musical properties and brain dynamics. This research seeks to advance the understanding of music therapy's potential as a viable treatment for depression, particularly within the Philippine context.

articleTitle: Detecting Eggs of Invasive Apple Snails on Rice Fields Using YOLOv8 Algorithm
abstract: Apple snails are invasive species that reproduce rapidly, outcompete native species, damage ecosystems, and even endanger human health. They threaten agriculture by consuming rice seedlings in their early stages and potentially transmit crop diseases, causing significant economic and environmental harm. Though various management techniques are employed to control their population, these methods primarily focus on adult apple snail invaders and cause unintended harm to non-target species. Hence, detecting them early at their embryonic stage is crucial to mitigate the negative impacts of the apple snails and their traditional management methods alike. Utilizing object detection and embedded computing boards, apple snails can be managed in an environmentally sustainable and economically feasible manner. This study introduced an object detection model that localizes apple snail egg masses, leveraging YOLOv8 - a leading one-shot object detection framework, in conjunction with the Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, creating a portable and handheld detector. The developed model achieved impressive precision, recall, m<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>P50, and mAP50-95 rates, respectively (92.708%, 88.6%, 94.22%, 74.62%), demonstrating their effectiveness.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Sensor Fault Mitigation
abstract: Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) technology has proven great potential in industrial, commercial, and consumer applications specifically in the field of process monitoring and control. The adoption of WSN for process monitoring and control delivers prodigious rewards over the conventional wired system. However, the low-cost sensors may create faulty measurements or fail completely. This might introduce serious glitches as the sensor data obtained is crucial. In this paper, an efficient method is proposed to predict the failed sensor data in a Wireless Sensor Network setup and compensate for sensor failures using machine learning and deep learning techniques. For implementation of the proposed algorithm the dataset from an industrial sensor network setup is considered for implementation.

articleTitle: Estimating the Inclination Angle of Steel Structures Using ToF Camera for Attractive Infrastructure Inspection Drones
abstract: In this paper, a method for estimating the inclination angle of steel structures using a Time of Flight (ToF) camera is proposed, enabling the attractive infrastructure inspection drone to be attracted to inclined steel surfaces. Through evalu-ation experiments, it was confirmed that the developed method can estimate the inclination angle of steel structures with a mean error of within 1 degree,

articleTitle: SigAuthUrdu: Signature Verification for Urdu Language
abstract: In this paper, we introduce SigAuthUrdu, a convolutional Siamese network designed to address offline writer-independent signature verification for the Urdu language. Siamese networks, consisting of twin networks with shared weights, are trained to map signatures into a feature space where dissimilar signatures are farther apart and similar signatures are closer together. This is achieved by presenting the network with pairs of similar and different signatures and optimizing the Euclidean distance between them. Our experiments on an Urdu dataset demonstrate the network's capability to accurately detect forgeries across various scripts and handwriting styles using dissimilarities. Additionally, we created and utilized our own dataset, 98UrduSignatureCorpus, for this purpose, as no such dataset previously existed. This dataset is a significant contribution, facilitating the development and evaluation of our Siamese network model for Urdu signature verification.

articleTitle: Centralizing Data Warehouse Platform for Mining Management Using AWS Computing Instance
abstract: Mining industry is one of significant industry in the world. In order to increase efficiency, safety, sustainability and environmental impacts in mining process. This article presents a centralized data platform for mining process by design based on microservices architecture which can be supported various of input data source such as manual form, excel file and internet of things (IoT) device and notification when the value is abnormal. Our platform implementation on Amazon Web Service (AWS) cloud. For development of productivity in process and controlling quality the mine environment. The results of the platform operations with various source of data acquisition with response time is less than 1.5 seconds per each request.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Selected Swarm-Based Robot Search Algorithms for Target Tracking
abstract: This study focuses on comparing the performance of several swarming algorithms, which are mainly basic and correlated with random walk, Brownian motion, and levy flight. These algorithms were applied to a swarm of E-pucks for tasks such as target tracking and surveying. The analysis evaluates algorithm accuracy, swarm and target density impacts, and consensus times. Correlated random walk achieved the highest accuracy, while Brownian motion and correlated random walk showed that higher swarm densities correlate with greater accuracy. The same insight may be acquired for target densities. From the simulation, it was seen that a greater number of targets allowed the swarm to acquire more accurate results. Lastly, for consensus times, it was a basic random walk that provided the most consistent and fastest consensus times, whereas correlated random walk provided high and greatly varying consensus times – indicating inconsistencies.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Capacitor-Based Active Cell Balancing Topologies for Lithium-Ion Battery Packs
abstract: With the rising demand for high-energy-density power sources, lithium-ion battery packs have become essential for powering electric vehicles, renewable energy systems, and numerous applications. However, imbalances in individual cells can reduce performance, lifespan, and yield safety concerns. Therefore, cell balancing becomes crucial to equalize battery packs. While passive balancing is common for its cost-efficiency and simplicity, this paper focuses on active cell balancing, specifically capacitor-based topologies, due to their low cost and ease of control. Two primary topologies were analyzed: the chain structure switched capacitor and the single switched capacitor configuration. These techniques were tested on a 6S1P battery pack of 18650 lithium-ion cells. From the software simulations, it was deduced that passive cell balancing resulted in the fastest balancing speed, followed by the two switched capacitor configurations. However, this came at the expense of wasting the excess energy into heat, with which the capacitor-based topologies optimized by cycling the charge. Nevertheless, considering the frequency of balancing throughout the battery lifespan, passive cell balancing proves to be more suitable for low- to mid-power applications, while the benefits of active cell balancing become more evident for high power applications.

articleTitle: Dual Mode Output Capacitorless Low Dropout with Low Quiescent Current for Hearing Aid Applications
abstract: This paper presents a novel low dropout regulator (LDO) for hearing aid applications, implemented in 65 nm CMOS technology. The LDO, designed without an output capacitor, achieves a low quiescent current of 3.09 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathbf{A}$</tex> through subthreshold operation. It features an adaptively biased regulation mechanism with two power transistors, supporting load current range up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$500\ \mu\mathbf{A}$</tex>. The Dynamic Voltage Scaling (DVS) block offers normal and low power modes, regulating output voltages to 0.7 V and 0.9 V. Simulation results show a power consumption of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.4 \mu\mathbf{W}$</tex>, PSRR of -75 dB at 1 kHz, line and load regulation of 1.10.7 mV/V and 0.484 mV/mA, respectively, and a settling time of 1.37 to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.6\ \mu\mathbf{s}$</tex>. The LDO maintains 0.9 V output for input voltages between 1.1 V and 1.4 V in normal mode, and 0.7 V at 1 V input in low power mode, with a dropout voltage of 100 mV and 89.89% efficiency.

articleTitle: Classification Precision in Endodontic Imaging: Advanced Deep Learning with Adaptive Squeeze-and-Excitation in Enhanced VGG-19 and Feature Pyramid Network
abstract: Precisely classifying and detecting endodontic treatment obturation is critical for effective dental diagnostics and optimal oral health. Conventional strategies are time-consuming and often need more precision. This study presents a novel deep-learning-based architecture, VGG19Fpn-ASENet, which is a modification of the VGG-19 network incorporating a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) and an Adaptive Squeeze-and-Excitation Network (ASENet) to enhance performance in this application. The existing SENet, known for its efficiency and compactness, has been refined by integrating these modifications to enhance feature extraction and adaptability. The proposed VGG19Fpn-ASENet model was evaluated using an open-access endodontic treatment image dataset, achieving 100% accuracy in both training and validation phases and 99.51 % accuracy on the test set. This significant advancement exhibits the model's prospect of greatly enhancing diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in dental care.

articleTitle: Exploratory Data Analysis for Brain Stroke Prediction Using Multiple Regression Models
abstract: Stroke has been one of the leading causes of death. Recognizing its warning signs early can lessen its severity and maximize the effectiveness of its prevention. A highly effective data-driven predictive algorithm is needed for this, which can be done through various machine learning-based techniques. In this paper, Linear Support Vector Machines (linear-SVM), Radial Support Vector Machines (rbf-SVM), Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Gaussian Naive Bayes, and Random Forests were used for stroke prediction. Among these models, linear-SVM, rbf-SVM, and Logistic Regression yielded the highest accuracy value of 95%. Cross-validation and boosting through ensembling were also conducted to further enhance the overall confidence of model prediction.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Refreshable Braille Display for Learning Braille Fundamentals
abstract: Learning for the visually impaired has been mainly based on Braille, a haptic assistive technology that aids in reading and writing through an embossed dot. However, the currently available braille in the market is expensive and not reusable, making it more unreasonable for its price, which results in low braille literacy in the country. These problems led to the conceptualization of a three-character refreshable braille display integrated with deep learning optical character recognition (OCR). The development of the device aims to instruct braille fundamentals not just among the visually impaired but also among all Filipinos who wish to learn braille. By following the Iterative Project Development Model, an operational device was successfully developed. The device was found to be effective in providing an introduction or teaching braille fundamentals. However, the functionality of improving braille literacy was not achieved due to the time required to test one's literacy. Test results show an unfavorable response time due to device limitations, but evaluation presents that integrating GPU into the device would greatly improve the response time.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of a Rain-Powered Pelton Turbine
abstract: This study presents numerical simulations and analysis of rain power Pelton wheel turbine for a household application. The material used and compared in the simulation are ABS AND A390 Aluminum Alloy. An average rainfall data was used in the modeling simulation with different head height and number of buckets. Torque, RPM and Shaft Power were simulated using SolidWorks. Based on the simulation the 22 & 24 number of buckets at a height of 3 meter have a close result with the two dissimilar materials. In this research a rain power Pelton wheel turbine with different materials, varying height and number of buckets was simulated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Smart Docent System for Visually Impaired People with Mobile-Based Artificial Intelligence of Things
abstract: With the increasing demand for high-quality user experiences in museums and art galleries, interest in smart guidance systems has grown. These systems aim to provide detailed information about the artwork and deliver audio explanations related to the pieces of interest. Traditional guidance systems typically use techniques such as numbering, QR codes, and beacons. However, these methods can be challenging for visually impaired individuals, as they rely on visual cues. To address this issue, this paper introduces a novel smart docent system designed to enhance the gallery experience for visually impaired visitors. The system features two primary functional frameworks, supported by Artificial Intelligence (AI) models: user escorting and audio touring. These frameworks utilize mobile-based sensing, dynamic Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) beaconing, and edge computing. The system employs an on-device object detection model to minimize communication delays caused by large amounts of visual data. Although BLE beacons are statically installed within the art gallery, they dynamically update location IDs. Edge computing helps correct positioning errors based on the user's movement history and direction. Moreover, the system adaptively provides an audio tour based on the user's behavior, such as approaching or passing by artwork, or leaving an exhibit while listening to audio descriptions.

articleTitle: Tunable 1st Order IIR Phase Shifter Design and Implementation
abstract: This paper presents a new phase shifter which is a first-order infinite impulse response (IIR) filter that can shift phase both in phase-lead <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0^{\circ}\ \text{to}+180^{\circ})$</tex> and phase-lag <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-180^{\circ}\ \text{to}\ 0^{\circ})$</tex> fashion. Moreover, continuous phase tuning is also proposed in our phase shifter. The z-transform pair of phase-shifted cosine signal is utilized as the origin, then factorization of such term can give transfer function of first-order IIR phase shifter. The filter structure realization of the tunable phase shifter will be shown and applied with a digital cosine oscillator. Both simulation and hardware experiments can show phase-shifted signals in real-time controlled by phase-tuning parameters compared with a cosine reference signal as a demonstration. The allpass phase shifter will be used as a benchmark, and trade-off analysis using the proposed phase shifter will also be discussed.

articleTitle: IMU-Based Model for Precise Toothbrush Stroke and Orientation Tracking
abstract: This paper presents a model designed for precise orientation estimation and stroke distance tracking of toothbrush activity. The model leverages Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) technology, which includes accelerometers and gyroscopes, to capture detailed motion data during the activity. The proposed Corrective Fusion Filter Technique (CFFT) helps integrate accelerometer and gyroscope data with several corrective steps to estimate orientation precisely, and the combined sensor data accurately measures stroke distance. This filtering method also minimizes sensor noise and drifting issues, enhancing the model's reliability and performance.

articleTitle: ConvKAN: A Convolutional KAN for Brain Tumor MRI Classification
abstract: Brain tumors represent a critical challenge in medical diagnostics due to their diverse manifestations and the necessity for precise classification from MRI scans to facilitate effective treatment decisions. This paper introduces a novel Convolutional KAN (Kolmogorov Arnold Network) architecture tailored for the classification of brain tumors, including subtypes such as glioma, meningioma, pituitary adenoma, and non-tumor cases. Inspired by the Kolmogorov-Arnold superposition theorem, the network integrates advanced convolutional layers with attention mechanisms to enhance feature extraction and interpretability. The model harnesses the intricate spatial patterns and structural anomalies typical of brain tumors, capturing subtle nuances in MRI scans that traditional methods often overlook. Experimental validation demonstrates the network's robust performance in accurately categorizing tumors, leveraging saliency maps for visualizing crucial diagnostic features. This research significantly advances automated brain tumor diagnostics, potentially revolutionizing clinical practices by offering reliable and efficient diagnostic tools that aid in timely and accurate patient care.

articleTitle: Time Efficiency of BATS Coding on Wireless Relay Network with Overhearing
abstract: Wireless relay network is a solution to extend the reach of a wireless connection by installing a relay node between the source node and the sink node. Due to the broadcast nature of wireless transmission, the sink node has a chance to receive part of the data sent by the source node. In this paper, we apply a network coding scheme called BATS codes on a wireless relay network where the relay node has a stable power supply, so that we can aim for the best decoding time instead of minimizing the number of transmissions for saving energy. We optimize the time efficiency that maximize the average decoding rate per unit time by some heuristics, and bring out a message that it is not optimal to set an average number of recoded packets per batch at the relay node equals the number of packets per batch sent by the source node.

articleTitle: Towards Collaborative Weather Sensing: An SDR-Based Interoperability Gateway for Weather Information Aggregation (SIGWA)
abstract: Weather Monitoring Systems available in the market are typically closed systems that are designed to work only with other equipment from the same manufacturer. This hinders the collection of information from a variety of weather stations, preventing denser data collection and better observation of weather patterns through collaborative weather sensing among individuals and institutions. We leveraged the programmability of software-defined radios (SDRs) to enable collecting data from multiple, heterogeneous weather stations by a single radio. We developed a weather station gateway equipped with SDRs that are programmed to receive and decode information from weather stations that use different protocols and operate at distinct frequencies. Data from these stations are stored both locally and online, with update intervals being real-time for the local storage and every 15 minutes for the online database. Deployment results show reliable data reception from the heterogeneous weather stations over a 24-hour period.

articleTitle: Flatness Based Robust Control of Planar Snake Robot for Linearly Parameterizable Uncertainties
abstract: The state-of-the-art approach for solving the ma-neuvering control problem of a planar snake robot involves the adoption of a multi-layered control methodology. A gait function is imposed to achieve a desired body shape and subsequently, the gait parameters are adapted to obtain desired heading and velocity in separate layers. To facilitate simpler control design and trajectory planning, a differential flatness based approach has been proposed in this work utilizing the same serpenoid gait function. Filter tracking error based flat outputs have been chosen to obtain a flat system that can utilized to design suitable control law. A robust-adaptive control law has been designed for the flat system considering linearly parametrizable uncertainties which results into UUB stability of the same as verified through Lyapunov's method. Simulation studies affirm the performance of the proposed approach for a planar snake robot with parametric uncertainties.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Microstrip Patch Hexagonal Koch Antenna with Defected Ground Structure for Ku and K Band Applications
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a microstrip patch Hexagonal Koch antenna with a Defected Ground Structure operating at 13.2 GHz, 18 GHz, 22.7 GHz, and 24.7 GHz. The antenna features dimensions of 60 mm in length, 60 mm in width, and 0.12 cm in height, with RT duroid 5880 substrate adapted to achieve a gain of 8 dB within a multiband frequency range. Defecting the ground structure allows for increased power and efficient signal transmission in the specified frequency band. The design methodology, simulation, and performance evaluation of the proposed antenna are carried out using the HFSS tool. This antenna is suitable for various communication, radar, and satellite applications requiring Ku and K band frequency bandwidths.

articleTitle: fNIRS Acquisition Device for Monitoring Cognitive Load
abstract: Accurate and accessible cognitive load monitoring is essential for improving personalized learning and facilitating better mental health monitoring. Existing methods for measuring cognitive load can be intrusive, costly, and less effective for individuals with high melanin concentrations, emphasizing the need for an improved approach. This study presents a novel approach to monitoring the cognitive load using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) technology. A lightweight, cost-effective fNIRS device with a single optode was developed to record prefrontal cortex data, specially designed to suit the skin with high melanin concentration. Data from participants performing n-back tasks revealed significant differences between hemoglobin concentrations among 1-back, 2-back, and 3-back tasks via ANOVA analysis. To further explore cognitive load assessment, various machine learning models were implemented using open-access datasets acquired during n-back tasks. LSTM demonstrated the highest accuracy at 89.55%, suggesting its selection as the best model. The chosen LSTM model was then employed on our recorded dataset, achieving an accuracy of 74.04%. This integration of fNIRS technology and machine learning holds promise for accurate and accessible cognitive load assessment, with potential applications in education, human-computer interaction, and neuroscience research, contributing to a more sustainable future.

articleTitle: Predicting On-Road Carbon Emissions Using Traffic Camera Images
abstract: This article presents a framework for estimating carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from highways using images captured at regular intervals by traffic speed cameras, complemented by speed data collected from loop detectors on expressways and major arterial roads. Vehicle counting is performed using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) algorithm to identify and classify cars, buses, and trucks. The results highlight variations in traffic flow and emissions between weekdays and weekends.

articleTitle: AI Based Fish Feed Distributor
abstract: Aquaculture has emerged as a crucial industry to meet the escalating global demand for seafood. In this industry, the efficient management of fish feed plays a pivotal role in the health and growth of aquatic species. One of the primary factors contributing to the economic significance of fish feed in aquaculture is its substantial share in the total variable costs. Any improvements in the efficiency of fish feed utilization directly impact the economic viability of fish farming. Minimizing fish feed loss emerges as a strategic imperative to enhance profitability and sustainability in the aquaculture sector. Fish feed loss poses a multifaceted challenge to the aquaculture industry. Unutilized feed can contribute to nutrient overload in aquaculture ponds, leading to water quality degradation, oxygen depletion and increased susceptibility to diseases. Addressing these challenges is crucial not only for the overall expenditure of the aquaculture operations but also for the overall sustainability of the industry.

articleTitle: Quartered Chirp Spectral Envelope for Whispered vs Normal Speech Classification
abstract: Whispered speech as an acceptable form of human-computer interaction is gaining traction. Systems that address multiple modes of speech require a robust front-end speech clasifier. Performance of whispered vs normal speech classification drops in the presence of additive white Gaussian noise, since normal speech takes on some of the characteristics of whispered speech. In this work, we propose a new feature named the quartered chirp spectral envelope, a combination of the chirp spectrum and the quartered spectral envelope, to classify whispered and normal speech. The chirp spectrum can be fine-tuned to obtain customized features for a given task, and the quartered spectral envelope has been proven to work especially well for the current task. The feature is trained on a one dimensional convolutional neural network, that captures the trends in the spectral envelope. The proposed system performs better than the state of the art, in the presence of white noise.

articleTitle: Detection of Violators of Garbage Disposal Schedule with Monitoring System
abstract: The Detection of Violators of Garbage Disposal Schedule with Monitoring System tackles important waste management issues such as compliance challenges with garbage disposal schedules, illegal dumping, and monitoring problems in Barangay Santiago, Malvar, Batangas. The work relies on rigorous data collection from related studies and literature, which is enriched by the knowledge gained from interviews with local government representatives. Through the use of camera technology, the system proposed here provides a new way to improve monitoring and enforcement. The efficiency of the project clearly exceeds existing solutions, demonstrated through the thorough evaluation of the metric system. This new system will help other areas to have positive results for more efficient waste disposal, safe, clean and healthy environment. More studies can be conducted to determine its scalability, cost-effectiveness, and the potential of adaptations for different geographical areas to make it more effective and sustainable.

articleTitle: CCTV on Steroids: The Design and Implementation of BantAI, a Robbery Prediction System for Edge Devices
abstract: Traditional surveillance systems reliant on human monitoring often struggle to deliver the speed and accuracy required for effective robbery detection. Drawing inspiration from the Filipino concept of bantay, which means to keep a watchful eye, we designed and implemented BantAI, a watchful AI that is lightweight enough to run on an edge device. BantAI operates as a two-stage system that automates surveillance and predicts potential robberies before they occur. The first stage consists of machine learning modules that analyze the video feed to detect behaviors that are often related to robberies: crowding, loitering, and concealment of one's face in public. The outputs from these modules are forwarded to the second stage, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) inference system that generates the Robbery Behavior Potential (RBP). We deployed BantAI on a resource- constrained edge device and demonstrated that it can achieve an F1 score of 0.756 and a prediction lead time of 25.17 seconds.

articleTitle: RF-to-DC Conversion Circuit with Configurable Impedance Matching Circuit for RF Energy Harvesting in 65nm CMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a multiband rectifier with a configurable impedance matching circuit and a low-dropout (LDO) voltage regulator for RF energy harvesting applications at 1.8GHz, 2.1GHz, and 2.4GHz frequency bands. The configurable impedance matching circuit allows the shifting between the three target impedance settings to optimize the system performance in each frequency band. The rectifier circuit is coupled with an auxiliary PMOS transistor for threshold voltage cancellation, enhancing the DC extraction efficiency of the conventional circuit. The LDO voltage regulator circuit is designed with Miller compensation to ensure stability and prevent oscillations in the control loop and a feedback capacitor to improve its transient response. Simulation results show that the overall efficiency of the proposed RF -to-DC conversion circuit is 75.4 % with power dissipation of 6.71 mW, average peak PCE of 63.7 %, and average APE of 9.4 % at the three target frequencies for a regulated DC output voltage of 1V with an output load resistance of 50k Ω. The proposed conversion circuit is implemented using 65nm CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Safe and Trustworthy AI Framework (STAIF): Addressing Uncertainty in AI-Based Models for Real-World Deployment
abstract: While artificial intelligence (AI) has great promise for revolutionizing many facets of our lives, questions about its ethical and long-term use still need to be answered. Recognizing the widespread impact of AI, governments have initiated legislation, with the European Union's AI Act and the United States' AI Act as pioneering efforts. AI's connection to sustainability factors, including trustworthiness, reliability, privacy and security, efficiency, and ethics, necessitates careful consideration. This paper proposes a framework for integrating safe and trustworthy AI practices into AI development and deployment, aimed at promoting reliability, efficiency, and sustainability. Extending the Software Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (SFMEA), the framework proactively identifies and mitigates potential risks based on system criticality, enhancing reliability and trust. Additionally, the paper discusses implementation strategies for building trustworthy AI systems, incorporating sustainability goals, and presents a case study using this framework. The conclusion highlights the framework's potential to guide the development of responsible AI for a sustainable future, acknowledging ongoing challenges and future research directions.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Wearable Nasal Sensor for Respiratory Assessments Using a NOVEL EDRS-LSTM Deep Learning Model
abstract: Recent advances in the wearable sensing technology haves paved the development of various wearable respiratory sensors that aids in monitoring the breathing patterns as well as to handle covid-19 like extraordinary situations. This specific research work highlights the performance of the wearable nasal mask integrated with multivariable sensors for breathing/respiratory assessments. A flexible miniaturized nasal sensor with electronics to measure the variation of left and right nostril has been designed and was attached on the inner part of the n95 mask for continuous recordings of respiratory signals. Three variables, temperature, pressure and humidity which were the integral part of the nasal sensor were then used to collect the breathing patterns with normal and deep breathing as well as breathing changes while walking. Inorder to assess the efficiency of the wearable nasal mask, a novel Encoder-Decoder Respiratory Signal-LSTM (EDRS-LSTM) deep learning model was deployed to perform multi pattern recognition. The proposed study involves 42 healthy volunteers with 35 minutes recording and a total of 2 trials was conducted. Experimental results showed an overall accuracy of 99.69% with AUC value 1.0 and F1score of 0.99 with the proposed deep learning model. The designed wearable with multiparameter variables with left and right nostril ensures the recognition of breathing patterns with an overall accuracy of 99.69% while comparing its performance with other known deep learning models such as RNN.

articleTitle: Learning Media Advancement Using Virtual Reality Technology for Heavy Equipment Safety in Indonesian Vocational Schools
abstract: Mining Geology is one of the study programs provided by Indonesian Vocational Schools that explores surface mining. Mining is a work in hazardous environments that poses numerous risks. The use of heavy equipment is a frequent cause of mining accidents. Therefore, enhancing vocational students' understanding of heavy equipment safety is essential. However, having heavy equipment for learning its safety is costly and complex maintenance, demanding substantial financial investment from schools. Moreover, many vocational schools still use traditional learning media that cannot provide an immersive experience in learning. Thus, this study developed an immersive and engaging virtual reality (VR)-based learning media for vocational students learning heavy equipment safety. The validity and feasibility of the learning media contents were evaluated by experts. The result concluded that the contents presented are valid and have good feasibility. Moreover, the learning media was tested in the learning process and the usability was assessed by vocational students. The result concluded that the learning media demonstrates significant potential to improve the educational experience in vocational schools, leading to better learning outcomes and increased student engagement.

articleTitle: A Novel Machine Learning Approach to Optimize Energy Forecasting in Industry
abstract: The rising energy costs and increasing environmental concerns have compelled industries to seek innovative solutions for optimizing their energy consumption. This paper presents a data-driven approach utilizing Internet of Things (IoT) sensors to collect energy data and a comparative study on various time series forecasting techniques to improve energy forecasting in industries. This experiment is based on public energy usage dataset from steel company which produces various types of steel plates, iron plates and coils. In this paper, we have discussed about the data preprocessing techniques including effective feature engineering and use various Machine Learning (ML) techniques to identify patterns and trends. Also, we have compared the results with previous research outcomes on various time series forecasting models such as deep learning, and other ensemble techniques tested with this dataset for improved energy consumption forecasts. This paper shows how including additional features improves the prediction accuracy of the models allowing industries to achieve optimal energy utilization. The results shows that XGBoost model consistently outperformed other models in energy forecasting with lowest RMSE value of 0.037 and MAE of 0.015 comparing with other deep learning and tree based techniques. The proposed methodology has the potential to significantly reduce energy costs by finding the area to save energy, improve sustainability, and enhance operational efficiency in various industrial sectors.

articleTitle: Cuckoo Search Based MPPT with Quadra Tied Solar PV Array for Maximising Power Extraction Under Partial Shadows
abstract: Solar photovoltaics are playing a key role in letting us meet our energy needs and it is important to harvest it efficiently to make it commercially viable. In this paper, a Cuckoo Search (CS) based MPPT algorithm is used to mitigate the challenges caused by partial shading of solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays and enable extraction of maximum power. The PV array is connected in a novel Quadra Tied (QT) configuration which is also designed to produce maximum power under various partial shading conditions (PSCs). This combination is tested under different PSCs common in urban areas using simulations in Simulink and in real time with Chroma Solar PV simulator and Texas Instruments TMS320F28379D micro controller. The performance of the CS MPPT algorithm is compared with the conventional Perturb & Observe (P&O) MPPT algorithm.

articleTitle: Hybrid Digital Twin-P&O Photovoltaic Controller for Partial Shading Conditions
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) arrays have emerged as a prominent clean and renewable energy source within modern smart grids. However, this transition in energy production brings forth new challenges, one of which is partial shading. Partial shading refers to the uneven shading pattern that occurs on a PV array, leading to multiple peaks on the PV power curve. Traditional Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) methods often struggle to extract the maximum power under such conditions. This paper investigates the potential of utilizing digital twins, an emerging technology, to address this challenge. Digital twins represent virtual counterparts of physical objects—in this case, the PV array. These virtual models are engineered to estimate the maximum power point of a PV array amidst partial shading conditions. A hybrid controller that integrates a neural network-based digital twin with a conventional perturb and observe (P&O) controller is proposed. Through simulations conducted using Simulink and Python under rapidly changing irradiance conditions, the efficacy of the proposed approach is validated. Simulation results demonstrate that the hybrid controller effectively extracts the maximum power from the PV array even under partial shading conditions.

articleTitle: Configurable FOCV- Based MPPT for Indoor Light and TEG Energy Harvesting Systems
abstract: This study introduces a configurable Maximum Power Point Tracker (MPPT) designed for energy harvesting systems, focusing on optimizing output power from ambient light using photovoltaic (PV) cells and heat gradient from thermoelectric generators (TEG). Utilizing the Fractional Open Circuit Voltage (FOCV) algorithm, the configurable MPPT system achieves a tracking efficiency that exceeds 90 percent for PV cells and over 70 percent for TEG. Notably, it demonstrates excellent performance in tracking the Vmpp for PV cells for 0.8V to 1.2V input voltage. Also, it effectively tracks the Vmpp for TEG systems, consistently maintaining a stable output response for input voltages below 0.6V relative to Voc. The power consumption of the MPPT system remained relatively low, measuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$246.4\text{uW}$</tex> when a PV source is utilized and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$217.5\text{uW}$</tex> when a TEG source is employed, indicating efficient operation.

articleTitle: PointBi-FPN: An Extention to Pointpillars for LiDAR 3D Object Detection in Autonomous Vehicles Using Bi-Directional Feature Pyramid Network
abstract: Autonomous vehicles increasingly rely on accurate three-dimensional (3D) object detection for safe navigation. While two-dimensional (2D) methods offer computational efficiency, the shift to 3D detection enhances precision in understanding environments. Point-based and voxel-based approaches are accurate but computationally intensive for onboard deployment. Pillar-based methods like PointPillars provide efficiency but may lack detection accuracy compared to voxel-based approaches. In this paper, we focus on enhancing the performance of PointPillars, a popular pillar-based detector, using LiDAR data. The proposed approach (PointBi-FPN) employs a bi-directional feature pyramid network (Bi-FPN) as a backbone, that aggregates multiscale features in the input data, providing a holistic view of the environment, which is crucial for detecting objects of varying sizes and distances accurately. Bi-FPN improves the model's understanding of complex scenes, making it more robust to occlusions. Through extensive experimentation on the KITTI dataset, the PointBi-FPN approach demonstrates better performance across all three detection benchmarks: BEV (Bird's Eye View), 3D (Three-Dimensional), and AOS (Average Orientation Similarity). Notably, the proposed approach exhibits significant improvements, particularly in accurately detecting objects labeled as “hard” difficulty.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of KNIME Low Code Platform in Deep Learning Study and Optimal Hyperparameter Tuning
abstract: A low-code platform is a software development environment that allows for the creation of applications through graphical user interfaces and configuration instead of traditional hand-coded computer programming. In this study, the application to classify a dataset of traffic sign images using the KNIME low-code deep learning development platform will be discussed to represents this software performance especial in term of model optimization processes. By creates the workflow to perform image preprocessing, create the CNN layer under KERAS sequential API and finding the best set of key hyperparameters among traditional KNIME build-in optimization algorithm including Brute force, Hill climbing, random search, Bayesian Optimization and black-box optimizer Optuna optimization algorithm under 3 types CNN architecture as simple CNN, Resnet-50 and VGG16 to classify traffic sign images. The result demonstrates that both grid search and random search optimization can be effective, while both Optuna and Bayesian optimization stands out as a powerful method due to its ability to efficiently explore the hyperparameter space and achieve superior results to meet 99% accuracy under simple CNN environment, but Optuna is significantly improve optimization times than Bayesian about 7 - 8 times. The KNIME low-code platform provides a user-friendly environment for developing and fine-tuning models to contribute the ongoing progress in machine learning and deep learning research development.

articleTitle: Ransopedia: Your Trusty Guide to Ransomware Trends
abstract: Ransomware is a form of malware which attackers use to encrypt corporate and individual victims' data to blackmail them for financial gain. While ransomware-related cyberattacks occur frequently, information regarding historical ransomware attacks and their exploited vulnerabilities is sparse and unorganized. We present Ransopedia, a tool that achieves two goals. Firstly, it is a curated encyclopedia that is intended to provide the public with insights on ransomware attacks and associated vulnerabilities. Secondly, it forecasts potential future vulnerabilities through predictive analytics.

articleTitle: Adaptive PV Systems: Using Genetic Algorithm and Random Forest Classifier to Mitigate the Effects of Partial Shading on Solar Photovoltaic Systems
abstract: Mismatch losses due to partial shading of solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays can limit their generated power. One method to improve their power output is to electrically reconfigure the array based on the principle of row irradiance equalization. Shaded panels in an array are identified to determine the array's optimal configuration and maximize its power output. In this study, a random forest classification model was developed to identify the partial shading pattern incident on an array. Features of the model included the individual panel currents and the array irradiance of preset 20 shading patterns. The data used to train the model was obtained using an off-grid <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 3$</tex> array composed of nine 10-W PV modules in total-cross-tied (TCT) topology. The model achieved a mean accuracy of 90% using the testing data and 98% using 5-fold cross-validation. This was integrated with a genetic algorithm-based irradiance equalization heuristic, which takes a predicted shading pattern as input and outputs an optimized configuration. For each shading pattern, the suggested reconfiguration was recorded and its corresponding power change was calculated. Power recovery ranged from −15.70% to 40%. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 3$</tex> PV array reconfigured successfully to the optimum configuration.

articleTitle: Psychological Aspects of AI Enhanced Learning Experiences
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the educational landscape by offering personalized learning experiences that cater to individual student needs. This report delves into the psychological aspects of AI -enhanced learning experiences, focusing on their impact on student motivation, engagement, cognitive load, and emotional well-being. By analyzing various case studies and existing literature, we explore the benefits and challenges associated with integrating AI into educational settings. The findings indicate that AI-driven tools can significantly enhance motivation and engagement by providing tailored learning paths and real-time, relevant feedback. Additionally, AI can help manage cognitive load and offer emotional support, fostering a supportive and effective learning environment. However, challenges such as dependency on technology, data privacy concerns, and potential stress must be addressed to fully harness the benefits of AI in education. This report underscores the importance of strategic implementation and continuous evaluation of AI tools to ensure they contribute positively to students' psychological well-being and academic success.

articleTitle: Hydrogen Sensing Properties of the Pt Caped Ag Doped Gallium Oxide Nanomaterials
abstract: A thin film of gallium oxide possesses the characteristics of an n-type semiconductor and remains stable at an elevated temperature. In a thin film, the concentration of hydrogen influences the resistivity of Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. A hydrogen sensor was constructed according to this design principle. With Ar as the sputtering gas, RF magnetron sputtering was used to deposit a gallium oxide film from the metal Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> target onto the alumina substrate. Thin coatings of Pt caped Ag doped Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> that conduct electricity and are hydrogen-sensitive at temperatures of 400°C were manufactured using a sputtering process. A bulk effect independent of the film thickness determines their sensitivity to stable hydrogen. The duration of the responses is measured in seconds. Pt caped Ag doped Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films have the potential to function as catalytically inactive hydrogen sensors when temperature compensation is appropriate.

articleTitle: A Study on New PWM Signal Generation and Control Methods Application in Power Electronics Control
abstract: In the field of electrical energy conversion, inverters and converters play an important role. In addition, motors will play a central role in the trend toward electrification of mobility. Inverters also are necessary for variable speed control of motors. A new PWM generation method to operate inverters is proposed and clarify its effectiveness. Furthermore, we will clarify that the proposed method will make the advanced control method easier to use and have a positive effect.

articleTitle: WENN-4: Weighted Ensemble for Enhanced Diabetic Retinopathy Detection
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a serious eye condition that impacts individuals with diabetes, leading to retinal damage and potentially resulting in gradual vision loss. In this paper, we proposed a novel framework for diabetic retinopathy detection using deep learning techniques. The proposed framework employs an ensemble learning model named WENN-4 to classify fundus images into five classes and measure the severity of blindness of individuals. The proposed framework consists of following steps: customized preprocessing method that includes Gaussian Blurring and augmentation techniques, subsequently followed by inputting the processed images into diverse CNN architectures to extract discriminatory feature vectors for classification and early diagnoses and categorizes blindness severity levels, including no-DR, mild DR, severe, moderate, or Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (PDR). To enhance the overall performance of our proposed framework, we utilized an ensemble of models, WENN-4. This ensemble comprises ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, InceptionV3, and EfficientNetV2. This model achieves a remarkable accuracy of 93.7% accuracy on test data of APTOS 2019, surpassing existing methods. This ensemble of models lead to increased accuracy by leveraging complementary strengths, correcting individual misclassifications, and ultimately producing superior outcomes.

articleTitle: Design of Control System for Adult Ventilator
abstract: This study describes the development of a control system for a low-cost ventilator prototype for adults. A prototype was developed based on the existing infant ventilator. Flow meters and another solenoid valve were integrated into the design to satisfy adult patients' requirements. Other components, such as PLC, HMI, LED light, buzzer, and throttling valves, were used. 3D printed parts were also developed for particular components that are not available off the shelf. Alarms were also incorporated in the system design. The ventilator was tested in different ventilator settings. Results show that the minimum requirement for an Emergency Use Ventilator (EUV) was satisfied. The range of Tidal Volume is 100mL to 650mL and 5cmH2O to 17 cmH2O for PEEP. For Tidal Volume, PEEP and PIP measurements, the values fall within the acceptable tolerances: ± 50mL or ±10% of measured value for Tidal Volume and ±2.5 cmH2O for PEEP and PIP. This study covers only the design and development, functional and stress testing. Clinical test will be conducted in separate study.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Cooperative Task Assignment and Path Planning Algorithms in UAV Networks
abstract: This paper aims to comprehensively perform an evaluation of cooperative task assignment and path planning algorithms for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks, designed for increased operational efficiency in a plethora of mission contexts. We carry out a systematic study of a range of the state-of-the-art algorithms, ranging from classical methods to advanced machine learning models with a view to understanding their efficacy in optimizing task assignment and flight path planning under a myriad of conditions. In our study, the critical factors considered for the performance evaluation of algorithms include mission completion time, energy efficiency, and collision probability in UAV networks. The qualitative and quantitative means of analysis are used to present the extent to which the performance and reliability of each algorithm is different. The simulation results show that the right algorithm has to be selected depending on the mission requirements, being aware of mission complexity, environment unpredictability, and computation resources.

articleTitle: Enhancing Deepfake Detection with Ensemble Learning: A Study on Celeb DF Dataset
abstract: Deepfakes, generated digital content using deep learning methods, have become more sophisticated nowadays with the development of new techniques like diffusion models. They are now causing a serious threat to the social balance, reducing trust in digital content. While research is still going on to improve the quality of generated content, techniques are also being developed to detect fake content. This research tackles particularly deepfake images. This research develops and tests a robust model based on ensemble learning on the Celeb-DF dataset. The ensemble technique used in this study is the averaging technique. At the same time, the efficiency of transfer learning models in detecting deepfakes is assessed. An accuracy of 97.62 % was achieved, testifying to the power of transfer learning and ensemble models. This paper showcases how different models can be used together to improve the accuracy and sensitivity of the models created to tackle the deepfake detection problem.

articleTitle: A Meta Surface Material Based Patch Antenna for Future Wireless Sensor Space Craft 5G Systems
abstract: As per latest technology and development, wireless sensor-based spacecraft design techniques are being using to detect the geometric parameters of humans become a future of innovative research.
