The meta surface are the periodic structures having doped semiconductor, metallic, and dielectric titanium as materials that are intended to interact with electromagnetic waves to enhance the performance of the radiator. Moreover, the meta surface has great potential as a high refractive index sensor for the detection of wireless sensor systems. In this paper, we are going to present a dielectric FR4 epoxy structure-based meta surface patch antenna. It is highlighted that the proposed antenna has a maximum reflection coefficient of -50 dB, with a valued gain of 9 dBi and a specified bandwidth 8 GHz at the resonating frequency 17 GHz. Our results demonstrate that the meta surface has a promising ultra-sensitive qualitative exposure in chemical and temperature sensing, with a low profile features. The proposed antenna have been measured and fabricated with the designed antenna parameters.

articleTitle: Optimizing Convolutional Image Processing on RISC-V Using Branch Prediction on FPGA
abstract: This paper explores the enhancement of convolutional image processing on a RISC-V based architecture through the implementation of branch prediction (BP) techniques. Con-volution, a critical operation in image processing, is essential for tasks such as edge detection, blurring, and feature extraction. Efficient execution of convolution operations, particularly in a RISC-V architecture, requires effective BP to minimize delays caused by conditional operations. This study presents the development of a 5-stage pipelined 32-bit RISC-V processor, integrated with a 2-bit saturating counter branch predictor using a Branch History Table (BHT). The efficiency of the RISC-V processor was evaluated by synthesizing and implementing it using Xilinx Vivado on the Kintex- 7 KC705 Evaluation Platform and testing with a convolution algorithm written in assembly language. Experimental results demonstrate that optimizing BP significantly improves the execution efficiency of convolution operations, making it a promising approach for advanced image processing applications.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Operating Point of Multi-Reactive Power Compensation Equipment Considering Facility Characteristics
abstract: Increased integration of renewable energy sources, which are typically inverter-based, has heightened concerns about voltage stability in power systems. This paper presents an optimization strategy for the operating points of reactive power compensation equipment, specifically Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) and fixed shunt capacitors, to enhance voltage stability. The proposed method employs QV sensitivity to linearize the relationship between reactive power and voltage, formulating the optimization problem as a Mixed Integer Quadratic Programming (MIQP) problem. By leveraging the unique characteristics of FACTS and shunt devices, the method aims to minimize voltage deviations and reactive power imbalance without extensive power flow calculations. Simulation results on the IEEE 39-bus system demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in maintaining voltage stability and optimizing the reactive power response under various loading conditions.

articleTitle: Real-Time AI-Driven People Tracking and Counting Using Overhead Cameras
abstract: Accurate people counting in smart buildings and intelligent transportation systems is crucial for energy management, safety protocols, and resource allocation. This is especially critical during emergencies, where precise occupant counts are vital for safe evacuation. Existing methods struggle with large crowds, often losing accuracy with even a few additional people. To address this limitation, this study proposes a novel approach combining a new object tracking algorithm, a novel counting algorithm, and a fine-tuned object detection model. This method achieves 97% accuracy in real-time people counting with a frame rate of 20–27 FPS on a low-power edge computer.

articleTitle: Score Calculation with Local and Global Features for Visual Place Recognition
abstract: Visual place recognition (VPR) seems effective for the localization process in visual navigation of a robot because a robot can recognize locations and poses using only visual information if the accuracy of VPR is sufficient. However, to apply VPR for actual scenarios where multiple locations to be distinguished are in a captured image, the classification accuracy should be improved. To solve this problem, we propose a novel method for likelihood computation in location matching composed of two kinds of components corresponding to local and global features. Experimental results using a novel dataset composed of actual images taken around the course of the Tsukuba Challenge showed that the proposed method improved accuracy by 1–6 % compared to conventional reranking methods using only local features.

articleTitle: Compact Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna with Harmonic Suppression for Enhanced Ambient RF Energy Harvesting
abstract: This work presents the design of a compact circularly polarized antenna with harmonic suppression for potential application in RF energy harvesting. The designed antenna operates at 2.4 GHz for suitable harvesting of energy from Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and other devices operating in the ISM band. The radiating unit comprises a rectangular patch embedded with cross shaped slot for harmonic suppression. Four unique bulb shaped structures with suitable modifications are also introduced close to the diagonal edges of the radiator to realize circular polarization. The designed antenna achieves a - 10 dB operating bandwidth of 80 MHz and axial ratio bandwidth of 20 MHz at the resonating frequency of 2.40 GHz. An overall gain of 3.9 dBi is also noticed within a compact circuit dimension of 47.2 × 53.7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Multi-Label Emotion Share Regression from Speech Using Pre-Trained Self-Supervised Learning Models
abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) has been enabling natural human-machine interaction. Previous SER only focused on predicting a single emotion from humans' voices, whereas emotions from voices might have multiple categories. This study aims to predict emotion share from a voice, i.e., the proportion of the different emotion categories expressed in the speech. We evaluated eight pretrained self-supervised learning (SSL) models from major companies for multilingual emotion share recognition. The models were evaluated on the Hume-Prosody dataset, which contains 51,881 samples of nine different emotion categories. We observed the important factor of wider window size for multilingual emotion share recognition in contrast to the narrow window size used (around 5.5 s). The most effective evaluated pretrained model for this case is the large version of HuBERT, which achieved a Spearman correlation score of 0.579, showing the feasibility of emotion share recognition using SSL.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of Multi-LFSR Pseudo Random Number Generator
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a hardware pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) using multiple linear feedback shift registers (LFSRs) for generating pseudo-random numbers and ambient electromagnetic noise for seed generation. The PRNG algorithm is deployed on a Digilent CMOD A7 field-programmable gate array (FPGA) board, producing 16-bit random numbers at a frequency of 50 kHz, which are then displayed on a 7-segment display. To facilitate the transfer of generated numbers to a laptop for further use in different applications, a dedicated high-speed UART with a baud rate of 1,152,000 is designed. The performance and effectiveness of the PRNG are evaluated in this setup.

articleTitle: Parametric Study of The Microstrip U-Slot Patch Antenna for Concrete Strength Monitoring
abstract: This paper presents a parametric study of a microwave microstrip patch antenna based using finite element modelling software to conduct simulations applied to dielectric material characterization. A probe-fed U-slot patch antenna has been designed to function as a material sensing applicator. The primary objective of this study is to provide non-destructive measurements for predicting the grades of cast concrete in the construction industry. The size, shape, and dimensions of the designed patch antenna are described in detail. The parametric study focuses on the shift in the minimum peak of return loss, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert$</tex> (dB) of the antenna in relation to changes in the dielectric constant of the material under test. The modelling done on the antenna show a significant response in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert$</tex>, when placed on materials selected to simulate concrete samples at different periods of the curing process, and also at different strength grades. It is known that different strength grades of concrete have varying relative permittivity and dielectric constant values. Consequently, the shift in the minimum peak of the measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert$</tex> (dB) correlates with changes in concrete strength, thus offering a simple, non-destructive, fast, and effective system for testing concrete quality.

articleTitle: TriSpectraLSTM for COPD Detection via Lung Sound Analysis
abstract: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease is a progressive health condition characterized by restricted air-flow in the lungs, leading to life-threatening risks including loss of life. Detecting and diagnosing COPD early can significantly enhance disease management and patient well-being. However, existing diagnostic approaches for COPD are costly, time-intensive, and demand specialized equipment. Consequently, there is a pressing demand for an automated, accessible, and cost-effective diagnostic tool for diagnosing COPD. This work proposes a novel TriSpectraLSTM model that listens to the melody of lung sounds through multiple audio features, such as: Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, chromagram, and Mel spectrograms. Each sub-model analyzes its assigned instrument, extracting distinct sonic signatures, before the hybrid network merges them, revealing the hidden COPD features. The model achieves a remarkable 93% accuracy on test data, surpassing existing methods. This multimodal approach by capturing the entire range of lung sounds, it produces a more precise and detailed diagnosis. This work employed the power of machine learning with healthcare, paving the way for a future where lung sounds become the key to diagnosing COPD diseases.

articleTitle: Linear Phase FIR Filter Design for Digital Hearing Aids Using a Neural Network-Based Optimization
abstract: A neural network-based optimization for the design of linear phase digital filters used in digital hearing aid applications is presented in this paper. To achieve hearing loss compensation, a 53-tap finite impulse response (FIR) filter is utilized, and the weights of the trained network can be used to obtain the impulse response of the FIR filter. The target frequency response or label comes from the audiogram, the training data is created, and a linear perceptron supervised learning model is used. Audiogram matchings are shown in design examples. The proposed neural network-based design approach can give a very high accuracy, high processing speed when compared with the existing methods, and also low complexity in filter structure realization.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control-based Adaptive Traffic Signaling Scheme for Philippine Urban Traffic
abstract: Traffic congestion is a recurring issue on Philippine urban roads resulting in increased travel times. One of the contributors to this is the inefficient fixed-time signaling in local stoplights. This work explored a Model Predictive Control (MPC)-based adaptive traffic system to solve the congestion issue. Using the SUMO simulator, the optimal green times of stoplights were computed and applied in a simulation of traffic in the Katipunan Avenue - Aurora Boulevard intersection in Metro Manila. The MPC-based scheme performed consistently better than the existing fixed-time signaling, reducing average queue time and queue length by 57.43 % and 41.85 %, respectively, for the same flow rate. The adaptive traffic scheme was also robust, with negligible degradation in performance when subjected to 20 % vehicle count errors.

articleTitle: ELECTRIFAI: An AI-Driven Solution for Enhancing Electricity Distribution Efficiency and Preventing Unauthorized Power Tapping in the Philippines
abstract: The Philippines faces significant challenges in its power sector, including power leakage, losses, and unauthorized electricity tapping. These issues led to substantial financial and environmental impacts, particularly for utility companies and local power cooperatives. ElectrifAI aims to enhance the efficiency of electricity distribution and mitigate losses through advanced technological solutions. The application integrates sensors and real-time data analysis to detect and address power leakages and inefficiencies. It utilizes the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) metric to measure and improve energy efficiency. ElectrifAI also combats unauthorized electricity tapping by employing advanced algorithms like the Isolation Forest, achieving a 98% accuracy rate in detecting anomalies. The system's smart grid capabilities allow proactive maintenance and immediate issue resolution, reducing operational costs and ensuring a stable power supply. Furthermore, a mobile application provides consumers with real-time insights into their energy consumption, promoting energy-saving behaviors. The implementation process involves meticulous component selection, integration of IoT devices, and extensive testing. Based on field trials, it demonstrated ElectrifAI's effectiveness in detecting unauthorized tapping and analyzing real-time data. By modernizing the power distribution network and integration of AI-driven solutions, ElectrifAI significantly enhances the reliability, efficiency, and sustainability of the power sector in the Philippines.

articleTitle: Impact of Dielectric Materials in an Asymmetrical Shaped Band to Band TFET
abstract: In this manuscript, the band-to-band tunnel field effect transistor TFET has an asymmetrical structure and is named a T-shaped channel TFET. The TFET drain current and transconductance parameters are analyzed at different dielectric materials and doping concentrations. Here observed that the ON current of the TEFT is high for HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gate dielectric compared to other materials. Also, the switching ratio of the TFET is higher than other material combinations. All these analyses are carried out in the TCAD-Sentaurus software. Due to double gate TFET, the device is better immune to the short channel variations. Because the device drives controllability more towards the gates. The doping concentration of the TFET also changes the drain current of the device.

articleTitle: Non-Contact Measurement of Temperature Using RGB Facial Images
abstract: With the arrival of COVID-19, non-contact temper-ature measurement methods quickly gained popularity and have since been used ubiquitously, from malls to government buildings. But research claims that the existing non-contact techniques are less accurate than the contact methods. To obviate this issue, this study proposes a novel algorithm for estimating body temperature without skin contact, using a smartphone camera that captures RGB facial videos. Involving 83 volun-teers, temperature measurements were taken from various body locations using infrared, digital, and analog thermometers. A 30-second facial video was recorded for each participant. Machine learning models were trained to estimate core body temperature from these images. The algorithm is based on a combination of image preprocessing techniques and hyperspectral bands extraction that quantify skin reddening with increasing temperature. The performance of different machine learning algorithms was discussed. Performance metrics revealed that the Extra Trees Regression model achieved the highest accuracy and the lowest Root Mean Square Error. Support Vector Machine required the least amount of computation time. Also, K-Nearest Neighbors algorithm has a good mix of accuracy, Root Mean Square Error, and computation time. Clinical validation against thermal camera measurements confirmed the algorithm's reliability.

articleTitle: Federated Byzantine Agreement-Inspired Blockchain Protocol for Swarm Robotics
abstract: In this study, we present a novel Federated Byzantine Agreement (FBA)-inspired consensus framework for swarm robotics, integrating blockchain technology to enhance security and efficiency. The proposed system leverages decentralized, scalable consensus without requiring global agreement, ensuring robustness against Byzantine attacks. We conducted extensive simulations using the ARGoS simulator and e-puck robots to validate the framework. Results indicate that the FBA approach significantly outperforms frameworks without blockchain and base blockchain configurations, demonstrating superior resilience and reliability in consensus maintenance. This framework is particularly applicable to real-world pi-puck and e-puck robots, offering a promising solution for secure and efficient swarm operations. The significant implications of this study include enhanced robustness of swarm robotics against cyber-attacks and improved consensus reliability, which are critical for practical deployments in complex and potentially adversarial environments.

articleTitle: Improved Medical Image Captioning Using Vision Transformers and Graph Networks
abstract: Image captioning intersects Computer Vision (CV) and Natural Language Processing (NLP), aiming to generate fitting captions for specific images. This area has many applications, from recommendation systems to medical report generation and social media. One challenge within medical report generation is creating captions with detailed information, such as the scan location and the relationships between image objects and clinical findings. Though research exists in this field, there is limited comprehensive coverage of its various challenges. This paper focuses on medical image captioning for chest X-rays. It identifies image concepts separately and generates captions using graph networks and deep learning architectures. This method broadens the potential applications of medical report generation and offers a more intuitive image captioning framework.

articleTitle: Identification of DDoS Attacks Through SHAP-Based Feature Analysis and Transformer Models: A Multivariate Time Series Data Approach
abstract: DDoS attacks are pervasive and lead to significant economic losses because they are cost-effective and rely on readily available resources. This study introduces crucial features identified through SHAP-based analysis to capture the temporal characteristics of DDoS attacks within the Transformer model. The potential for improving online detection and classification of DDoS attacks using reduced features is evident and thoroughly discussed. The simulation results demonstrate that reducing to 20 features with selected input window sizes yields optimal performance, reaching an F1 Score of up to 99.58%. This improvement could greatly enhance real-time defense mechanisms, particularly in identifying attacks promptly when they occur in a streaming fashion.

articleTitle: Optimizing Wheat Ear Head Detection and Yield Estimation Through UAV Based Imagery
abstract: Accurate identification and counting of wheat heads are essential for reliable crop yield estimation. This study introduces a novel model, customized YOLOv8, specifically designed for wheat head detection in challenging agricultural environments using orthomosaic UAV imagery. Our end-to-end pipeline starts with orthomosaic images, identifying and extracting plots using YOLOv8, followed by plot tiling and detection on these tiles. The results are seamlessly stitched to reconstruct the original image with detected wheat heads. To enhance image quality-improving brightness, contrast, exposure, and reducing blur-Real ESR GAN was employed. Coupled with the Random Cut Out Method for occlusion handling, this significantly improved input image quality, facilitating accurate detection under challenging field conditions. Evaluation of the Mahycho dataset demonstrates promising results, with the model achieving a mean average precision (mAP) of 99.2% on plot detection and 83.4% accuracy on wheat head detection, surpassing existing benchmarks. The model exhibits robust performance under adverse conditions, maintaining high R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> values, and retains accuracy across different growth stages in field-collected datasets. Overall, the customized YOLOv8 model offers precise wheat head detection, advancing crop monitoring and management in real-world agricultural applications.

articleTitle: Development of a Solid Waste Identification and Segregation Hub (SWISH) System with CNN
abstract: Improper waste disposal leads to significant environmental challenges, including pollution that adversely affects ecosystems. Effective waste segregation is crucial for sustainability, significantly reducing the amount of waste sent to landfills. This research leverages computer vision technology to develop an automated waste segregator that classifies waste into biodegradable, non-biodegradable, and recyclable categories. Fifteen waste object classes were specified, and model performance was found to be highly dependent on dataset quality and the choice of model. Extensive experimentation using ResNet-50, trained on 8,621 images, yielded optimal results. The final model, enhanced with extended training and data augmentations, achieved a training accuracy of 94.2% and a validation accuracy of 95.9%. Despite challenges with classifying deformable waste items, overall hardware deployment accuracy is 76.67%. This study highlights the potential of machine learning techniques to enhance automated waste segregation and improve waste management efficiency.

articleTitle: CMOS Design Of Reconfigurable Data-Panning Algorithm Based Sorter for 8-Input, 8-Bit Digital Data Using the 0.35um Library
abstract: The aim of the study is to design a CMOS based data-panning algorithm sorter. It aims to design a reconfigurable circuit that allows user to select the number of data to be simulated inside the sorter. The design was able to simulate 8 inputs and be sorted from lowest to highest simultaneously after 8 clock cycles. It has also a minimum hardware component compared to the other data sorter algorithms in terms of multiplexers, data registers, and magnitude comparators. It uses 2*N multiplexers, N*(b+1) data registers, and N/2 magnitude comparators for N represents the number of inputs while B represents the number of bits of the inputs. The CMOS layout occupied an area of 1.35 sq. m., a power consumption of 555 mW and a frequency of 50KHz.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of Hybrid PEMFC/Lithium-Ion Battery Power Systems Using Rule-Based Cycle Charging Algorithm for Telecommunication Base Stations
abstract: Fuel cell/battery systems are increasingly favored for their quiet operation, minimal moving parts, reduced environmental impact, and compact form factor, especially in telecommunication base stations (TBS). However, oversizing or undersizing these power sources can lead to cost inefficiencies or reliability issues. This study presents a sizing methodology for systems using rule-based controls, with the fuel cell operating in three modes: off, maximum efficiency, and maximum power. In the proposed system, the battery maintains the bus voltage, and controller decisions are based on the bus voltage levels. A MATLAB/Simulink model was developed to simulate system performance with different source sizes. The study focuses on a hybrid system with a proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) and a lithium-ion battery. Results show that a small capacity battery is sufficient, and the optimal fuel cell size is one that frequently operates at rated power. Larger fuel cells, while more efficient, do not justify the cost savings. Thus, a fuel cell sized for frequent rated power operation without draining the battery is recommended for optimal performance and cost efficiency in TBS.

articleTitle: Investigation of Environment Dependence in Wi-Fi CSI-Based Crowd Counting Systems
abstract: Crowd counting systems are generally categorized as vision-based and sensor-based, wherein the former requires LOS and may cause privacy concerns, and the latter requires contact and calibration. Recent systems explored the use of radio signals, particularly from Wi-Fi, to perform crowd counting and estimation. Wi-Fi crowd counting systems use channel state information (CSI) as input to the classifier to sense the number of people in the environment. These systems often do not investigate the environment dependence of the data (i.e., the training environment is the same as the testing environment). In this study, we gathered thousands of CSI time samples for 3 crowd count classes (0-person, 3-person, and 5-person) in various indoor environments for several days in the span of 3 months. Due to the high temporal and environmental dynamics caused by the 3-month long data collection, our crowd counting system trained without a prior knowledge of the target environment did not perform as well as the system trained with partial knowledge. By partially training the crowd counting model, we can see a performance boost of around 16–20% in the classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning YOLOv8 for Enhanced Accuracy in Marine Environments
abstract: Marine ecosystems, vital for biodiversity, are threatened by plastic pollution. This study enhances underwater debris detection using YOLOv8, addressing poor image quality issues with contrast-enhanced histogram equalization (CLAHE) and gamma correction. The Adaptive Feature Aggregation (AFA) method improves detection by replacing the traditional YOLOv8 feature extractor. Despite pruning the model, transfer learning ensures high performance. Results show 97.8% detection accuracy, 97.4% mAP@50, and superior GPU speed. This research, adhering to ethical standards and plagiarism checks, aims to protect marine ecosystems using advanced ML and DL techniques.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study on AI Applications for Promoting Equity in Engineering Education
abstract: This study explores how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be used to enhance diversity and inclusion in engineering education. By using AI, schools can find and reduce biases, tailor learning to individual needs, and support students from underrepresented backgrounds. AI can also improve accessibility and help teachers adopt more inclusive methods. We discuss the benefits and challenges of using AI in this context, showing its potential to make engineering education more equitable.

articleTitle: A Novel Two-Phase Social Network-Based Consensus Mechanism: Opinion Dynamics for Large-Scale Group Decision-Making
abstract: The emergence of large-scale group decision-making (LSGDM) has generated significant interest and pre-sented novel issues for decision-makers. This article presents a framework consisting of a two-phase technique that assists decision-makers in large-scale groups in achieving consensus by integrating a social network context and a consensus-reaching approach. Initially, the analysis focuses on the social network of a significant number of decision-makers to examine the impact of social relationships. This network is then utilized to allocate weights to the decision-makers. The suggestion counsel can be developed using social relationships to aggregate group viewpoints into a collective resource. Furthermore, the clustering approach of K-Means, based on Eigen Vector centrality, has been employed to discover distinct subgroups that do not overlap. Additionally, a modified multi-voting technique has been used to facilitate achieving a consensus. We conducted a comparative analysis with other current methodologies, and our results demonstrate superior production compared to the others.

articleTitle: Emission Gating of Sheet Electron Beam for High-Power Gridless Inductive Output Tube
abstract: The gridless inductive output tube (IOT) is a versatile variant of the conventional IOT. It primarily offers high-power operation in the MW-range, and a compact, flexible design. The electron beam is density-modulated at the cathode to achieve bunching with a non-intercepting anode. This paper presents an analysis on the emission gating of a sheet electron beam designed for a high-power gridless IOT. Here, the focusing electrode is utilized for this modulation by applying a potential difference, relative to the cathode. The field intensity required for emission is calculated using a modified Fowler-Norheim equation, which accounts for the transition into the space-charge limited regime, and compensates for the geometric effects of the emission surface. The beam voltage is 80 kV, beam current is 36.5A, and perveance is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.6 \times 10^{-6}\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{V}^{3/2}$</tex>. The beam is confined with a magnetic field of 0.7 T. The compressed beam dimensions are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.54\ \text{mm} \times 37.6\ \text{mm}$</tex>. The simulated current density at the cathode is 20.27 A/ cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a peak electric field of the order of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{6}\mathrm{V}/\mathrm{m}$</tex>. The simulation results show agreement with the Fowler-Nordheim model for the electric field intensity required to operate this beam.

articleTitle: Design of Inset Feed Microstrip Patch Antenna for Wi-Fi Band Application
abstract: Microstrip patch antennas are extensively utilized in diverse electromagnetic applications due to their cost-effectiveness, compact size, straightforward fabrication, and adaptability. This paper presents an effort to design a microstrip patch antenna for Wi-Fi applications, with the objective of creating an efficient and affordable antenna suitable for indoor use. The simulation result shows an S11 of -23.94 dB and a VSWR of 1.135 at 2.488 GHz while at 5.74 GHz has an S11 of -26.551 dB and VSWR of 1.098. The fabricated antenna S11 and VSWR was also measured through a Network Analyzer at 2.452 GHz which has -27.095 dB and 1.518 of S11 and VSWR respectively.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Tracking Using YOLOv8 with Lucas-Kanade Optical Flow for Traffic Light Control Application
abstract: A robust pedestrian tracking system using YOLOv8 for detection and Lucas-Kanade optical flow for motion tracking under varying lighting conditions is developed. Pedestrian tracking is essential for surveillance, robotics, and autonomous vehicles, requiring accurate detection in dynamic environments. A Raspberry Pi camera is employed for real-time processing, and the system's performance is evaluated in artificial and real-world lighting scenarios. Results show a chi-square statistic value - 0.081, significantly lesser than the critical value of 5.991. Results suggests - no significant association exists between the lighting conditions. The results demonstrate effective pedestrian tracking capabilities, highlighting the system's potential to enhance pedestrian safety and traffic management. A significant challenge to be addressed is mitigating human occlusion, which is a primary problem for tracking accuracy in crowded or obstructed environments. Future research should focus on advanced techniques to minimize occlusion effects, ensuring reliable performance across diverse real-world conditions and validating their practical applicability.

articleTitle: LSTM Based Forecasting of Power Consumption
abstract: Power consumption forecasting plays a critical role in effective energy management and resource allocation. However, accurate prediction of power consumption presents unique challenges due to the diverse nature of energy use patterns. This intricate interplay requires the application of advanced forecasting methodologies capable of effectively capturing the temporal dynamics and inherent non-linear relationships embedded within power consumption data across diverse time horizons. In accordance with these findings, this research delves into the complexities of the prediction of energy consumption by proposing a novel approach. We leverage long-short-term memory (LSTM) networks, a type of recurrent neural network (RNN), for long-term energy usage predictions due to their ability to model temporal dependencies. We utilized a polyregression model for short-term forecasting tasks, capitalizing on its effectiveness with smaller, non-cyclical datasets. The results demonstrate the superiority of LSTMs in handling complex relationships within power usage data. In contrast, the polyregression model, while achieving an acceptable R2 of 0.763 for smaller datasets, struggled with limited data points. These findings contribute significantly to the field of power usage forecasting by highlighting the effectiveness of long-Short-Term Memory networks in handling large, featurerich datasets and providing a robust and reliable approach for utilities and energy providers seeking to improve their load forecasting capabilities, leading to more efficient resource management and grid operation.

articleTitle: Towards Regression Model Selection Framework for Stock Price Forecasting
abstract: This paper presents a regression model selection framework based on the metric analysis for stock forecasting. Four machine learning algorithms are selected for demonstration: Multiple Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, K-Nearest Neighbour Regression, and Neural Network Regression, a type of deep learning regression. The mean square error is selected as the measurement metric for the forecasting models. Two stock datasets, Microsoft and Google, are selected for the simulation analysis. The simulation results show that no single method can outperform the others due to the diversity and uncertainty of the patterns of datasets. The framework may be able to recommend the better decision for a particular stock based on the forecasting metric.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of PMaSynRM Using Kriging Surrogate Modeling and NSGA-II Integrated with Taguchi Method
abstract: Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motors (PMaSynRMs) are emerging as viable alternative to PMSMs, particularly in applications where cost and material availability are critical. Rotor geometry and magnet placement pose challenges and can be effectively handled through design optimization for improved motor performance. The process of improving motor performance through FEA simulations using multi-objective optimization is complex and time-consuming. This paper proposes a new motor design approach to improve the performance of a PMaSynRM with minimal computational cost by using Kriging surrogate modeling integrated with the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (NSGA-II). Initially, the critical rotor parameters influencing the performance characteristics of PMaSynRM, such as torque, torque ripple, and saliency, are identified. These parameters are sampled within their bounds using a five-level Taguchi orthogonal array, ensuring a balanced exploration of factor levels. A design of experiments (DOE) is carried out using these samples and the resulting responses are regarded as true responses. A Kriging surrogate model is also created with these samples to predict the responses and its accuracy is validated against the true responses. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed optimization approach, this paper presents the design of a 1.5 kW, 36-slot 6-pole PMaSynRM with a fluid flux barrier rotor. The proposed design approach achieves an improvement in rotor saliency by 2.5 times and torque ripple reduction by 6.3 % compared to one of the recent works.

articleTitle: Remote Blood Pressure Measurement Through Facial PPG Signals
abstract: Blood pressure (BP) is a measure of the force exerted by blood against the walls of arteries as the heart pumps it throughout the body. Today, isolated patients require regular and precise blood pressure measurements. The current sphygmomanometers demand a contact-based measurement setup using cuffs, which increases the risk of infection and skin sensitivity. The dataset comprises videos of 142 participants engaged in three activities. These activities were recorded using an iPhone 11 camera mounted on a tripod, and the videos underwent preprocessing techniques that includes background removal, face detection, selection of region of interest (ROI), and isolation of RGB channels. Motion artifacts removal is done by Richardson Lucy Algorithm - a blind deconvolution method which restores the image with high PSNR, BRISQUE score and edge sharpness. Extraction of ROI by UNET segmentation is done using rectangular shaped mask which has given good predictions with 95.02% accuracy. For non-contact BP measurement, Photoplethysmography (PPG) signals are extracted from each channel of the video. Two parameters, Pulse Transit Time (PTT) and Pulse Amplitude Ratio (PAR), are extracted from each dicrotic notches of PPG signal. Gradient Boosting Machine algorithm estimates both systolic and diastolic pressure with a minimum Root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.09 and an accuracy mean of 99.08%, outperforming the Multiple Linear Regression, Random Forest Classifier and Support Vector Machine algorithms.

articleTitle: Erroneous Reporting in a Multiple Antenna-Based Cognitive Radio Network Using Soft Fusion Scheme
abstract: This paper analyzes the potency of a multiple antenna-based cognitive radio (CR) network, wherein each unlicensed CR user is equipped with multiple antennas. A common receiver detects a licensed primary user's signal using both the soft fusion scheme and a conventional energy detector, considering error-prone reporting channels. Furthermore, for the proposed CR network, we derive expressions for the probability of missed detection and false-alarm. Thereafter, we present the optimal soft fusion problem. Subsequently, we illustrate the theoretical findings of the proposed CR network through numerical results, demonstrating that the CR network with multiple antennas outperforms a single-antenna CR network in terms of decision error probability.

articleTitle: Deep Explainable Ensemble for Medical Image Analysis
abstract: Traditionally, medical images have been analyzed manually. However, this manual analysis can be subjective, depending on the judgment of radiologists and pathologists, which can result in inconsistency and inefficiency. Computer vision and deep learning models have revolutionized the study and diagnosis of medical images such as X-rays, CT scans, and MRIs. Despite their effectiveness, these models often act as black boxes and are difficult to interpret. In this study, we propose an ensemble of two popular deep learning models, ResNet101 and EfficientNetB7, which not only provide higher classification accuracy for CT scans but also offer superior interpretability. Our ensemble model outperforms the original models in COVID-19 CT scan classification by more than 2%. We compared the performance of three eXplainable AI (XAI) visualization models including GradCAM, Guided-GradCAM, and LIME, against the ground truth data labeled by radiologists. The proposed ensemble method provides better interpretability for the CT scan images compared to the individual models.

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Recognition with DNN and Combination of CNN-LSTM
abstract: Emotion is essential to all living things. Understanding emotion is challenging for everyone, but it can solve thousands of problems and save many lives if done correctly. Emotion is represented in gestures, facial expression, speech, etc. Recording of speech is easy with non-invasive nature of processing. As a result, throughout the past three decades, numerous researchers have been interested in emotion recognition through speech. In this study, We address the crucial task of speech emotion recognition (SER) by leveraging deep learning architectures, namely Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) combined with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers and Deep Neural Networks (DNN). our approach utilises a diverse feature set, including Mel spectrogram, MFCCs, spectrogram, delta of MFCCs, chroma feature, and tonal centroid features extracted from the EmoDB dataset. Through extensive exper-imentation employing a 5-fold cross-validation methodology, we achieved notable classification accuracies of 77.38% with the CNN+LSTM model and 87.09% with the DNN model.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Prediction of Indian Criminal Case Outcomes
abstract: Indian courts have too many cases and not enough resources or judges, causing delays and undermining trust in the legal system. In addition, Indian law is quite complex, requiring law students and legal professionals to study and understand it thoroughly for better practice. To address these challenges, we have developed an AI-powered legal assistant designed to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of legal processes. The three main features of our proposed approach are judgment prediction, case summarization, and IPC section and punishment prediction. The judgment prediction uses AI & ML to analyze case facts and give the probability of each party winning. The case summarization compacts the long legal documents into concise texts, highlighting key legal terms and facts. The IPC section and punishment prediction identifies applicable sections of the Indian Penal Code and predicts. These features enhance legal workflows, reduce manual document analysis and improve legal decision-making. Our proposed legal AI system is tested by deploying on Streamlite, which provides interactive interface that can be used on any device with internet access. The performance of the proposed AI model is analysed and the general accuracy of the classification model is obtained as 97%. The performance can be further improved using a more comprehensive and diverse dataset. The consistency and reliability of the model are validated by computing macro- and weighted averages, affirming its robust performance across all IPC categories. In addition, the precision, recall, and F1 score values indicates the accurate identification of winning parties.

articleTitle: Rotten Fruits and Vegetables Detection: A Deep Learning and Transfer Learning Based Approach
abstract: Identifying spoiled food is crucial due to the severe health risks associated with consuming it, such as food poisoning, which can cause symptoms like nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. This condition can lead to dehydration and, in severe cases, require medical intervention and hospitalization. Vulnerable groups such as children, elderly, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals are particularly susceptible. Pathogens in spoiled food can also lead to long-term gastrointestinal issues. Ensuring food freshness not only promotes good health but also prevents discomfort and potential dangers from foodborne illnesses. In our study, various convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning models-including MobileNet, Inception, Xception, DenseNet121, ResNet, EfficientNet, RegNetx, and NASNetLarge-were evaluated for their ability to distinguish between rotten and fresh fruits and vegetables. ResNet achieved the highest accuracy of 0.9930, while CNN models reached a peak accuracy of 0.9835, demonstrating their effectiveness in food quality assessment.

articleTitle: Characteristic Parameters Retrieval of Frequency Selective Surfaces Based on Very Fast Simulated Annealling
abstract: This paper presents a retrieval method for the characteristic parameters of unit cells of Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS) based on Very Fast Simulated Annealing (VFSA). The reflection coefficients is first calculated using Finite Difference Time Domain-based CST electromagnetic simulation software (FDTD-based CST). The characteristic parameters are then reconstructed by iteratively minimizing a cost function that quantifies the difference between numerical simulations and forward model estimations, which are repeatedly updated. Ultimately, the method culminates in the accurate calculation of the characteristic parameters for a FSS unit cell., thereby enhancing the efficiency and precision in the design and analysis of FSS structures.

articleTitle: Innovative Control Strategies for Enhancing Self-Balancing Robots in Dynamic Environments
abstract: The self-balancing robot represents a significant advancement in the realm of mobile robotic platforms. This paper introduces the design of an intelligent embedded system aimed at managing the direction and speed of the stepper motor that drives the self-balancing robot. Controlling the speed and direction of the stepper motor is crucial for maintaining the stability of the two-wheeled robot. Stability is achieved by keeping the robot in an upright walking position. The proposed smart embedded system is engineered to handle sensing, control, and actuation functions.

articleTitle: A 9.94dBm IIP3 Inductorless Differential Low Noise Amplifier for Geofencing Applications
abstract: An inductorless differential Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) with high linearity, designed for geofencing applications, is presented. The LNA incorporates gm-boosting, linearity optimization, and noise-cancelling stages. A complementary derivative superposition technique is used for gm-boosting, while a common-source noise-cancelling path is employed to implement the linearity enhancement stage. The design uses a differential structure for linearity optimization, addressing inherent stability issues associated with the technique. Implemented in 65nm technology, the LNA occupies a chip area of 0.037 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and achieves a noise figure (NF) of 3.03 dB, a peak gain of 16.78 dB, and an IIP3 linearity of 9.94 dBm, with a power consumption of 28 mW. The LNA demonstrates good stability and process variation tolerance.

articleTitle: A Novel CNN Architecture for Herb Classification
abstract: Herbs are an integral part of any traditional medicine. India is rich in medicinal plants which possess the ability to cure many ailments such as cancer, asthma, arthritis etc. Accuracy in recognition of medicinal plants from a wide variety of plants from forest ecosystems is a difficult task. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is one of the deep learning techniques that performs well for many image classification applications. In this paper a CNN architecture has been implemented for herb classification. The proposed CNN consists of four convolutional layers, pooling layers, a fully connected layer and a softmax layer. The ReLU activation function and Adam optimizer improves the performance of proposed CNN with an accuracy of 96.25% with time based decay learning rate.

articleTitle: Low-Power Hamming Distance Detection Circuit Using Cross-Coupled Electronic Neuron
abstract: Pattern-matching efficiency is required to process vast amounts of real-time data in today's rapidly increasing information volume. In previous work, we proposed an associative memory that can perform pattern matching at high speed. However, the Hamming distance detection circuit, a component of the previous study, has a problem with high power consumption due to through-current in the circuit. In this paper, we propose a Hamming distance detection circuit that solves the through-current problem of conventional circuits by using cross-coupled electronic neuron. The power consumption of the proposed circuit is less than 1/6 of that of a conventional Hamming distance detection circuit. The effectiveness of this circuit was verified by HSPICE simulations, which showed the potential for improving the efficiency of associative memory.

articleTitle: Radio-Frequency GaN-on-Si HEMT Technology for Future Communication Applications (Invited)
abstract: GaN-on-Si technology has recently emerged as a viable alternative to GaN-on-SiC technology for future communication applications. This paper highlights the R&D work carried out at the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) to push the performance boundaries of RF GaN-on-Si technologies. An overview of the recently established National GaN Technology Centre (NGTC) and its technologies offerings will also be presented.

articleTitle: Detection of Esophageal Wall via Deep Learning-Based Object Detection with Ultrasound System
abstract: Conventional methods of assessing swallowing function are invasive and burdensome to the patient. Although swallowing function assessment can be performed non-invasively using an ultrasound system, one issue must be overcome: the position of the probe is not fixed. Therefore, deep learning-based object detection was used to detect the esophageal wall so that a more stable and accurate examination can be performed. As a result,. Although the detection rate was high enough and false positive rate was low enough for practical use, we believe that the detection rate can be further increased in the future by learning ultrasound images taken from various angles from a larger number of subjects.

articleTitle: Safety-aware Path Planning Using Metaheuristics
abstract: The proliferation of robotic applications has been notable in recent years, spanning a diverse range of use cases. Ensuring robot safety is crucial for safeguarding both robots and humans, as well as the infrastructure they operate within. Robots navigating indoor environments are particularly susceptible to hazards ranging from minor incidents to severe damage. Therefore, it is essential to consider potential risks and ensure safe navigation while maintaining efficiency. This paper proposes a path-planning method that prioritizes robot safety and path efficiency. Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) is employed in this method to find optimal solutions that balance path distance and the risks faced by robots. Experimental results validate that the proposed approach significantly reduces potential hazards robots may face in various environments during navigation compared to existing methods. Importantly, this risk reduction is achieved without compromising path distance or accessibility.

articleTitle: Can Optical Shading in Solar Concentrator Be Improved with Total Internal Reflection?
abstract: Solar concentrators with multiple stages are typically favored to reduce the overall dimension of the concentrated photovoltaics (CPV) design. However, dual-stage concentrators like Cassegrain concentrators pose an issue with shading losses as the part of the concentrator obscures the aperture. This study highlights the use of the total internal reflection (TIR) phenomenon to allow some light rays to transmit through a reflector by replacing it with a TIR prism. The prism was designed by initially defining the vectors of the intended ray pathway being transmitted through and reflected off. Optimization of the TIR prism was performed with a genetic algorithm to determine the suitable pitch for the prisms and fractal iteration on the lower part of the prism. Results demonstrated a drop in optical efficiency from 62.7% with aluminum reflectors to 49.8% with TIR prism. 0.18% of the optical efficiency is transmitted by the TIR prism, which indicates indifference to aluminum reflectors. Future work has been proposed to include different prism profiles and optimization methods.

articleTitle: Targeted Influence Maximization Using Centrality and Diminishing Weight
abstract: Social Networks are an integral part of our daily life. These networks are tools for sharing information among different users. In such a network, the most influential users become the source for disseminating information over the network. Hence, social network analysis was done to understand and identify the importance of a node in information diffusion. These influential nodes help to achieve maximum influence throughout the network. However, in certain cases, only a subset of nodes are needed to be influenced. This is called targeted influence maximization. In this paper, we use different centrality measures and diminishing weights to identify influential nodes and study the influence of these nodes on the target nodes. Our simulation shows that the seed selection scheme using centrality and diminishing weights activates more target nodes in a network than the existing schemes.

articleTitle: Similarity-Based Label Propagation for Electric Vehicle Network Representation Learning
abstract: The Electric Vehicle (EV) market is rapidly expanding as more individuals shift from traditional fuel-powered vehicles to EVs. This shift requires the broad deployment of Electric Vehicle Supplement Equipment (EVSE), including charging stations, to support the growing EV infrastructure. This paper introduces a semi-supervised learning approach to optimize EVSE charging station deployment. We propose a label-propagation algorithm to consider structural similarities across distant nodes in EVSE points in the electric vehicle charging networks, enabling more accurate similarity extraction. Our results demonstrate that this approach has potential for improving the accuracy and efficiency of EVSE charging station deployment. Our semi-supervised method can be applied to optimize efficient charging station deployment in a simulation for digital twin use.

articleTitle: Quantum Key Distribution Optimization: Reducing Communication Overhead in Post-Processing Steps
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is a ground-breaking method in modern cryptography that uses quantum mechanics to establish secure communication channels. Unlike classical cryptographic techniques, QKD provides unconditional security based on quantum principles, such as the no-cloning theorem and the uncertainty principle. However, existing QKD systems often suffer from high overhead in key post-processing, affecting efficiency and scalability, especially in resource-constrained environments such as IoT. This paper addresses these challenges by introducing two key optimizations to enhance the efficiency and security of QKD systems. First, we propose a method using Pseudorandom Number Generators (PRNGs) to determine key bit positions for verification by Alice and Bob, significantly reducing communication over-head. Second, we employ hash-based subsequence comparison to minimize data exchange and leverage the cryptographic strength of hash functions. Results demonstrate that these strategies effectively reduce key post-processing overhead and improve the efficiency of QKD systems in real-world conditions making QKD more practical and scalable for diverse application contexts.

articleTitle: Identification of Disney Heavy Consumers on Twitter
abstract: Analysis of consumers' identity, behavior, and opinions is possible from a collection of their digital activity data on Twitter (X) and other social media platforms. Feedback from “heavy consumers” is particularly important for companies and directly translates into revenue. However, manually identifying which Twitter users are such customers is time-consuming and costly. In this study, we identified heavy consumers of Tokyo Disney Resorts among Twitter users. We considered various complex characteristics of such heavy consumers: for example, their visitation frequency of the Resorts, the distance between their home and the Resorts, and their purchasing activities of Tokyo Disney products. We collected a total of 100,000 tweets posted by the heavy users of the Tokyo Disney Resorts and developed a BERT (bidirectional encoder representations from transformers) model to test our dataset. Our model scored more than 70% of accuracy in Precision for the text without emoji. Our model scored higher for the text without emoji (70% of accuracy in Precision), indicating that BERT processes pictogram-free text more easily. Thereafter, our model is also more accurate than ChatGPT in analyzing both types of text. As a result, the accuracy of our BERT model was higher than that of ChatGPT.

articleTitle: SpeeDF - A Speech De-Identification Framework
abstract: This paper proposes SpeeDF, a novel three-step framework for anonymizing speech data, particularly focusing on Singaporean English (Singlish). SpeeDF tackles the challenge of protecting less-studied Personally Identifiable Information (PII) like NRIC and passport numbers, which often go overlooked by traditional de-identification methods. Unlike approaches focused solely on entity extraction, SpeeDF leverages a combination of automatic speech recognition (ASR), named entity recognition (NER), and information anonymization. This comprehensive approach ensures thorough PII redaction while preserving the naturalness and usability of the anonymized speech data for research and various downstream applications.

articleTitle: Criteria Setting of Earthfault Relay Coordination for Bhutan Substation Considering the Interconnected Indian Grid Influence
abstract: Earthfault relays (51N) operate based on zero sequence fault current. Since most of the faults that occur on the power system are the earthfault, therefore, coordination of earthfault relays plays a vital role in discriminating the fault. More importantly, the criteria settings must be developed for earthfault relay coordination. Single Line to Ground (SLG) fault current of the system must be known for earthfault relay coordination, however for Bhutan grid, the fault current depends on gigantic Indian grid because of its interconnection. In this paper, short circuit studies pertaining to the SLG fault have been carried out in DIgSILENT to ascertain the SLG fault current. Further, the accuracy of the earthfault relay coordination based on the desired Coordination Time Interval (CTI) for a 132/33/11 kV substation in Bhutan has been validated through DIgSILENT. This paper recommends the earthfault relay coordination methodology and relay setting criteria for those system which is connected to a large grid, like the case of tiny Bhutan and gigantic Indian grid.

articleTitle: RLTQC: Reinforcement Based Tabular Q-Learning for Cowry Game
abstract: The Cowry game is a board game of imperfect information that originated in India. It is a game of chance where the player's pieces move along a specified path based on the roll of special dice, known as Cowry shells. This paper proposes using the Q-learning algorithm, an off-policy reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm, for the Cowry game. We implemented a Q-learning-based Cowry player, which learns to play by engaging in a series of games against opponent players. The results show that our Q-learning-based Cowry player outperforms the opponents with a significant winning margin, assuming the opponents follow either a random strategy or a hind-most strategy.

articleTitle: Adaptive Traffic Light Controller with Reinforcement Learning for Reducing Traffic Congestion
abstract: Reinforcement Learning is a machine learning method that has been adopted in smart traffic lights to reduce traffic congestion effectively. The algorithm is employed as an agent, like a traffic police officer, that can manage traffic jams with the intelligent capability. In this paper, we revisit the basic Q- Learning method applied to adaptive traffic lights by proposing systematic state-action definition, formulating reward policy, and evaluating the performance. The proposed method basically aims to adjust the duration of green lights at each intersection according to the level of congestion at that intersection dynamically, hence, can adapt with traffic condition. Simulation results confirm that the propose method works effectively in managing traffic congestion by maintaining vehicle queue length almost constant at around 40 vehicles queue, offering an improvement from the conventional method that give growth in queue more than 60 vehicles. In the future, we plan to implement the proposed work in an embedded hardware systems to address the real-time performance requirement.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Offshore Vertical-Axis Wind Turbine Farms
abstract: Due to the emergence of reducing the emission of pollutants, renewable energy sources have been increasingly employed worldwide. Vertical axis wind turbines (VAWTs) can provide a significant impact on renewable power generation owing to their advantages over the horizontal axis wind turbines (HAWTs). In this research, the optimal configuration of offshore wind farms consisting of H-type VAWTs is studied. The classical Jensen wake model is used to represent the influence of wake effect to downstream wind speed, which is a strongly nonlinear function of the input wind speed. Moreover, the annual average power generation of a VAWT wind farm is also a strongly nonlinear and nonconvex function of the wind speed, and hence, of the arrangement of VAWTs. As such, the overall optimization problem for maximizing the annual power generation of a VAWT wind farm is a nonlinear and nonconvex programming. To resolve this problem, the genetic algorithm (GA) is utilized. Simulations are then carried out with realistic wind speed data in two years in the Saikai city, Nagasaki prefecture, Japan, whose results show interesting configurations for VAWT wind farms.

articleTitle: A Study of Disaster Notification Wireless Mesh Network Applying Plumtree
abstract: In a huge earthquake, disaster notification system may cease to function due to the damage of communication cables, etc. Therefore, in this study, we assume a wireless mesh network using LPWA that operates independently from existing infrastructures such as the Internet. Disaster notification to first responders must be delivered reliably and with low latency. Flooding is a possible way to obtain redundancy. However, flooding increases the number of messages, and there is concern that increased latency due to time slot control. In this study, we focus on Plumtree that is a fault-tolerant and message-reducing algorithm and consider its application to the disaster notification wireless mesh network. Specifically, we propose a method to enable unicast notification to the first responder node by extending Plumtree. In the proposed method, each node has an additional routing table to keep the direction of the first responder node. Experimental results show that the number of hops in the proposed method is sufficiently small for message loss rates up to 5 %. Even when the loss rate is 50 %, the number of hops is less than approximately two and a half times compared to the shortest path tree.

articleTitle: Filipino Sign Language Recognition Using Wi-Fi Channel State Information
abstract: Sign language recognition (SLR) systems often employ cameras and wearable sensors to detect and interpret signs and gestures. However, vision-based systems rely on LOS and may lead to privacy issues, while wearable systems require calibration and user contact. Alternatively, radio-frequency (RF) sensing, particularly Wi-Fi sensing, may be used for contactless NLOS SLR systems. While there have been some efforts in investigating different sign languages using RF systems, to our knowledge, none have explored the Filipino sign language (FSL) using Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI). In this study, we gathered CSI time series data from different participants performing FSL gestures one at a time using Wi-Fi devices. A total of 600 CSI samples were acquired and preprocessed using outlier removal, denoising and dimension reduction. Our Wi-Fi FSLR systems trained on 80% of the dataset was able to correctly classify up to 83 out of 120 test samples, that is 69.3% accuracy, showing the feasibility of using Wi-Fi CSI for FSLR.

articleTitle: Robust Fetal Head Circumference Calculation on Ultrasound Images Using Just-in-Time Compiled Ellipse Fitting
abstract: Calculation of fetal head circumference (HC) is essential for various purposes, particularly in evaluating fetal health during prenatal care. However, performing HC calculations manually is labor intensive, prone to errors, and requires specific expertise. Thus, there is a pressing demand for automated methods for HC calculation. Recent automation methods for head circumference calculation focus on using deep learning that is often slow and memory hog due to the high computational complexity. This study presents a novel approach for fast and efficient automatic HC calculation from 2D ultrasound images by leveraging just-in-time compiled ellipse fitting based on Randomized Hough Transform. Before ellipse fitting, there are downscaling, blurring, and clean edge detection to increase robustness. After ellipse fitting, there is circumference calculation using the Ramanujan approximation. Our approach achieved a remarkable speed of 0.41 s per image with less than 800 kB of memory. It demonstrated robust accuracy with a Hausdorff distance of 3.88 mm, a Dice score of 0.93, and an absolute difference of 7.24 mm, which is comparable to existing methods.

articleTitle: Audio Fingerprinting Using Clustering
abstract: In the vast landscape of digital audio, the need for robust and efficient methods of identifying and managing audio content has become increasingly imperative. Audio fingerprinting emerges as a powerful solution to this challenge, offering a sophisticated means of uniquely characterizing audio signals for identification and retrieval purposes. Audio fingerprinting is a technique where a unique signature of music file that serves as a compact representation of audio is listened to and stored in an archive. When there is playback of that audio file anywhere, that audio is recognized, and it can be matched against a database that contains all the artist and ownership information for that copyright. The fingerprint feature should be based on perceptual features that are invariant with respect to signal degradation. The applications of audio fingerprinting are diverse and impactful. From music recognition and content matching in streaming services to copyright enforcement and audio-based search engines, technology plays a pivotal role in reshaping how we interact with and manage audio data in the digital era.

articleTitle: A Reinforcement Learning Based Model to Maximize QoS and Revenues of Network Slices in Software Defined Networks
abstract: Software defined networking enables the programmability of network behaviors. The network resource re-quirements of different services vary with respect to the QoS demands. Network slices created by infrastructure providers logically partition the network and encapsulate the resources demanded by the service providers. In general works in the literature are intended either towards maximizing the resource utilization and QoS or towards maximizing the revenue gained by the infrastructure providers. In this work, we have proposed a reinforcement learning based strategy that maximizes the QoS demanded by service providers and also the revenue factor of infrastructure providers.

articleTitle: Detecting and Localizing Electricity Pilferage Using Deep Neural Networks in a Low Voltage Distribution Network with both Smart and Traditional Meters
abstract: Electricity pilferage remains a persistent issue in the Philippines, where certain consumers resort to illegal means of utilizing power. Various studies have been conducted to devise methods for detecting the presence and location of pilferage in residential networks. Commonly used methods for detection are state estimation-based which utilize voltage and current values at grid nodes for estimation. In this study, a set of supervised deep neural networks (DNNs) were modeled and trained to estimate power values to aid in detection and localization of pilferage in a low voltage distribution network which have both smart and traditional meters, and no check meters. Errors between the readings from the meters and estimates from the DNNs were utilized to generate energy error graphs. The visualization of these errors was used to determine the presence of pilferage and possible localization. Three types of pilferage were simulated: meter bypass, diverted load, and direct tapping. It was observed that the power estimations for some houses were inaccurate. Despite this, the energy errors between the estimates and the actual readings were still helpful in the detection and localization of pilferage.

articleTitle: A Novel Architecture for Predictive Maintenance and Realtime Monitoring of Electric Vehicle
abstract: The rapid expansion of the electric vehicle sector presents a transformative opportunity for sustainable transportation, offering reduced emissions and increased energy efficiency. This paper introduces an innovative architecture leveraging the Internet of Things to enhance the maintenance and real-time monitoring of electric vehicles. The proposed system collects data from various sensors within the EV, including battery health, motor performance, and operational metrics. Machine learning models process this data in real-time, predicting maintenance needs before they become critical issues. Cloud integration enables remote monitoring and data accessibility, fostering a collaborative ecosystem. This architecture promises to elevate the reliability, efficiency, and sustainability of the EV industry, harnessing digitization and data-driven insights for cleaner, smarter, and more reliable transportation.

articleTitle: Lightness and Saturation Modification in RGB Color Space for Dichromats
abstract: Dichromatic vision is different from trichromatic vision. It is difficult for dichromats to discriminate specific color combinations. Conventional color conversion methods for dichromats tend to produce unnatural color tone and cause degradation due to over enhancement. In this study, we propose a method which converts an input image into the image to facilitate color discrimination in dichromatic vision without changing impression of the input image for dichromats and trichromats. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed method in comparison with the conventional methods.

articleTitle: NLOS Satellites Detection Method Applying Relative Positioning
abstract: In this paper, we present a detection method for non-line-of-sight (NLOS) satellites applying relative positioning. NLOS satellites affect the accuracy of positioning, and conventional approach to reduce the effect of multipath cannot improve the low accuracy. So, we propose the method to apply relative positioning. This method does not need some special devices or complex computations. In this paper, the observe at the fixed point and open sky condition is carried out to simplify the verification. The NLOS satellite was simulated by modifying the information obtained from the line-of-sight (LOS) satellite, and this method was applied. As a result, the NLOS satellite was successfully detected in approximately 98% of the simulation time.

articleTitle: Self-Learning Robot Manipulator Controller Using Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Traditionally, robot control has relied on mathematical solutions, particularly inverse kinematics (IK), to determine the joint angles needed for a desired end-effector pose. However, these solutions face significant challenges as robots increase in complexity with higher degrees-of-freedom (DoF) and adaptability requirements. This work introduces an approach for controlling robot manipulators by addressing the IK problem using the artificial intelligence (AI) technique. In this paper, a deep reinforcement learning approach is proposed to solve the IK problem for a 6-DoF industrial robot manipulator. The Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm is employed to train an agent capable of learning the robot's motion, allowing for random initial and target positions and orientations. Several reward functions are implemented to enhance the accuracy of the robot's movement towards the desired position and orientation. This proposed approach demonstrates a high success rate and low mean error, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, the approach is validated on a physical robot, confirming its practical applicability and effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Cognitive Approach for Transmit Waveform Generation for Active Phased Array Multifunction Radars
abstract: Multifunction radar utilizes a wide combination of frequencies, pulse lengths, modulations and many other programmable parameters among other factors to cater for different functions of the radar. Conventionally radar waveforms are predefined as per mode of operation. In Cognitive approach, radars pick up waveforms in real time in accordance with the conditions of operation such as to minimize spectral interference or track a target with sufficient resolution or counter jamming etc. The combinations of waveform parameters are adapted cognitively in every dwell or pulse to pulse within a dwell on this basis. This work presents a digital implementation of waveform generation module designed to adapt to the environment in real time and digitally generate the appropriate waveform for transmission in multi-function radars. For a radar to be cognitive it is of umpteen importance that in real time it learns from the environment and utilizes the information to intelligently adjust the transmit waveform parameters. The design presented here leverages data and real-time statistics obtained through feedback from the receiver to transmitter. This feedback mechanism enables intelligent operation in the radar system. Thus, this work is an attempt towards building a module for transmit waveform generation in radars that learns and optimizes design parameters such as resolution, pulse width, bandwidth, and modulation cognitively on the fly. It also incorporates platform motion compensation for radars on moving platform and anti-jamming measures in real time as per operational conditions.

articleTitle: Large Language Models for Video Surveillance Applications
abstract: The rapid increase in video content production has resulted in enormous data volumes, creating significant challenges for efficient analysis and resource management. To address this, robust video analysis tools are essential. This paper presents an innovative proof of concept using Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in the form of Vision Language Models to enhance the downstream video analysis process. Our tool generates customized textual summaries based on user-defined queries, providing focused insights within extensive video datasets. Unlike traditional methods that offer generic summaries or limited action recognition, our approach utilizes Vision Language Models to extract relevant information, improving analysis precision and efficiency. The proposed method produces textual summaries from extensive CCTV footage, which can then be stored for an indefinite time in a very small storage space compared to videos, allowing users to quickly navigate and verify significant events without exhaustive manual review. Qualitative evaluations result in 80% and 70% accuracy in temporal and spatial quality and consistency of the pipeline respectively.

articleTitle: A Dual Band Sawtooth Corrugated Vivaldi Antenna Design for Communication Signal Enhancement and Emergency Applications
abstract: In this paper, a unique dual-band sawtooth cor-rugated Vivaldi antenna (SCVA) for enhancing communication signals and expanding emergency response capabilities is presented. With dual-band operation at 900 MHz (Band 8) and 1800 MHz (Band 3), the antenna provides a broader coverage area. Designing and simulating were done using CST Studio Suite Software. Two antennas were made and manually etched with ferrous chloride on 0.8 mm FR-4 substrate. Voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) and return loss (S11) values were validated by measurements made with a Vector Network Analyzer. Successful operation was demonstrated via integration with a repeater, and drive and speed tests confirmed this. The study's conclusions expand the field of signal-enhancing antenna technology and offer a practical means of improving communication and responding to emergencies.

articleTitle: Discovering the Most Sustainable and Efficient WPT Method for EV Charging
abstract: Wireless Power Transfer technology has emerged as a transformative approach to electric vehicle charging. It offers a convenient and efficient alternative to traditional plug-in methods. It presents the analysis of WPT systems for EV charging and its various principles. This paper provides a detailed examination of how different EV charging technologies contribute to sustainability. Comparing various methods of WPT technologies, it has been found that Inductive Power transfer is highly efficient. It provides a comprehensive overview of how EV charging infrastructure can support sustainable transportation ecosystems by integrating renewable energy sources like solar and wind into charging stations and fostering smart grid integration. It discusses the potential of dynamic charging. It also explores the ways of adopting sustainable mobility.

articleTitle: Knee Joint Health Care Monitoring System Using AI - Classification Approach
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is a significant global health concern, 7% of the global population is affected with osteoarthritis problem. Early diagnosis and regular monitoring of knee joint healthcare is crucial to avoid surgeries. Vibroarthrography (VAG) signal records the vibration or acoustic signal of human knee joint while the movement of leg. VAG signal denoising is done by using Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD). This work investigates the effectiveness of VMD in separating a signal into its intrinsic components, followed by the identification and removal of noise-dominated modes. Signal characteristics have been identified using time-domain features, scalograms and spectrograms from the decomposed modes. Machine learning classifiers are then utilized to categorize these signals. Our results indicate that the ensemble voting classifier and AdaBoost achieved an accuracy of 93% in distinguishing between normal and abnormal VAG signals for knee joint healthcare.

articleTitle: Multi-Template Siamese Networks with Clique Contrastive Learning for Palmprint Authentication
abstract: Palmprint authentication systems are rapidly gaining significant attention as a secure and user-friendly biometric modality, especially suited for mobile applications. These systems leverage palm features that are stable, unique, and easily captured with standard mobile camera technology.
