Several works have developed biometric authentication approaches, leveraging Siamese networks. However, these works show several drawbacks such as using a single ground truth of an individual (also known as a template) and cannot process multiple templates simultaneously. In this paper, we propose a novel Clique Contrastive Learning (CCL) for multi-template Siamese networks, designed to enhance palmprint authentication by effectively utilizing multiple registered templates per individual. CCL adapts the Siamese network architecture to accommodate a clique of templates, applying a specialized loss function that minimizes intra-clique distances while maximizing inter-clique distances. This allows for a more robust authentication process that effectively handles the natural variations in palmprint images. We evaluate our approach using the 11k Hands dataset, focusing on authentication performance under conditions with and without accessories. Our results demonstrate that the multi-template CCL approach consistently outperforms traditional single-template methods, demonstrating the efficacy of our approach in improving the accuracy and reliability of palmprint authentication systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Creaky Nature of Asthmatic Speakers Voice in Sustained Phonation
abstract: Asthma is a reversible, obstructive lower respiratory disease, which is most common across all age groups. As the respiration is the source for speech production if there exist any respiratory complications it gets reflected in the signal produced. The current work explores the distinctive acoustical characteristics of obstructive and restrictive asthma by analyzing sustained phonations at soft, comfortable and loud modes. Analysis reveals periodic fluctuations in fundamental frequency, which are quantified through vibrato, and significant fundamental frequency lowering with multi-pulsing that characterizes a creaky voice in asthmatic speech across all severity and phonation modes. Furthermore, a shift in the frequency of high energy spectral component and fluctuations in formants are also observed in asthmatic speech.

articleTitle: Development of a Vision-Based Smart Security System for Vehicle Entry Monitoring in a Subdivision
abstract: Gated subdivisions and villages enhance community security through monitored access points in the Philippines. This study focuses on developing a robust electronic system for vehicle entry monitoring, leveraging machine vision and data analysis. The primary objective is to create an advanced security system that uses cameras to monitor and identify vehicles via their license plates. The system ensures accurate logging and classification of vehicles by integrating Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) technology with an SQL database. Implemented in Sta. Cecilia Village in Las <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Pinas}$</tex> City, the system achieved a high accuracy rate of 96.83% in vehicle detection and classification. This approach improves security by efficiently tracking vehicle entries and providing valuable traffic analysis data. The results demonstrate the system's potential to enhance community safety and operational efficiency, making it a promising solution for modern urban management.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Network Density Based Centrality for Influential Node Detection in Complex Networks
abstract: Comprehending the dynamics of disease or information diffusion requires influential node detection in complex networks. Numerous centrality measures were developed for calculating the spreading capacity of a node. However, they fail to produce a high monotonic ranking of spreaders, which is a highly desired property. Two new measures, local density and extended local density are introduced in this paper to calculate the spreading impact of every node using the density of edges in the neighborhood of the node and the node degree. Our experimental results demonstrate that both of our proposed metrics offer a more consistent monotonic result for node ranking and better rank distribution than other centrality measures.

articleTitle: Development of Microplastics Detector and Quantifier Utilizing Deep Learning Based Algorithm
abstract: Microplastics are tiny plastic particles with a size smaller than 5mm. These are considered ubiquitous environmental contaminants as they pollute shorelines and bodies of water globally. Also, there are potentially hazardous effects of alternate ingestion to humans and marine life. In alignment with SDG 14: Life Below Water, the researchers consider the Barangay Binuangan to correspond best in this endeavor. Binuangan is a barangay in the Philippine province of Bulacan's coastal municipality of Obando. The proposed solution is to create a prototype that utilizes a deep-learning-based algorithm that detects and quantifies microplastics. The system uses a deep-learning model; You Only Look Once version 4 (YOLOv4). The researchers used a manta trawl to obtain the residue for specific project design requirements, which is crucial as it leverages the accuracy percentage in detecting the microplastics. The target average precision (AP) and mean average precision (mAP) are greater than 85% and 65%, respectively. Using YOLOv4 achieved an AP for microplastics class of 92.25% and mAP of 70.52%, a 7.83% and 6.21 % increase to AP and mAP, respectively than that of using YOLOv4-tiny on a real-time detection using a microscopic camera.

articleTitle: Sustainable Wireless Charging Solutions: Design and Testing of a Portable Solar-Powered Charging Device
abstract: This paper details the creation of a portable wireless charging device powered by a solar panel and equipped with an advanced charging algorithm. The device includes a 6500mAh Li-ion battery (using 18650 cells) and is designed to charge electronic gadgets efficiently and sustainably such as smartphones and laptops. It consists of a solar panel, charging circuit, Li-ion batteries, a microcontroller, and wireless charging circuits. Tests have shown that it delivers a stable and reliable output of 5V/2A while maintaining high power transfer efficiency. The advanced charging algorithm fine-tunes the charging current and voltage according to the specific requirements of the device being charged, optimizing power transfer efficiency and reducing charging time. This device offers a sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional charging methods, especially useful in regions with limited access to power sources.

articleTitle: WSe2: ZnO Nanocomposite Based UV Photodetector with PMMA (HTL) and PCBM (ETL)
abstract: This letter reports a Al/PCBM/WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>: ZnO/PMMA/ ITO coated PET structure based UV photodetector. The fabricated device consist of WSe2: ZnO nanocomposite (NC) as an active layer whereas PMMA as a HTL (hole transport layer) and PCBM as a ETL (electron transport layer). All the sols were prepared by the dispersion method and the films were deposited through spin coating technique. The Al contacts were deposited over PCBM acting as ETL by means of thermal evaporation unit. The proposed photodetector exhibits UV detection with maximum responsivity Rs(A/W) of 1579 AIW, 576AIW, and 127 AIW; at 300nm, 350nm and 400nm at 0.5V bias. The nanocomposite, HTL and ETL, shows the promising characteristics for optoelectronic application.

articleTitle: Optimal Harmonic Estimation in Renewable Integrated Power System Using Grasshopper Optimisation Algorithm and Recursive Least Square Approach
abstract: Harmonic estimation in renewable integrated power systems is crucial for maintaining power quality and ensuring the reliability of the grid. This paper presents an innovative approach for optimal harmonic estimation by combining the Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (GOA) with the Recursive Least Square (RLS) method. RLS is used for estimation of amplitude of harmonics, whereas phase is estimated by GOA. The performance of GOA-RLS is investigated in detail for estimation of power system signals using test signals buried with noise. The integration of GOA, a nature-inspired optimization technique, with RLS, a statistical method, provides a robust framework for accurately identifying harmonics in power systems. The proposed method is tested on a simulated renewable integrated power system, demonstrating superior performance in terms of accuracy, convergence speed. The results highlight the potential of this hybrid approach in enhancing the operational efficiency and stability of modern power grids with high penetration of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Identifying Suitable Anatomical Planes in 3D MRI for AD Classification by Employing ViT Pipeline
abstract: This work aims to identify the suitable anatomical planes in 3D MRI for discriminating different types of Alzheimer's disease (AD) - cognitively normal (CN), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and final stage Alzheimer's (AD). Such classification tasks in deep learning (DL) framework displayed noticeable results. Existing works consider global feature selection-based techniques in convolutional neural networks (CNN) and most of them consider all 3D images as input, which creates insignificant use of data that may not be suitable. Therefore, this work aims to identify suitable images from different anatomical planes of 3D MRI and emphasize on local-level features by involving the self-attention mechanism in Vision Transformer (ViT). For validation, MRI data from benchmark ADNI database has been taken into account. Aiming to find suitable MRI scans, 10–12 slices from each of three different anatomical planes - axial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{x}})$</tex>, coronal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}})$</tex>, and sagittal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{g}})$</tex> are segregated. Further, the images are fed into ViT by framing three cases (a) individual planes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{x}}, \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}},\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{g}}, (\mathrm{b})$</tex> planes in pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\mathbf{A}_{x_{-}} \mathbf{C}_{\mathbf{r}}\right),\left(\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{x}_{-}} \mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{g}}\right)$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}_{-}}\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{g}})$</tex> and (c) all planes together <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{x}_{-}} \mathbf{C}_{\mathrm{r}_{-}} \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{g}}\right)$</tex>. The analysis has been performed by measuring accuracy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(A_{c})$</tex>, sensitivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S_{e})$</tex>, specificity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S_{p})$</tex>, and Fl-score for a different set of inputs; while CNN model as a baseline. The results show that the ViT outperforms the CNN model, while the input pair <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{x}-}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{I}}$</tex> achieved accuracy as high as 93.3%. Thus, the analysis shows that choosing pair of planes could be suitable for MRI-based AD while involving DL-based techniques.

articleTitle: Compact and Lightweight Cable Attitude Measurement Device for Aerial Transportation Applications
abstract: Small-scale Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) such as quadrotors and helicopters are popular nowadays in various applications like surveillance, aerial photography, air logistics, mapping, etc. In some applications, it is required to transport the payload by suspending it using cable or rope. Cable suspension of the payload provides the advantage of picking and placing the payload from a certain height. However, while transporting such cable-suspended payload, the payload is likely to oscillate. Sometimes its oscillations become severe and destabilize the UAVs, leading to an accident. To stabilize the oscillations of the payload, the control architecture of the UAVs has to be modified. Most of the recently developed control architectures require real-time feedback of the payload oscillations in terms of the cable's angular position. In this regard, we designed a Cable Attitude Measurement device to measure the cable attitude in this letter. The device's design is compact and capable of measuring cable attitude in real-time at 740 Hz by establishing communication between UAVs onboard autopilot. Indoor experiments using a motion capture system are carried out to validate the CAM device and identify its accuracy.

articleTitle: RuralCasting -A Non-Internet Based Distribution System for Digital Resources in the Philippines
abstract: The RuralCasting project is a non-internet-based system for distributing digital resources to communities in the Philippines that have difficulty in accessing the internet. Providing Philippine schools and communities digital resources for learning and general information e.g., disaster related information, livelihood resources, health, etc. To maximize the user's smart devices, the users need only connect to the local Wi-Fi network using their Wi-Fi devices. The RuralCasting system utilized datacasting in the digital TV standard (ISDB- T) to receive over-the-air updates through digital TV broadcasts. The system developed comprises of the user-end device or the RuralCasting Box, the ISDB- T module for receiving digital TV transmissions, its own Wi-Fi LAN to accommodate multiple users simultaneously, the transmission/reception setup for testing, an offline usage measurement tool, and the landing page (RuralCasting Portal) hosting digital content from verified partners. The system tested can accommodate up to 12 users connected when connected to the Wi-Fi network. Tested to receive a 6 MB over-the-air patch using a digital TV broadcast test setup. And a successful full loop test has been done with partnered schools to determine the possible implementation framework for the RuralCasting box.

articleTitle: Study on Variable Tee and Bridge Tee Attenuators to Enhance IQ Mixer Sideband Suppression in Synthetic Aperture Radar Applications
abstract: The IQ mixer is a vital component in developing a synthetic aperture radar system. It needs to maintain its reliable performance, including the ability to suppress un-wanted sidebands in a single sideband modulation process. The sideband suppression performance of the IQ mixer depends on the imbalance of the signal power that meets at the output port. The adjustment of the input power of base chirp signals is required and can be performed by taking advantage of a variable attenuator. A variable attenuator offers practical and efficient use at wide frequencies to reduce the power signal and make two signals equal. This research study focused on variable tee and bridge tee attenuators to enhance IQ mixer sideband suppression in synthetic aperture radar applications. The simulation results show that the tee attenuator offers a high-resolution attenuation at a dynamic range of 1.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{dB}$</tex>. It also has a wide range flat response (up to 6 GHz) compared to the bridge tee attenuator.

articleTitle: A Novel Select Method Based on the Sparseness as Acquiring Appropriate Data for the Data Interpolation of Accelerated Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
abstract: Accelerated nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (A-NMRS) is one of a molecular analysis method which requires an interpolation process to a measurement data. In general, the condition for the data acquisition has been determined beforehand. However, with the principle of A-NMRS, the condition can be changed both before and during the data acquisition. This study proposes a method to improve interpolation performance by adjusting the data acquisition condition through real-time data analysis. Based on the conventional knowledge, the interpolation method for A-NMRS was based on a sparse optimization. The current study has proposed a method to identify the conditions that allow us to measure the data with the lowest sparseness. To demonstrate an advantage of the proposed method, this paper experiments to compare the interpolation performance of the conventional methodology and the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Domain Isolation Algorithm Using Mininet-WIFI
abstract: Today's digital world is influential in every aspect, making people want to change things to be more practical. There is a high demand for using WiFi technology in every sector. The highest impact on network infrastructure planning was developed by the Software-Defined Network (SDN) to address all the complex problems and connectivity needs of the future. The connectivity needed in the future is something new that can be developed so that the network can better adapt to dynamic conditions and increase flexibility. Thus, the support of WiFi technology on SDN networks became a dream, and this paper aims to implement a domain isolation algorithm (DI) to be applied to WiFi networks on the SDN. The algorithm allows for the acquisition and transmission of packets between end devices using the network's shortest and least congested pathways. Furthermore, we assessed the effectiveness of the employed algorithm by evaluating their performance based on different quality of service (QoS) metrics, utilizing the iPerf tool. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system achieved favorable outcomes in quality of service (QoS) metrics.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of the Thermal Properties of Beeswax Based Phase Change Materials for Thermal Energy Storage Applications in Comparison to Paraffin: Highlights: Exploration of the Application of Beeswax as a Sustainable Substitute for Paraffin wax in Thermal Energy Storage. Comparison of Heat Flux and Temperature Rise of Beeswax and Paraffin Better Temperature Control with the Beeswax was Noticed in PCM. Heat Flux for Parafin Wax and Beewax Based PCMs are Almost Same.
abstract: Due to the high energy demand in society, energy storage and management have become major areas of research in recent days. Commonly used for heat storage, paraffin, a petroleum-derived phase change material (PCM), raises sustainability concerns. This paper investigates the possibility of using beeswax (BW) as a bio-based, sustainable alternative to paraffin wax for thermal energy storage applications by comparing beeswax's heat flux and temperature rise profiles with those of paraffin to assess its suitability for various heat storage system designs. The results showed the potential of beeswax as a viable replacement for paraffin wax. Better heat storage capacity and thermal control of beeswax were noticed with almost equal heat flux.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence to Expedite Thermal Index Testing and Accelerate Polymer Regulatory Approvals
abstract: With the increasing focus on sustainability, industries are rapidly adopting technologies such as 3D printing and making significant investments to achieve their environmental goals. This technological shift is driving a surge in the development of new polymers, including the revival of materials like aliphatic polyketone and the creation of innovative resins such as polyacrylates. These new materials, targeting at specific properties like flame retardancy and heat stabilization, require rigorous regulatory approval to be used in applications with strict safety standards, especially in electrical connectors and components. Validating short-term properties of these resins is relatively quick and straightforward. However, assessing their long-term thermal stability, particularly through tests like UL's Relative Thermal Index (RTI), is a complex and time-consuming process, often taking months. This lengthy testing period poses a significant challenge for new resins entering the market, due to the high time and cost involved. The advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) offers a transformative solution to this problem. This paper explores how AI can be utilized to predict long-term thermal performance accurately, effectively reducing the duration of RTI testing by up to 50% without compromising on reliability. More specifically, An AI-based methodology is proposed to estimate the RTI temperature by incorporating the physics of thermal degradation, where data from shorter testing periods at higher temperatures is used to predict the results of longer testing durations at lower temperatures. Through this innovative approach, AI enables faster regulatory approvals, allowing new polymer developments to reach the market more quickly and efficiently, keeping pace with the dynamic advancements in the field.

articleTitle: Teaching AI and Data Analytics to Electrical Engineering Students
abstract: Artificial intelligence and data analytics began to dominate all aspects of technology. Electrical Engineering graduates entering the workforce will likely rely on AI tools and systems to manage their engineering tasks, or they may be required to integrate AI features into the products and services they develop. Traditionally, these subjects were part of computer engineering curriculum rather than electrical engineering. Considering the recent advances made in AI and machine learning, and their widespread application in various fields, integrating these subjects into electrical engineering curriculum would be beneficial to engineering graduates. Nevertheless, it is a challenging task. A major challenge is to make the subject relevant to the body of electrical engineering knowledge. Another obstacle to overcome is students' shortcoming in computing knowledge and programming skills. In this paper, we present our initiatives to integrate AI, machine learning and data analytics concepts into electrical engineering curriculum and report our key findings and challenges encountered.

articleTitle: ScamDetector: Leveraging Fine-Tuned Language Models for Improved Fraudulent Call Detection
abstract: This paper introduces a fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) for detecting scam calls, a response to the growing severity of telecommunication fraud in Singapore, which has seen a consistent increase in scam incidents over recent years. Our approach significantly enhances scam detection capabilities through the strategic augmentation of existing datasets with generative AI. This process involves consolidating multiple datasets and employing generative models to synthesize culturally relevant scam scenarios specific to the Singapore context. We use the augmented dataset to fine tune pretrained LLMs, including GPT-2 and Llama. We conducted extensive experiments to compare the effectiveness of traditional machine learning (ML) models, deep learning (DL) techniques, transformers, and our fine-tuned LLMs. The results clearly show that our fine-tuned LLM outperforms other models in terms of inference accuracy while maintaining acceptable inference times, thereby establishing itself as a practical tool for real-time scam detection. The source code of this work is made publicly accessible at https://github.com/ict-at-sit/ScamDetector.

articleTitle: Teleoperation System Design for a Mobile Robot Using BeagleBone Black Board
abstract: This paper proposes the implementation of the teleoperation system for a mobile robot using the BeagleBlack board. The Omnidirectional Mobile Robot represents the master robot, including the copy robot stationed at two distant locations. Both copy robots replicate the pose of the master robots controlled with a human hand. The teleoperation system uses position feedback control and real-time monitoring system powered by the virtual instrumentation and control program, namely Lab View. The communication system is established by the Local Area Network. Three controllers PI, PD, and PID are employed in the teleoperation system to evaluate stability and effectiveness. All three experimental results verify that the teleoperation system designed can be operated and achieved on the Beagle Black Board as well.

articleTitle: GAN-Based Tone Curve Learning Approach to HDR Image Reconstruction Method Using Single LDR Image
abstract: In recent years, the use of HDR images is becoming more widespread. In this study, we discuss a method for converting an already taken LDR image into an HDR image. HDR generating methods based on the deep learning have been well studied in recent years. However, these methods have problems such as adding non-existent information on the image. In this paper, using single LDR image and a few reference LDR images, we propose a new HDR generation method based on a GAN to calculate the tone curves. The advantage of the proposed method is that there are no restrictions on the size or scene of the input and reference images, and they can differ. Numerical experiments show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Evaluating Blockchain Platforms Using an Integrated Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Approach: AHP and TOPSIS Methods
abstract: Blockchain technology is gaining immense popularity in the past few years, and is extensively applied in various domains. The diversity of commercial blockchain platforms and their unique features poses a challenge in selecting optimal platform for meeting requirements of an organization. For successful implementation of block chain based application, selection of appropriate blockchain platform is very crucial. The present study proposes a methodology to select the best blockchain platform using a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) approach. An Integrated approach of Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and TOPSIS method is adopted for ranking of blockchain platforms. Five blockchain platforms were evaluated on the basis of seven criteria namely: transaction fees, security, transaction speed, interoperability, scalability, energy requirements, and smart contracts as use case. The utility of the proposed approach has been established through an illustrative example for ranking blockchain platforms. The results demonstrate how and integration of AHP and TOPSIS methods can effectively prioritize Blockchain platforms based on specified criteria while reducing inconsistencies, ensuring the best possible decision in blockchain platform selection.

articleTitle: State Estimation of Nonlinear Oscillatory Chaotic System: Application to Aircraft Wing Rock Using Cubature Particle Filtering
abstract: The aircraft wing rock system is chaotic and highly oscillatory in nature. This work formulates the oscillatory chaotic dynamics of the wing rock system and integrates it with a noisy measurement model. Subsequently, we introduce a cubature rule-based particle filter (CPF) to track the roll angle and roll velocity (system internal states). The CPF uses the third-degree spherical-radial rule for integral approximation. The desired state estimation information may be used to design a state-based control scheme to regulate the motion of the wing rock. The simulation results showcase the performance of the proposed method in the presence of uncertainties.

articleTitle: Integrating RAG with Face Recognition for Personalized Guest Services for Hospitality Industries
abstract: The hospitality industry has increasingly adopted advanced technologies to enhance guest experiences, yet many guests remain dissatisfied with on-site services despite effective pre-stay recommendation systems. Our proposed AIReceiptionist system integrates Face Recognition (FR) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) modules to provide personalized and efficient guest services. The FR module identifies guests as they enter the public lobby, and the RAG module retrieves detailed guest information from the relevant database, generating prompts to notify staff. We present the system implementation of our AIReceiptionist by leveraging existing deep learning tools, including MTCNN for face detection and InceptionResnetV1 for face recognition, combined with OpenAIEmbeddings for data embedding and GPT-4o for language model responses. Using synthetic data tailored to hospitality operations, we validated AIReceiptionist's performance and compared it with the existing GPT-4o model. The chatbot responses show that our AIReceiptionist enhanced by FR-RAG module significantly outperformed the generic GPT-4o in delivering personalized guest services, demonstrating its feasibility in enhancing guest satisfaction in hospitality environments.

articleTitle: Practical Mobile Based Services for Identification of Chicken Diseases from Fecal Images
abstract: Poultry farming is a vital component in a food chain. Health of chickens in the farms directly plays an important role in both quality and safety of all chicken products. Accurate diagnosis of poultry diseases from chicken feces using standardized polymerase chain reaction is relatively very expensive, making it rather challenging especially for small local farms. To tackle this, we developed a practical mobile-based service that aimed to provide local farmers an easy-to-use tool capable of preliminary identification of common diseases chickens may have from their fecal images. Our system was deployed as an official Line account on a familiar Line application that most farmers have on their mobile phones. Trained and evaluated on a large open database of chicken fecal images, it achieved a segmentation mean average precision of 86.49 % and classification accuracy of 95.93 %. Ours also, with high confidence, correctly identify healthy images taken by local farmers.

articleTitle: Cooperative Localisation System Using Ultra-Wide Band and GPS
abstract: This paper presents a Cooperative Localization System (CLS) that integrates Ultra-Wideband (UWB) and Global Positioning System (GPS) technologies to elevate positioning accuracy. By capitalizing on UWB's precision and GPS's extensive coverage, the CLS excels in both indoor and urban settings. Employing a cooperative framework, UWB-equipped nodes collaborate by sharing ranging information to refine GPS-based position estimates. Experimental evaluations underscore substantial improvements in accuracy compared to standalone GPS and UWB systems. The CLS not only delivers enhanced accuracy but also offers scalability and reliability, rendering it well-suited for diverse applications such as asset tracking and group monitoring. This integration of UWB and GPS technologies in the CLS framework represents a significant advancement in localization systems, with wide-ranging implications for various fields requiring precise and dependable positioning solutions.

articleTitle: HAR-CLET: A Novel Conv-LSTM with Extra Tree Classifier for Human Activity Recognition
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel ensemble of Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory with an Extra Tree Classifier for automatic feature engineering in the spatiotemporal domain and classification of different human activities collected using inbuilt smartphone sensors. Prominent sensor-based HAR systems are trained and validated in extracted features of datasets collected in a controlled and simulated environment, which can adversely impact the reliability in real-world scenarios. Our approach utilizes unsimulated data from diverse users collected using inbuilt smartphone sensors in real world environment. Also, the proposed model was effectively trained and tested with multiple standard public datasets for validation and benchmarking with diverse evaluation metrics. With effective parameter tuning and lightweight feature extraction architecture, the proposed model achieved an average performance accuracy of 99 % with their own generated dataset, mHealth and MotionSense dataset, in comparatively optimized computational time compared to the benchmark models.

articleTitle: Advancements in Efficient and Sustainable Wireless Charging for Electric Vehicles
abstract: The transition to Electric Vehicles (EVs) is crucial for sustainable transportation. However, the adoption of traditional plug-in charging systems remains limited due to their time-consuming nature and infrastructure demands. This study presents a Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system leveraging inductive coupling to enhance EV charging efficiency, compatibility, and safety. The system converts AC to DC with power factor correction, then transforms it into high-frequency AC to energize the transmitter coil. The receiver coil generates alternating current (AC), which then converts to direct current (DC) for charging the battery. The proposed WPT model, developed using MATLAB Simulink Optimizer, demonstrates a charging efficiency ranging from 90 % to 93 %, resulting in energy losses as low as 10 % to 15 % and improved user convenience by reducing the need for manual plug-in operations. The developed model assumes a standard 60 kWh EV battery can be charged from 20 % to 80 % in approximately 3 hours using the proposed WPT system, compared to 5–6 hours with conventional plug-in chargers.

articleTitle: Mitigating NLOS Error in Urban and Suburban Environment Using Enhanced CSA-PSO Algorithm
abstract: Non-Line Of Sight (NLOS) propagation introduces errors to the time-of-arrival (TOA) measurements and degrades the localization accuracy. This paper focuses on mitigating NLOS errors and improving the localization accuracy of a TOA localization system where the unknown position of a Mobile Station (MS) is estimated based on the known positions of several Base Stations (BS). We formulate the problem into a Maximum Likelihood (ML) framework and propose an enhanced Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm where the Crow Search Algorithm (CSA) is employed to guide the initial population generation for PSO. Simulation results show that our proposed method achieves higher localization accuracy in urban and suburban environments with different NLOS conditions than the state-of-the-arts (SOTA) PSO-based method.

articleTitle: Dual-Path CCM Boost Converter Optimization for Indoor Light Energy Harvesting in Biomedical Devices
abstract: This study presents the design of a Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM) Boost Converter with a dual-path circuit configuration that integrates a supercapacitor for electrocardiogram (ECG) devices, using 65nm CMOS technology. The boost converter effectively increases the battery-powered input voltage from the solar source, ranging from 0.15 V-0.4 V to a stable output of 0.7 V, ensuring reliable power delivery to ECG devices. Key performance metrics include a peak efficiency of 84.85% with ideal components and 69.54% with non-ideal components. The dual-path architecture enhances efficiency, achieving 83.40 % when switching from primary to secondary paths and maintaining 84.33 % during secondary path operation. The system demonstrates significant improvements in line regulation, from 2.195m V/m V of the traditional approach to 0.000014 mV/mV with the dual-path and load regulation improvement from 1.4562mV/mA to 0.019713 mV/mA, coupled with reduced voltage ripple (<1 %), minimizing the output voltage surge. The designed boost converter has a total chip area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.61mm^{2}$</tex>, supplying a load current of 1.14 mA and an output power load of 801.90 μW, sufficient to power electrocardiograms.

articleTitle: Cyber Threat Analysis Through Densified Causal Knowledge Graph
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework to construct a dense, informative causal knowledge graph from a massive corpora of news articles leveraging both state-of-the-art transformers and traditional machine learning methods such as clustering. The proposed framework, specifically designed for modeling cause effect relationship through a graph-based data structure, consists of three steps, namely, i) cause-effect (CE) relation extraction, ii) argument clustering, and, iii) construction of causal knowledge graph (CKG). We thereafter perform experiments with 22,342 news articles crawled from the Internet with predetermined key words suggested from a centralized cyber security division within Panasonic Holdings. We demonstrate that the clustering-based strategy results in a dense CKG that conveys domain specific insightful information to the business user that would help in long and short term strategic and operational decision making. Finally, we design a metric to evaluate the performance of the CKG based on entropy motivated by information theory. We discuss the results and provide some future direction of research in this area.

articleTitle: Object Recognition and Tracking using Multiple LiDARs
abstract: This paper presents an object recognition and tracking method using multiple light detection and ranging sensors (LiDARs) set in an environment. Each LiDAR recognizes objects, such as cars, two-wheelers, and people, using CenterPoint, which is an end-to-end method for three-dimensional object recognition. Information about recognized objects (the position, size, heading, and the confidence score of the objects) is sent to a central server and fused using nonmaximum weighted method. The fused objects are tracked using an interacting multimodel estimator, and their poses and behavior are estimated. Simulation experiments using three LiDARs placed in an intersection environment validate the performance of the presented method.

articleTitle: Walkable Southeast Asia: A Comparative Study Between Phnom Penh and Ho Chi Minh City
abstract: This study presents a data-driven approach to compute walkability indicators from open-data sources. We compare Phnom Penh and Ho Chi Minh City, two Southeast Asian cities that share cultural, historical, and economic similarities. We inspect street network connectivity, population density, building density, facilities density, and elevation range. Overall, the findings suggest that Phnom Penh exhibits higher walkability due to its greater network density, population density, and facility density, fostering greater city-wide connectivity. In contrast, Ho Chi Minh City, a key economic hub in Vietnam, shows lower walkability metrics, possibly influenced by higher urban development and income levels. Wealthier residents may prefer vehicular transportation, supported by the city's robust GDP-driven infrastructure.

articleTitle: Quantum inspired genetic algorithm and optimization of queuing delay
abstract: Queuing delay is the waiting time for the packets in the queue before processing. It significantly impacts the network compared to processing, and transmission delays. The delay occurs when a packet suddenly arrives faster than the processing of packets at different time. Minimum queuing delay is required to have better network control and high efficiency. In this paper, we proposed the quantum inspired genetic algorithm to obtain the minimum queuing delay and maximum arrival rate in a network. A quantum inspired crossover and mutation technique is designed. It provides an optimal point between maximum average arrival rate with minimum average queuing delay. The performance and convergence of the proposed algorithm are evaluated. The inspired algorithm can help to solve other optimization problems as well.

articleTitle: Joint Angle and Rang Estimation with Low-Cost Ris-Assisted FDA Direction Finding System
abstract: This article explores the integration of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) with Frequency Diversity Array (FDA) radars to advance sixth-generation (6G) communication technologies. The study specifically addresses the challenge of low-cost RIS-assisted FDA radar localization. To solve the joint angle-range estimation problem, we employ the Atomic Norm Minimization (ANM) approach. Traditional semidefinite programming (SDP) methods, often used for this purpose, suffer from high complexity and dependence on interior point methods. To improve efficiency, we propose an iterative solution based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). Our simulation results demonstrate that this ADMM-based method not only enhances parameter estimation accuracy but also maintains low computational complexity, outperforming existing algorithms. This research marks a significant step forward in radar localization technology, effectively combining RIS with FDA radars and introducing a novel, efficient method for precise signal processing.

articleTitle: Validating Pseudo-label Dataset for Japanese Hate Speech Detection
abstract: Currently, labeled datasets for hate speech detection in Japanese are insufficient. Therefore, we show that it is possible to construct a high-performance model using a pseudo-labeled dataset. This method can reduce the cost and time required to create a labeled dataset for Japanese hate speech detection. In the validation, we compared the performance when trained on a human-labeled dataset and a pseudo-labeled dataset. As a result, the F1 score of the human-labeled dataset was 0.5443, while that of the pseudo-labeled dataset with LLM was 0.5073. Thus, this method can be used to construct a high-performance hate speech detection model without human labeling.

articleTitle: Detection and Tracking of Nile Tilapia Using DeepLabCut with ResNet50 and MobileNetV2
abstract: Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) is vital for aquaculture due to its rapid growth and high productivity. This study tackles detection and tracking concerns using machine vision techniques, developing an automated system with DeepLabCut™ and training classifiers with ResNet50 and MobileNet V2-1.0. MobileNet V2 showed balanced performance, with lower training (634.5 pixels) and test errors (723.7 pixels), and a higher mean likelihood (0.60) for the body region. ResNet50, despite efficient learning, suffered from overfitting, with training and test errors of 1121.2 and 1083.3 pixels, and low mean likelihood (0.1) for all body parts. These results indicate MobileNet V2 is better for reliable, resource-efficient predictions, while ResNet50 could improve with better data quality and annotations. Future research should focus on enhancing data quality, extended training, and advanced regularization techniques.

articleTitle: Failure Mode Classification of Wind Turbine Gearbox Utilizing Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: There has been a substantial expansion in the use of renewable resources, such as wind energy. Wind energy is converted into electricity, which is situated outside, rendering them vulnerable to inclement weather situations. These situations can result in various forms of harm to wind turbines, reducing their lifespan and efficiency and subsequently increasing their operational expenses. Hence, monitoring conditions and identifying problems early are of utmost importance. By employing machine learning techniques, it is possible to proactively avoid the deterioration of wind turbine components and identify and diagnose malfunctions. This method enables the automated and self-directed knowledge acquisition to forecast, identify, and analyze mechanical malfunctions in wind turbines. The study simulated three distinct failure scenarios in wind turbines and compared the performance of various AI methodologies, including Extra tree, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Neural Networks, and SVM. This work assesses various approaches for statistical feature extraction, such as standard deviation, mean, kurtosis, and skewness. Implementing these strategies makes it possible to predict and classify equipment failure types. Significant outcomes are achieved with a precision of 96.6%.

articleTitle: Enhanced Instrument Identification Using CNNs: A Comparative Study with Random Forest Models
abstract: This study explores the effectiveness of instrument identification algorithms (IIAs) using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Random Forest (RF) models. Utilizing the NSynth dataset from Tensorflow, we began by evaluating the original CNN model, then enhanced its structure and feature selection to improve performance. The updated CNN model was compared to both the unmodified CNN and the RF model. The unmodified CNN achieved a practical validation accuracy of 55% and a training accuracy of 66%, indicating an 11% loss. The RF model demonstrated an average accuracy of 65%, with accuracies ranging from 92% for strings to 45% for reed instruments. Despite an initial inclination to refine the RF model, our research showed that CNNs could achieve higher accuracy with minimal preprocessing adjustments. By switching the input from mel spectrograms to MFCCs, we observed significant improvements. Our enhanced CNN model outperformed both the unmodified CNN and the RF model, highlighting the potential of CNNs in IIA development. However, this approach also resulted in increased training times and processing demands.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experimental Validation of Optical Camera Communication
abstract: While simulation tools for visible light communication (VLC) with photo detectors (PDs) have been widely investigated, similar tools for optical camera communication (OCC) with complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) sensors are lacking in this regard. Camera based VLC systems have much lower data rates owing to camera exposure times. Among the few extant OCC simulation tools, none allow for simulation of images when exposure time is greater than the signal period. An accurate simulation of the OCC system can be used to improve the data rate and quality of performance. We propose a simple simulation technique for OCC which allows to test for system performance at frequencies beyond the camera shutter speed. This will allow much needed data rate improvement by operating at the actual frequency a decoding algorithm ceases detection instead of the exposure limit used now. We have tested the accuracy of simulation by comparing the detection success rates of simulated images with experimental images. The proposed simulation technique was shown to be accurate through experimental validation for two different cameras.

articleTitle: A 25Gbps Single-Ended to Differential Low-Noise Transimpedance Amplifier in 45nm SOI for High-Speed Optical Transceivers
abstract: High-speed optical transceivers are advancing towards lower noise and power consumption, necessitating enhanced transimpedance amplifier (TIA) designs. This paper presents a 25Gbps single-ended to differential (S2D) low-noise TIA implemented in 45nm SOI technology. The design utilizes AC-coupling capacitors and a cross-coupled capacitor pair to achieve differential output. To optimize noise and bandwidth performance, a high-gain, low-bandwidth input stage is followed by a continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE). The CTLE incorporates inductive peaking and negative capacitance techniques, achieving a bandwidth extension ratio (BWER) of 3.9 with less than 0.5dB peaking. Post-simulation results demonstrate the TIA achieves a transimpedance gain of 57.1 dB and a bandwidth of 23.7 GHz, considering a photodiode capacitance of 70fF. The input average noise current spectral density is 10.9 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$pA/\sqrt{Hz}$</tex>, with a power consumption of 38mW at a 1.3V supply voltage.

articleTitle: A 2μA Quiescent Current Output-Capacitorless LDO with Adaptive Power Transistors for Low Power Management in Energy Harvesting
abstract: This paper presents a low quiescent current outputcapacitorless low-dropout (LDO) regulator implemented in 65nm CMOS technology dedicated to the power management in Energy Harvesting Unit (EHU) applications. Most of the blocks in the proposed circuit operate in the subthreshold region in order to provide their specific outputs while consuming less current. To further reduce current consumption, a subthreshold voltage reference which can also be used to bias the error amplifier while providing a voltage reference of 500.2 mV with a TC of 55ppm/°C and a power consumption of 433.2 nW is utilized. The proposed LDO regulator uses a current-efficient adaptively biased regulation using two power transistors. The adaptive biasing circuit senses the load current and adjusts the bias point of the amplifier correspondingly. The results from the simulation demonstrate that the low dropout regulator can achieve a remarkably low quiescent current of 1.98859uA and a power consumption of 2.349134 uW under no load conditions. Additionally, the LDO regulator has a PSRR of −50.3228 dB, a good stability margin of 72.66°, and a maximum settling time of 3.437 us all under different load conditions. Moreover, the regulator can successfully maintain a regulated output voltage of 1V from a supply voltage of 1.2V, with a dropout voltage of 200 mV leading to an overall efficiency of 83.33%. Furthermore, the overall chip layout area is 0.0739 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: W-Band Backward Wave Oscillator Utilizing a Diverging Radial Sheet Electron Beam
abstract: This paper introduces a W-band Backward Wave Oscillator (BWO) with a radial rectangular concentric grating (RRCG) slow wave structure (SWS) and a diverging radial sheet electron beam (RSEB). This radial BWO design overcomes the limitations of traditional axial BWOs by offering a larger interaction area and reducing space-charge effects, thereby eliminating the need for an external guiding magnetic field and simplifying the electro-optic system. The high-frequency characteristics of the RRCG SWS are numerically analyzed, and Particle-in-Cell (PIC) simulations are conducted for the BWO using a diverging RSEB without an external magnetic field, operating at a beam voltage of 24 kV and a current density of 49.5 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The device achieves a peak power of 9.9 kW, an average power of 4.95 kW, and an efficiency of 5.15%. FFT analysis of the frequency spectrum reveals the generated signal frequency is 91.3 GHz. These findings demonstrate that the proposed radial BWO design operates effectively without an external magnetic field, making it suitable for high-efficiency millimeter wave generation in W-band applications.

articleTitle: Similarity Based Characterization and Identification of Breast Ultrasound Lesions in Space-Frequency Subband
abstract: Breast Ultrasound (BUS) has gained popularity over mammograms due to its higher sensitivity, accuracy, faster imaging and lower cost. Computerized diagnosis of breast abnormalities using BUS images is crucial for better treatment planning, monitoring and clinical trials. Present work decomposes the original BUS images by using Stationary Wavelet Transform (SWT) to estimate the textural similarity of breast lesions. The proposed detection approach employs a contrast enhancing technique using sigmoid and gradient magnitude filter to reduce artifacts, nipple shadowing and missing structures of BUS images. Spatial Fuzzy c-Means (FCM) clustering algorithm is used to segment the contour of lesions. Following this, textural compositions of lesions have been assessed in the space-frequency plane to study the degree of homogeneity/heterogeneity of lesions, present in different space-frequency subbands. Some similarity measuring quantifiers are used to estimate textural homogeneity of lesions. Finally, support vector machine (SVM) and Hybrid Adaboost classifiers have been designed to categorize the benignancy/malignancy stages of test data. Experimental results are reported on three standard benchmark datasets and compared with other state-of-art detection techniques.

articleTitle: Unitary Operator Based Quantum Secure Access Structure for Medical Image Sharing
abstract: Ensuring the secure storage and sharing of medical records in the cloud is increasingly crucial due to vulnerabilities in classical encryption methods, such as key manipulation and cloud collusion. This paper introduces a novel quantum-based approach using Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) and Unitary operators. We designed three quantum circuits for different image sizes: one for the Unitary operator, one for encryption, and one for decryption. DICOM images are first transformed into quantum images with the NEQR algorithm, then encrypted using a Unitary operator, which serves as the encryption key. This key is securely transmitted via quantum teleportation, enhancing protection against classical and quantum attacks. Extensive simulations show the method's effectiveness and robustness in safeguarding medical data during cloud storage and transmission. This makes it a promising solution for secure medical image sharing in quantum communication networks.

articleTitle: High Performance Flow Table for 5G Core Networks Based on FPGA
abstract: Flow Tables play a crucial role in the architecture of smart network interface cards (smart NICs). Essentially, they are data structures that map incoming packets to specific actions or destinations based on predefined rules. In the 5G core network, with the explosive increase in User Equipment (UE) connections and the significant number of TCP connections per UE, the importance of Flow Tables has risen significantly to accommodate hundreds of millions of flows. To achieve both high capacity and processing speed for Flow Tables, this paper presents a design approach where flow entries are stored in Double Data Rate 4 Synchronous Dynamic Random Access Memory (DDR4 SDRAM), supplemented with a cache stored in Double Data Rate 4 Synchronous Dynamic Random-Access Memory (SRAM) for frequently used flows, utilizing the CLOCK algorithm for cache placement management. Additionally, we implement the cuckoo hashing algorithm to improve collision resolution within the Flow Table. Furthermore, by applying pipelining and parallel processing, we enhance the throughput of the lookup process. Validation and performance evaluation were conducted on the Xilinx Alveo U200 card, yielding outstanding results: at an FPGA clock frequency of 300 MHz, our implementation achieved a superior throughput of up to 50 million flows per second.

articleTitle: Machine Learning in Laboratory Diagnosis
abstract: This work explores the critical role of autoverification in laboratory medicine, where timely and accurate test results are imperative for effective patient care. Auto-verification systems can significantly reduce the time to report and enhance the reliability of test outcomes, which is particularly crucial in time-sensitive diagnostic environments. This study delves into meticulous preprocessing of clinical data to prepare them for analysis, addressing challenges such as data inconsistency and missing values. By integrating advanced machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models, we develop robust algorithms aimed at automating the verification of laboratory test results. Furthermore, we demonstrate the feasibility of these algorithms by replicating the processes in KNIME, a data analytics platform. This not only substantiates the scalability of our approach but also underscores its potential for real-world application in improving diagnostic workflows and patient outcomes.

articleTitle: A Pencil Beam Electron-Optical System for Teahertz Vacuum Electronic Devices
abstract: The simulation of a terahertz pencil beam electron-optical system (EOS), comprising an electron gun and a uniform magnetic focusing system with operating voltage of 18–20 kV and current of 14-16.5 mA, is reported. The beam current density exceeds 360 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> due to the miniature radius of beam as 35 μm and tunnel as 50 μm, while the cathode surface current density below 3 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Therefore, the magnetic system provides a peak magnetic field strength of approximately 0.6 T to ensure stable transmission over distances exceeding 30mm with transmission efficiency of 100%.

articleTitle: 1 μA Quiescent All-MOS Subthreshold Design Technique of Voltage Reference for Biomedical and IoT Device Applications
abstract: Novel low-voltage, low-power voltage reference circuit is introduced, capable of functioning down to 350m V with a power consumption of 6.2n W (with a quiescent current of 4.3nA) at room temperature. Implemented in a 65nm process node, the circuit utilizes a topology in the weak inversion region of transistors. Although weak inversion operation is sensitive to temperature and process variability, the circuit employs compensation techniques ensuring independence from process, voltage, and temperature variations. Simulation results using Monte Carlo Analysis shows that VT<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</inf> dependence can be reduced to less than ± 1 % (3σ) and with minimum PSRR of 50.52 dB and 56.19 dB at 100Hz and 10MHz respectively. Furthermore since it is a resistor-less voltage reference, it only consumes a very small die area which is advantageous in biomedical and portable applications.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a oneM2M-Based Remote Monitoring System for Water Supply in Water Distribution Networks
abstract: In the Philippines, water distribution systems face challenges like intermittent supply, slow flow, and low pressure. Water utilities struggle with non-revenue water (NRW) mainly due to leaks in distribution systems. Regulators focus on evaluating utilities' performance based on service standards. There is a shared need among customers, utilities, and regulators for a remote monitoring system to measure water parameters. To address this, a system was developed to monitor water storage levels, pressure, and flow rate using ultrasonic, water pressure, and water flow sensors. The system employs machine-to-machine communication based on oneM2M standards, allowing for scalability and integration of additional sensors. It was implemented on a small-scale model with interconnected PPR pipes and five wireless sensor nodes.

articleTitle: Detection of Neurological Disorders Using Advanced AI Techniques
abstract: Neurological diseases have a huge impact on global health and are known to be major causes of death and disability around the world. There are more than 600 neurological diseases, but there isn't yet a single automatic standard detection method that can find more than one of them using a single framework. A major challenge with neurological disorders is changes in cognitive functions and behaviors. Diseases like Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and schizophrenia need early detection to enable possible intervention. In this work, we emphasize non-invasive techniques for disease detection through Electroencephalography (EEG) signals using Machine Learning techniques. We, also Homogenize the three datasets under consideration and attempt multiclass classification for the three neurological disorders. We have compared the performance of proposed models with existing models for the accurate identification of neurological disorders, focusing on their efficacy and reliability. This means that EEGbased diagnostics could become one of the most prospective ways for early and accurate disease detection by applying advanced AI classification algorithms. This work contributes to ongoing efforts in neurology to improve health outcomes through artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Community-Collaborative Solar Dryer Prototype: Development, Deployment, and Testing for Sustainable Food Preservation
abstract: In the Philippines, the prevalent method for drying agricultural and aquatic products like rice, corn, and fish relies on the traditional sun-drying technique where the produce is laid out under the sun, in an open area, and exposed to environmental factors like dust, dirt, and insects. This practice persists primarily because no other alternatives can guarantee a cost-effective yield when drying agricultural products. To address this, a multilevel solar dryer with solar-powered monitoring for households was developed as a sustainable option. Inputs from farming and fisherfolk communities were gathered through interviews and consultations, which served as the basis in designing the solar dryer. A prototype was built and then deployed in a fisherfolk household in Bani, Zambales. In this paper, three species of fish, locally known as bisugo, mataan, and danggit, were dried using the solar dryer. In parallel, traditional sun drying was conducted to compare the drying time of the two methods. Data showed that the multilevel solar dryer was effective in trapping the heat inside its drying chamber. Moreover, the water activity of the dried products was obtained to determine their susceptibility to spoilage. The measured values were below the maximum threshold set by the Philippine national standard for dried fish, which indicates that the dried products can be sold commercially. Lastly, the minimum viable product of the solar dryer developed in this study costs Php 20,000.00 (USD 350.00), making this an affordable alternative.

articleTitle: Research on the Electromagnetic Interference of the Balise System of High-Speed Train
abstract: In the actual railway environment, the working environment of the balise system is faced with all kinds of electromagnetic harassment, and the electromagnetic environment is very complicated. The electromagnetic interference simulation analysis model of the balise system is built, and the coupling mechanism of electromagnetic interference is studied. In this paper, the downlink and uplink antenna simulation models of the balise system are constructed. Then the simulation is verified by feeding the antenna port, the expected simulation effect is achieved. At last, the influence of the crosstalk current at the antenna port of the vehicle balise is analyzed and summarized for different cases by varying the angle of polarization, incidence, pitch and azimuth of the interfering signals at each angle.

articleTitle: 91.2% Efficiency Low Power Non-Inverting Buck-Boost Converter
abstract: Two architectures of high efficiency low power DC-DC noninverting buck-boost (NIB B) converter is presented in this paper. The first architecture is NIBB with voltage divider in the feedback circuit and the second architecture is using Type-III Compensator using Op Amp-RC architecture. Second architecture improves stability and achieves low settling time. Both the circuits are implemented on Cadence Virtuoso using a 45nm CMOS process. With a maximum output load current of 200 mA, both produce a consistent 0.8 V when the input voltage varies between 0.6 and 1 V at 1MHz switching frequency. The first architecture network achieves a peak efficiency of 91.2% when the load resister is 12 Ω and the output voltage ripples were maintained under 91 mV. Also, the settling time for the second architecture is improved from 12.5μs to 8.2μs transition from boost to buck mode and from 7.5μs to 6.9μs from buck to boost mode. Additionally, both the architectures can achieve effective load and line regulation.

articleTitle: Development of Game based Virtual environment for post stroke rehabilitation patients
abstract: Stroke, which is a leading cause of long-term dis- ability in adults, occurs due to the blockage of blood vessels in the brain and has the signs like drooping of the face, weakness in one arm, slurred speech and vision problems, and lack of coordination. With over 12.2 million strokes each year, new rehabilitation methods are vital. Recent studies showed the applicability of virtual reality (VR) in post-stroke situations where patients are exposed to balanced training environments. Nevertheless, the current literature provides no clear information on what influences VR effectiveness and such design characteristics. The objective of this paper is to provide a critical analysis of VR-supported tools for balance training after stroke, discussing technological parameters, sensors, motor activities, virtual environments, and control approaches. Thus, in the present review, we outline specific recommendations that could help to overcome existing deficits and improve post-stroke rehabilitation results.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Accuracy of Mapping Paddy Rice Using Polarimetric Decomposition Parameters and Backscatter Intensity
abstract: Polarimetric decomposition parameters are crucial for characterizing ground objects by their unique scattering mechanisms, particularly in crop monitoring and specifically for mapping paddy rice fields. This study evaluates their impact on mapping accuracy by deriving entropy (H), anisotropy (A), and mean alpha angle (a) from a multi-temporal Sentinel-1 dataset. These parameters served as input features for training a random forest classifier to delineate rice-growing areas. Additionally, another random forest classifier was trained using backscatter intensity from the VH (Vertical Transmit, Horizontal Receive) polarization channel to provide a comparative map, enhancing the evaluation of the study outcomes. Adjustments to the temporal resolution of the input dataset were necessary due to the computational constraints of Google Earth Engine (GEE), the cloud-based platform used in this study. Despite the reduced temporal resolution, the classifier trained with polarimetric decomposition parameters performed comparably to the classifier using the full temporal resolution of backscatter intensity. The classifier utilizing backscatter intensity reported slightly higher overall accuracy and kappa coefficient, with values of 0.8460 and 0.6920, respectively. The classifier using polarimetric decomposition parameters achieved an overall accuracy of 0.8250 and a kappa coefficient of 0.6499. The performance of the two classifiers varied with respect to the calculated producer's and user's accuracies, though the differences were not significant. These results suggest that entropy (H), anisotropy (A), and mean alpha angle (a) effectively capture the distinct scattering properties of rice throughout its growth stages, as well as those of other crops and land cover types, enabling reliable rice classification. Future research could explore additional parameters and their combinations to further enhance mapping accuracy.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Parkinson's Disease Using Continuous Wavelet Transform-Based Time-Frequency Domain Analysis of Speech Signals
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) ranks as the second most prevalent neurological ailment globally, following Alzheimer's disease. The early diagnosis of PD is a significant challenge due to its gradual evolution and the progressive development of its symptoms. Recent research has indicated that alterations in speech can serve as a valuable diagnostic for the timely detection of PD. This paper presents a novel approach for diagnosing PD using speech sounds, utilizing a continuous wavelet transform (CWT). The utilization of CWT was employed to obtain the time-frequency representation (TFR) for each voice recording. From the TFR, entropy and energy are calculated for every frequency component and used as features for the classification of PD-affected speech and healthy individuals' speech. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is verified using the vowels of the GITA database. The support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) are used as a classifier for the classification. Using the vowel /o/, the highest classification accuracy of 88.70% is attained. The results demonstrate that the proposed CWT-based features can accurately diagnose PD using a person's speech.

articleTitle: An Evaluation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Closing Stock Prices in the Indian Stock Market
abstract: This study examines how effective machine learning algorithms are at forecasting the closing stock prices of five major FMCG companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE). The focus is on methods such as Random Forest, Decision Trees, Linear Regression, and Support Vector Regression, aiming to analyze their performance against metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The goal is to uncover insights regarding the reliability of different machine learning techniques for stock price prediction, ultimately assisting investors and financial analysts in making well-informed investment choices. The study will leverage historical stock price data, incorporating relevant technical indicators and fundamental features to train and test the predictive models. To ensure data quality, a meticulous preprocessing stage will address missing values, normalize features, and minimize potential biases. The models' performance will be evaluated using robust metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and R-squared to assess accuracy and overall effectiveness.

articleTitle: CARE-PCR: A Portable OpenPCR Thermocyler
abstract: Environmental monitoring applications often employ an RT-PCR assay step in their methodologies, and often collect samples in the field, far away from a laboratory. In this setting, such fieldwork would benefit greatly from a device that can carry out the reaction. This project involved the construction of a custom RT-PCR thermocycler based on OpenPCR's open source design with the objective of portability, achieved through battery operation. Design changes were made to both scale back the power consumption of the device to 50W, while managing the tradeoffs that come with this miniaturization in order to achieve battery powered operation. A heating element was introduced to improve temperature ramp rate performance, alongside a custom power module to facilitate battery operations. Portability is supplemented by LCD-keypad standalone user interfacing, alongside logging and real time clock features for user accessibility.

articleTitle: Mitigating Drift in Extraction of Joint Angle Measurements from Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) Data
abstract: Inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensors are widely used in sports science to acquire motion-related data, such as joint angle measurements, and provide valuable insights into the performance of the athletes. These sensors can be used for specific purposes that needs regular calibration to compensate for drift since assessment of muscle stress rely on these devices. However, sensor-based systems may not always provide accurate joint angle measurements. This paper aims to mitigate the drift of the IMU data by pre-processing it with various sensor fusion algorithms: Complementary filter, Kalman filter, and Madgwick filter. The output of the calibrated IMU sensor device was compared with the data collected from the VICON motion capture system to validate its accuracy. Finally, the calibrated IMU sensor output is used to measure the joint angles. As a result, the complementary filter resulted in a better accuracy and reliability performance than the Kalman and Magdwick filter. The Kalman filter obtained a higher reliability and precision due to its lower variability and standard deviation of 37.68. Moreover, it also indicated that the complementary filter often yielded low error values, suggesting better performance as seen in its Root- Mean-Square Error (RMSE) of 9.75. An Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) test was done, indicating that the RMSE accepts the null hypothesis, H0, that there are no significant differences among the means of the metrics.

articleTitle: Improved Text Summarization with RL-Enabled PEGASUS and Siamese Network Evaluation
abstract: Text summarization is a fundamental down-stream task in NLP, a field of AI that focuses on the interactions between computers and humans through natural language. With the exponential growth of digital information and advancements in various fields of science, the need for summarizing scientific papers has increased drastically. Classical statistical methods, deep learning models, and transformer-based architectures are employed to extract concise summaries from large scientific datasets. In this paper, a comparative analysis of these techniques is conducted using standard benchmark datasets and evaluation metrics, such as ROUGE scores, to assess their performance in terms of summary quality, coherence, and informativeness. An RL-enabled PEGASUS model is proposed for slightly enhanced performance in scientific text summarization. Addressing the current lack of a proper evaluation metric for summarization tasks, a new Siamese Networks-based architecture is proposed to serve as a better evaluation metric for generative language models, including text-summarization models.

articleTitle: Detection of Oral Diseases on Fluorescence Images Obtained Under Blue Light Irradiation
abstract: In recent years, devices for evaluating oral mucosa using light-illumination of various wavelengths have attracted attention for the detection of oral diseases. When blue light is irradiated on oral diseases, the blue-band wavelengths are absorbed and lesional tissues appear darker. However, it is difficult to accurately detect the diseased area because its appearance depends on the direction and amount of irradiation on the target area. In this study, we attempted to detect oral diseases in fluorescence images obtained under blue light irradiation using Mask R-CNN, an instance segmentation method. The success or failure of disease detection was determined by whether or not the intersection over union (IoU) with the lesioned region was greater than a set threshold value. We found that 87.0% of lesions were detected under IoU ≥ 0.5, and 97.5%under IoU > 0.0. These results indicate that the false negative rate would be very small, since a portion of the diseased area was detected in almost all cases.

articleTitle: Control System Design for Simultaneous Stabilization of Multiple Internet-Connected Inverted Pendulums Considering Communication Delay
abstract: This study examined the method to simultaneously conduct identical experimental classes across different locations, particularly considering the potential for remote classes during pandemics such as COVID-19. The goal was to achieve a system configuration that allows for distributed classes while maintaining a sense of unity, similar to in-person sessions. Hierarchical optimal control methods were applied for this purpose. Further-more, this study addresses the communication delays that occur during remote control between distant locations by applying the concept of state-prediction control in time-delay systems. This approach demonstrated the ability to calculate the current state of a counterpart from the past states, thereby mitigating the impact of delays. The effectiveness of this approach was demonstrated experimentally using an inverted penduluman iconic system used in control engineering education.

articleTitle: Uf-PromptGAN: A Nighttime Flare Removal Network Using Learnable Prompts
abstract: Flares are unwanted perturbances in a digital image surrounding a light source that hide details of the artifacts behind them. Many efficient data driven approaches using CNN and transformer based architectures have been recently proposed for the removal of reflective as well as scattering flares, but most of these networks work well only for daytime flares. For Night time flare removal, state of the art models use transformer based U-Net Architecture (Uformer), but they have not achieved truly accurate results. These models either fail to effectively remove flares or struggle to accurately reconstruct the artifacts hidden by them. In this paper, we introduce PromptGAN, a two stage model which first uses the Uformer to remove the flares followed by a learnable prompt-based AOT-GAN to inpaint the regions adversely affected by Uformer. We use learnable prompting to learn and encode background information images which helps the GAN to make more informed decisions while inpainting. Thus, the proposed approach ensures an effective removal of surrounding flares, resulting in a more realistic image reconstruction and accurate recreation of artifacts which were previously hidden by the flares.

articleTitle: A ResNet-Based DVFS Regulator for Heterogeneous Multi-Core Mobile Processors
abstract: Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) is commonly used for the balance of performance and power of mobile processors. Conventional DVFS regulators take the processor cores with the same power and performance weight showing their inability in the regulation of heterogeneous processors. This paper proposes a core-aware frequency-power evaluation scheme that utilizes a multilayer perceptron (MLP) to assess the efficacy of DVFS regulation actions. Additionally, a ResNet-based DVFS regulator, trained with the assistance of the MLP, is developed for heterogeneous multi-core processors. Evaluated on Xiaomi 13 Pro powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, the proposed DVFS approach achieves an up to ×1.47 improvement in FPS Performance Per Watt (FPPW) compared with the Qualcomm's default DVFS governor in video recording scenario.

articleTitle: Stixu: An Open-Source Idea for Planning Integrated Circuit Layouts Efficiently
abstract: Stick diagrams are a traditional tool used to quickly design the topology of an integrated circuit on paper before beginning the time-consuming CAD layout process. Stixu is a browser-based, open-source EDA tool for stick diagrams. It provides built-in output analysis capability and offers both VLSI learners and professionals with an open-source means to quickly and easily validate CMOS topologies.

articleTitle: A Non-Overlapping Synthetic Clock Generator for DC-DC Boost Converter in 65 nm CMOS Technology
abstract: Boost converters have been widely adopted in battery-powered technologies due to their compact size, afford-ability, and ability to generate a higher output voltage than the input voltage. Regulating the output voltage is crucial for these converters in portable devices, as these devices operate across a wide range of current loads, potentially affecting output voltage stability. Feedback loops in boost converters can effectively address this regulation issue. A key component in these feedback loops is the clock generator, which manages the switching activities of the boost converter. It controls the inductor's charging and discharging phases to produce the boosted output voltage. This paper introduces a non-overlapping synthetic clock generator for boost converters, designed to maintain an almost constant switching frequency for stable output voltage regulation across a wide load current range. This system is implemented using the TSMC 65nm CMOS technology process.

articleTitle: A TENG Finger Sensor Enabled Human-Machine Interface for VR Applications
